<meta>This page serves as the formal introduction to a treatise on astrology and astronomy. It establishes the divine origin of the Vedas and the specific importance of Jyotish (astrology/astronomy) as the 'eyes' of the Vedic corpus.</meta>

# Introduction

> I bow to the Goddess who stands upon the heart of a corpse, her face adorned with a gentle smile, holding in her lotus-like hands a severed head, a sword, and the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness. She has conquered the hosts of enemies and appears fearsome, yet she shines with large, high breasts decorated by a garland of severed heads. Having offered salutations, the skillful Nanda, son of Achyuta and others, expands upon this Introduction to Natal Astrology. <note>original: "तिष्ठन्तीं शवहृत्सु..." This opening verse is a traditional 'Mangalacharan' or auspicious invocation, here dedicated to a form of the Goddess (likely Kali) to ensure the successful completion of the work.</note>

It has been entirely proven by both ancient and modern histories that among all available books, the Vedas are the most ancient. These are called *apaurusheya* <term>apaurusheya: not of human origin</term>, meaning that no human being authored them. Rather, for the welfare of humanity, the Almighty God revealed them through the sages—who possessed knowledge of the three periods of time <note>past, present, and future</note>—at the very beginning of creation.

The Veda has six limbs <term>Vedangas: auxiliary sciences required to understand the Vedas</term>, such as: Grammar is the mouth, the science of Astronomy/Astrology is the eyes, Etymology is the ears, Ritual Code is the hands, Phonetics is the nose, and Prosody is the feet.

-> It has also been said: <-

> The science of words is the mouth, Astronomy/Astrology the eyes, Etymology is called the ears, and Ritual Code the hands. That which is the Phonetics of this Veda is the nose, and the two lotus feet are Prosody; so it has been stated by the ancient wise ones.

Because it is the "Eye of the Veda," the science of *Jyotish* <term>Jyotish: the combined study of astronomy and astrology</term> is considered the most excellent among all the limbs. This is because a person, even if endowed with all other limbs, can do nothing if they are deprived of eyes. Therefore, the illustrious Bhaskaracharya <note>A famous 12th-century Indian mathematician and astronomer</note> has stated in the *Siddhanta Shiromani*:

> This Astronomy/Astrology is indeed remembered as the Eye of the Veda, and therefore it is called the principal among its limbs. Even if joined with other parts like the ears and nose, a person lacking the limb of the eye is incapable of doing anything.

This science has two primary divisions: *Siddhanta* (Theory) and *Phalita* (Predictive).
*Siddhanta* is that which contains the description of Geography, Astronomy <note>literally: "the sphere of the earth" and "the sphere of the heavens"</note>, and related subjects.

<summary>This introductory page establishes the divine authority of the Vedas and argues that Jyotish (astronomy/astrology) is the most vital of the six Vedic sciences because it functions as the "eyes" of the scripture. It introduces the two main branches of the study: theoretical Siddhanta and predictive Phalita.</summary>
<keywords>Vedas, Jyotish, Bhaskaracharya, Siddhanta Shiromani, Vedangas, Astronomy, Astrology, Apaurusheya</keywords>

# Introduction

Predictive astrology <note>original: "Phalita"</note> describes all life events, natural conditions, and circumstances of every human being from the moment of birth until death. It has five main branches: Natal Astrology <note>Jataka</note>, Omens and Mundane Astrology <note>Samhita</note>, Horary Astrology <note>Prashna</note>, Annual Horoscopy <note>Tajika</note>, and Electional Astrology <note>Muhurtta</note>.

Among these, the Natal <note>Jataka</note> section is used for all matters related to the birth chart <note>Janmapatri</note>. However, because this work cannot be accomplished by a single book alone, astrologers usually require many different volumes. Yet, this single book titled **Jatakabharanam**, composed by the preeminent astrologer Shri Dhundhiraj Daivajña—a resident of Parthnagar near the Godavari River—is sufficient for this purpose. Almost all modern practitioners of predictive astrology accept this fact.

In this book, for the purpose of creating a birth chart, the results of all subjects such as the Year <note>Samvatsara</note>, Solstice <note>Ayana</note>, Season <note>Ritu</note>, Month, Fortnight, Planetary Conjunctions, Celestial Yogas <note>Nabhasa Yoga</note>, and the effects of Planetary Aspects have been described in an easy-to-understand manner. In fact, nothing has been left out in terms of explaining all matters related to the birth chart. In the current era, most astrologers create birth charts based solely on this single primary text.

Despite being such a captivating treatise on predictive astrology, until now, no edition has been published that contains a purified original text, the true meaning, and practical examples, which would benefit everyone from the novice student to the learned scholar.

Therefore, to remove those aforementioned many shortcomings, I have written this simple Hindi commentary <note>Tika</note> named **"Vimala"** <note>meaning "The Pure" or "The Lucid"</note>. In this incomparable edition, the purified original text, the meaning in truly simple Hindi language, and examples have all been clearly provided. Along with this, an appendix section has also been given at the end of the book. This is because certain essential matters were not present within this original text, which sometimes forced practitioners to seek help from other books when creating more detailed charts...

<summary>This introduction defines the branches of astrology and promotes 'Jatakabharanam' as a comprehensive manual for natal horoscopy, introducing the 'Vimala' commentary intended to make the text accessible to all levels of scholars.</summary>
<keywords>Predictive Astrology, Jatakabharanam, Dhundhiraj Daivajña, Birth Chart, Vimala Commentary, Natal Astrology, Five Branches of Astrology</keywords>

# Introduction

...had to be undertaken. Therefore, to remove this difficulty, this section has been provided.

In this, the knowledge regarding the planets' mutual natural <term>Naisargika</term> and temporary <term>Tatkalika</term> relationships, the refined "great-friendship" <term>Adhi-mitra</term> and similar states, the lords of the zodiac signs, and the various divisional charts—namely the <term>Hora</term> <note>one-half division</note>, <term>Drekkana</term> <note>one-third division</note>, <term>Saptamansha</term> <note>one-seventh division</note>, <term>Navamansha</term> <note>one-ninth division</note>, <term>Trishansha</term> <note>one-thirtieth division</note>, and <term>Dwadashansha</term> <note>one-twelfth division</note>—have been clearly presented. Furthermore, it includes considerations of the houses and friends of Rahu and Ketu <note>the lunar nodes</note>, the mathematics of major <term>Dasha</term> and sub-periods <term>Antardasha</term>, the method for calculating the precise lifespan, and the results of the house lords <term>Bhavesha-phala</term>.

Now, I must say with confidence that by using this single book alone, no difficulty will be encountered in performing all tasks related to the birth chart <term>Janmapatri</term>. Excessive praise is useless; practitioners of predictive astrology <term>Phalit-gya</term> will experience this themselves by looking at it with an unbiased mind.

Having written the commentary for such an incomparable book, I have given the rights for publication to the famous **Manager of the Chowkhamba Sanskrit Series Library of Kashi, Babu Shri Jayakrishna Das Ji Gupta Mahodaya**.

It is hoped that learned scholars, upon seeing this, will make my immense labor successful.

In the end, my humble prayer is that if any error has remained due to oversight or printing faults, the learned should correct it and inform me. I will present it again before those gentlemen, rectified in the next edition.

->It has also been said—<-

> Even while walking, a slip occurs somewhere due to carelessness.
> The wicked laugh at it, but the virtuous set it right.
<note>original: "Gacchatah skhalanam kvapi bhavatyeva pramadatah | Hasanti durjanastatra samadadhati sajjanah ||"</note>

Rama Navami <note>The festival celebrating the birth of Lord Rama</note>
Vikram Samvat 2008 <note>Approx. 1951 CE</note>

Humbly—
**Pandit Shri Achyutananda Jha**,
Jarisau

->Salutations to the Illustrious Lord Ganesha.<-

# The Ornament of Nativity
## Adorned with the "Vimala" commentary including illustrative examples.

---

### Here begins the auspicious invocation by the commentator:

> I bow to the Goddess who shines with the brilliance of the sun at the end of an eon <note>The "end of an eon" refers to Pralaya, the cosmic dissolution</note>, who strikes fear into opponents, and whose eyes are the moon, sun, and fire. With a tongue flickering in anger and a wide-open mouth, her chest is smeared with blood. With red eyes and a terrifying form, she fills the entire three worlds with her radiance. Having offered salutations to her, the one named Achyutananda composes this beautiful commentary titled *Vimala* <note>Vimala means "The Stainless" or "The Pure"</note>. || 1 ||

> I bow to the son of Shambhu <note>Lord Ganesha, son of Shiva</note>, who is like a mass of concentrated bliss, possessing the face of an elephant. From his temples flows an endless stream of ichor <note>Mada: the fluid secreted by elephants in rut, symbolizing power and abundance</note>. He is the thunderbolt that shatters the mountain-like array of obstacles, the remover of all hindrances. || 2 ||

### The auspicious invocation by the author of the text:

> I always worship in the lotus of my heart the lotus feet of the Giver of Prosperity, the granter of boons. By remembering him, even a <unclear>mute</unclear> <note>original: "muka"</note> person immediately attains a status comparable to the preceptor of the gods <note>Brihaspati, the planet Jupiter and teacher of the deities</note>. || 1 ||

By whose remembrance even a dull-witted person very quickly becomes worshipful like Brihaspati among the gods—meditating with my heart upon the lotus feet of Lord Ganesha, the giver of all desired fruits, I offer my salutations. || 1 ||

> Using his generous intellect as the Mandara mountain <note>A reference to the Puranic myth of the Churning of the Ocean</note>, the illustrious Dhundhiraja churns the great ocean of the *Hora* scriptures <note>term: Hora (Astrology/Genethliacs)</note> to produce this work, truly a collection of stainless gems of speech for the worship of the noble. || 2 ||

The astrologer named Shri Dhundhiraja, having churned the ocean of the ancient Sage-authored astrological sciences with his vast intellect acting as the churning mountain, brings forth the jewels of flawless poetic expression. || 2 ||

> Having meditated with true devotion in my mind upon the lotus feet of my teacher, Jnanaraja, this work of natal astrology named *The Ornament of Nativity* is composed to bring delight to those learned in the science of births. || 3 ||

<page-num>2</page-num>
<header>In the Jatakabharana—</header>

Devoutly meditating in my heart upon the lotus feet of my teacher, named Jnanaraja <note>Literally "King of Knowledge," a renowned 16th-century astronomer and the author's father</note>, I compose this work on natal astrology titled "Jatakabharana" <note>The Ornament of Nativity</note> to bring joy to astrologers. || 3 ||

->The minds of astrologers become greatly agitated and confused by consulting various scattered texts while preparing a birth chart according to the scriptures. Therefore, in this work on horoscopy, I shall make all the statements regarding nativities perfectly clear.<- || 4 ||

Astrologers create birth charts as prescribed by the scriptures using many different books; however, looking through so many diverse texts causes their minds to become distressed and overwhelmed. For this reason, we are clarifying the entirety of astrological teachings within this single volume. || 4 ||

->This work is sufficient in its clarity to empower those who desire to create wonderful birth charts to write them in the proper sequence without excessive labor. Therefore, its name is truly meaningful and appropriate.<- || 5 ||

This book is perfectly adequate and clear for providing the ability to write birth charts systematically and without hardship for those who take pride in making intricate horoscopes. Thus, the name "Jatakabharana" <note>meaning "The Ornament of Birth"</note> is proven to be descriptive of its actual purpose. || 5 ||

->The verses containing auspicious blessings and benedictions are being spoken hereafter. Those skilled in the preparation of birth charts should write these merit-bestowing verses first.<- || 6 ||

The auspicious and celebratory verses written below should be recorded first by clever astrologers when they begin the process of drafting a birth chart. || 6 ||

->**Auspicious verses to be written at the beginning of a birth chart—**<-

->May the elephant-faced Lord <note>Ganesha</note>, who is filled with an abundance of joy—expressed through the swaying of his trunk, the tossing of his head, the opening and closing of his eyes, the rhythmic flapping of his beautiful ears, the humming of bees attracted to his temple-fluid, his playful movements, and his trumpeting with face upturned—ordain our well-being.<- || 7 ||

By the moving of his trunk, the shaking of his head, the blinking of his eyes, the flapping of his ears, the listening to the sound of bees settled in his ichor <note>The fluid secreted by elephants in rut, considered auspicious in Sanskrit poetry</note>, and the various playful acts performed while raising his face to roar—may Shri Ganesha, thus filled with bliss, grant us prosperity. || 7 ||

<summary>The author, Dhundhiraja, explains that this text was written to simplify the complex process of chart-making for astrologers and provides the initial benedictory verse dedicated to Ganesha to be used in horoscopes.</summary>

May the lunar day, weekday, constellation, yoga, karana, and the specific moments at the time of birth bring welfare to the person whose birth chart <note>original: "Janma-patri"</note> is being created according to the Shastras <note>Sacred scriptures or scientific treatises</note>. || 11 ||

> May those planets which act as significators <note>original: "karakas"; planets that produce specific results based on their office</note> grant their full results to the one whose birth chart is being prepared. || 12 ||

May the Royal Yogas <note>combinations for power and wealth</note>, the Nabhasa Yogas <note>celestial configurations based on the shape planets form in the sky</note>, and the significator planets grant all their complete fruits to the subject of this chart. || 12 ||

With great curiosity, I am writing this birth chart; may the Goddess Lakshmi remain forever stable in the house of that person. || 13 ||

> I have not employed a water-clock <note>original: "udaka-yantra"; an ancient device for measuring time by the flow of water</note> to observe the time, nor have I used a gnomon <note>original: "shanku"; a vertical pillar used to tell time by its shadow</note>. Based on the time provided by others, I am diligently describing the auspicious and inauspicious fruits of this birth. || 14 ||

To determine the time of birth, I neither held a mechanical instrument nor measured the shadow of a gnomon; rather, I am writing this birth chart based on the time reported to me by others. || 14 ||

> May all the planets, beginning with the Sun, along with the lunar mansions <note>original: "nakshatras"</note> and the signs of the zodiac, grant a long life to the one whose birth chart this is. || 15 ||

May all the planets like the Sun, together with all the constellations and signs, provide longevity to the owner of this birth chart. || 15 ||

### Method for determining the name of the Year from the Shaka Era—

> "Multiply the Shaka year <note>an era starting in 78 CE</note> by twelve; add 4291. Divide the result by 1875. Add the resulting quotient back to the Shaka year. Divide that sum by sixty. The remainder indicates the number of years passed in the cycle starting from Prabhava; the next year is the current year according to the Jovian cycle <note>original: "Barhaspatya-mana"; a 60-year cycle based on Jupiter's movement</note>." || 1–2 ||

Multiply the Shaka year by 12 and add 4291. Divide that sum by 1875. Add the quotient obtained to the original Shaka year and divide the total by 60. The remainder represents the years passed in the sequence starting with the year 'Prabhava,' and the following one is the current year. || 1–2 ||

Example—As in the Shaka year 1868, one wishes to know the name of the year.

<summary>The author invokes blessings for the subject of the birth chart and humbly notes that the accuracy of the reading depends on the birth time provided by others. He then provides the mathematical formula for calculating the specific name of the year within the 60-year Jovian cycle using the Shaka Era date.</summary>

# Results of the Yearly Cycle

When the Shaka year 1868 <note>The Shaka era is a historical Hindu calendar epoch beginning in 78 CE; 1868 Shaka corresponds to 1946-47 CE</note> is multiplied by 22, the result is 41,196. By adding 4,261 to this, we get 45,427. Dividing this by 1,875 gives a quotient of 24 and a remainder of 387. The remainder is not required; taking only the quotient and adding it to the Shaka year 1868, we get 1,892. Dividing this by 60 <note>The Jovian cycle consists of 60 unique year names that repeat</note>, the remainder is 32. Therefore, following the sequence starting from *Prabhava*, the 32nd year named *Vilambi* is the past year, and the next one, named *Vikari*, is the current year.

### Results of Birth in the Vibhava Year

# Results of Birth in the Ishvara Year—

A person born in the **Ishvara** year is very quick to anger, filled with happiness, virtuous, majestic, clever, a knower of arts, and of a good disposition. || 11 ||

# Results of Birth in the Bahudhanya Year—

<note>original Sanskrit: "Vyaparadakshah kshitipalamani..."</note>
A human born in the **Bahudhanya** <note>The 12th year; the name means "Abundant Grain"</note> year is clever in trade, honored by kings, charitable, proud, a knower of the scriptures, and possesses much wealth and grain through various means. || 12 ||

A person born in the **Bahudhanya** year is clever in conducting business, respected by the state, charitable, dignified, a knower of the scriptures, and through many methods becomes possessed of much grain. || 12 ||

# Results of Birth in the Pramathi Year—

<note>original Sanskrit: "Rathadhvajachhatraturangamadyair..."</note>
A person born in the **Pramathi** <note>The 13th year; the name means "Tormentor" or "Chaotic"</note> year is endowed with chariots, flags, ceremonial umbrellas, and horses; he is devoted to the scriptures, a destroyer of enemies, a minister to a king, and a knower of the *Shruti* <term>Shruti: the Vedas, or sacred revealed knowledge</term>. || 13 ||

A person born in the **Pramathi** year is endowed with chariots, flags, umbrellas, horses, etc.; he is engaged in the scriptures, a slayer of enemies, a royal minister, and a knower of the Vedas. || 13 ||

A person born in the **Raudra** <note>The "Terrible" or "Fierce" year</note> year is fearsome, a keeper of animals, always intent on criticizing others, cunning, possessed of a bad reputation, evil-minded, and cruel. || 54 ||

### Results of Birth in the Durmati Year

A man born in the **Durmati** <note>The "Evil-minded" or "Foolish" year</note> year is one who takes great pride in fulfilling his own word, is devoid of cheerfulness, is highly lustful, inclined toward sinful deeds, and possesses a wicked intellect. || 55 ||

A person born in the Durmati year is proud of carrying out his own speech, lacks happiness, is extremely lecherous, a performer of bad deeds, and is of corrupt mind. || 55 ||

### Results of Birth in the Dundubhi Year

One born under the name **Dundubhi** <note>The "Drum" year, associated with celebration and resonance</note> will always be granted honor by kings; he will be endowed with elephants, horses, land, and gold, and will be exceedingly fond of the triple arts of music <note>The "Tauryatrika" refers to the triad of singing, instrumental music, and dance</note>. || 56 ||

A person born in the Dundubhi year is always honored by rulers, is possessed of wealth such as elephants, horses, land, and gold, and is a lover of dance and song. || 56 ||

### Results of Birth in the Rudhirodgari Year

A person born in **Rudhirodgari** <note>The "Blood-vomiting" or "Blood-expelling" year</note> has reddish eyes, may become extremely emaciated due to the onset of diseases like jaundice, is excessively angry, has deformed nails on his feet or hands, and suffers pain from weapons. || 57 ||

A person born in the Rudhirodgari year has red eyes, sometimes has a body made very weak by diseases such as jaundice, is extremely irritable, has bad nails, and suffers distress from the strike of a weapon. || 57 ||

### Results of Birth in the Raktaksha Year

A man born in **Raktaksha** <note>The "Red-eyed" year</note> is deeply devoted to righteous conduct and traditional customs, is highly influenced by the power of desire, cannot tolerate the superiority of others in the slightest, and suffers from blood-related ailments. || 58 ||

A person born in the *Raktaksha* <note>literally "Red-Eyed"</note> year is endowed with righteous conduct, is extremely lustful, cannot tolerate the progress of others, and suffers from eye diseases. || 58 ||

## Results of Birth in the Krodhana Year—

The person born in the year named *Krodhana* <note>meaning "Wrathful"</note> creates obstacles in the work of others, is fearsome due to an excess of the quality of darkness <note>original: "tamoguna," the quality of ignorance or inertia</note>, and is intent on deceiving the intellect of others. || 59 ||

A person born in the *Krodhana* year interferes in the work of others, is very fearsome due to the quality of darkness, and is a deceiver of others. || 59 ||

## Results of Birth in the Kshaya Year—

One whose birth occurs in the year called *Kshaya* <note>meaning "Loss" or "Destruction"</note> spends all earned wealth, is devoted to service, possesses a cruel disposition, and has little inclination toward the path of good deeds. || 60 ||

One born in the *Kshaya* year spends what they earn, is an employee <note>literally "engaged in service"</note>, is harsh, and gives little thought to performing good works. || 60 ||

## Now the results of the Solstices; therein, the results of birth in the Northern Solstice—

A man born during the Northern Solstice <note>original: "Saumyayana" or "Uttarayana," the period when the sun moves north toward the Tropic of Cancer</note> is always cheerful, blessed with the love of children and spouse, deeply contented, long-lived, devoted to good conduct, generous, and courageous. || 1 ||

A person born in the Northern Solstice is always happy, filled with joy through their wife and sons, long-lived, virtuous, liberal, and steadfast. || 1 ||

## Results of Birth in the Southern Solstice—

A man who has attained birth in the Southern Solstice <note>original: "Yamyayana" or "Dakshinayana," the period when the sun moves south toward the Tropic of Capricorn</note> possesses no small pride, is a performer of agricultural work, is rich in four-legged animals <note>livestock</note>, has a very harsh heart, is deceitful, and is indeed unbearable to other men. || 2 ||

A person born in the Southern Solstice is very arrogant, a farmer,

### Now, the Consideration of the Solstices —

> When the Sun is in the six signs starting from Capricorn, it is called the Northern Progress. When the Sun is in the six signs starting from Cancer, it is known as the Southern Progress.

When the Sun resides in the six zodiac signs beginning with Capricorn <note>Makara</note>, it is the Northern Solstice <term>Uttarayana: the period when the sun moves northward on the celestial sphere, considered auspicious</term>. When it resides in the six signs beginning with Cancer <note>Karka</note>, it is the Southern Solstice <term>Dakshinayana: the period when the sun moves southward</term>.

### Now, the Results of the Seasons; First, the Result of Birth in the Spring —

> A person born in Spring is as beautiful as the God of Love, wise, majestic, and proficient in the sciences of music and mathematics. Their heart is purified by the study of scriptures, and they are ever joyful. || 1 ||

A person born in the Spring season <note>Vasanta Ritu</note> is handsome like Kamadeva <note>the deity of desire</note>, intelligent, powerful, skilled in music and mathematics, possesses a heart made pure through the study of sacred texts, and is of a cheerful disposition. || 1 ||

### The Result of Birth in the Summer Season —

> Endowed with lordship, knowledge, wealth, and grain, a speaker with long and clean hair; such a person is an enjoyer of life and fond of sporting in the water, if they have attained birth in the summer time. || 2 ||

One whose birth occurs in the Summer season <note>Grishma Ritu</note> is endowed with prosperity, learning, wealth, and food-grains. They are a good orator, possess long and clean hair, are a seeker of pleasures, and enjoy playing in the water. || 2 ||

### The Result of Birth in the Rainy Season —

> Steadfast in battle, wise, majestic, a lover of horses, and handsome; of a phlegmatic and windy temperament, a delighter in women, the man born in the rains is full of joy. || 3 ||

A person born in the Rainy season <note>Varsha Ritu</note> is intelligent, powerful, fond of horses, beautiful, possesses a physical temperament dominated by phlegm and wind <note>Kapha and Vata in Ayurvedic terms</note>, enjoys the company of women, and is a person of diverse and joyful thoughts. || 3 ||

### The Result of Birth in the Autumn Season —

A man [born in Autumn] is slow to anger, of a windy temperament, proud, wealthy, fond of his work, and pure.

# The Fruits of the Seasons
Page 21

He who is born in the season of Autumn <note>Sanskrit: Sharad; typically September to November</note> is a lover of battle and possesses many vehicles. || 4 ||
A person born in the Autumn season has a slight temperament for anger, a "windy" constitution <note>referring to the Vata dosha in Ayurvedic medicine</note>, is proud, wealthy, interested in performing good deeds, pure, a lover of war, and is endowed with various modes of transport. || 4 ||

->The Results of Birth in the Pre-Winter Season<-

A man born in Hemanta <note>The season of "cool" or pre-winter, roughly November to January</note> becomes a minister to kings, is clever, generous, and endowed with beautiful qualities. He is devoted to righteous deeds and religion, is high-minded, and is always humble. || 5 ||
A person born in the Hemanta season is a royal counselor, clever, exceedingly generous, possessed of excellent virtues, engaged in auspicious religious works, and is wise. || 5 ||

->The Results of Birth in the Winter Season<-

One born in the Shishira season <note>The late winter or "dewy" season, roughly January to March</note> is constantly devoted to sweet foods and drinks, is very hungry, and enjoys the happiness of sons and a wife. He performs good deeds, has a fine appearance, is prone to anger, and is very powerful. || 6 ||
A person born in the Shishira season is dedicated to eating sweets, is extremely prone to hunger, possesses the happiness of children and a spouse, performs noble deeds, has a beautiful form, is irritable, and is possessed of great strength. || 6 ||

->Now, the Knowledge of the Seasons is Described in Context<-

When the Sun is in Pisces and Aries, it is known as Spring <note>Vasanta</note>. In Taurus and Gemini, it is Summer <note>Grishma</note>. In Cancer and Leo, it is the Rainy Season <note>Varsha</note>.
In Virgo and Libra, the season is called Autumn <note>Sharad</note>. In Scorpio and Sagittarius <note>original: "the pair of Scorpio," referring to the transition to the next sign</note>, it is Pre-Winter <note>Hemanta</note>. In Capricorn and Aquarius, it is Winter <note>Shishira</note>.
When the Sun resides in Pisces or Aries, it is Spring; in Taurus or Gemini, it is Summer; in Cancer or Leo, it is the Monsoon; in Virgo or Libra, it is Autumn; in Scorpio or Sagittarius, it is Pre-Winter; and when the Sun is in Capricorn or Aquarius, it is the Winter season.

->Now the Results of the Months; First, the Results of the Month of Chaitra<-

One born in the month of Chaitra <note>The first month of the Hindu calendar, overlapping March and April</note> is endowed with good deeds, knowledge, and humility; he is an enjoyer of life and an eater of sweet foods. He is devoted to worthy recipients and friends, acts as a counselor, and possesses wonderful secrets <note>or "extraordinary counsel"</note>. || 1 ||

# Results of Birth in the Month of Vaishakha:

> One born in Madhava <note>original: "Madhava," a poetic name for the month of Vaishakha</note> is well-featured, devoted to virtuous qualities, powerful, a devotee of the learned and the divine, amorous, long-lived, fond of drinking water, and blessed with the happiness of kinsmen. || 2 ||

A person born in the month of Vaishakha <note>mid-April to mid-May</note> is endowed with excellent physical characteristics, a seeker of merit and virtue, strong, devoted to gods and Brahmins <note>the priestly/scholarly class</note>, lustful, long-lived, often thirsty, and possesses the happiness of relatives. || 2 ||

# Results of Birth in the Month of Jyeshtha:

> One born in Jyeshtha is forgiving but of a restless mind, fond of living in foreign lands, intense, of diverse intellect, a procrastinator <note>original: "dirghasutra," literally 'long-threaded,' meaning one who takes a long time to complete tasks</note>, and a most eminent man. || 3 ||

A person born in the month of Jyeshtha <note>mid-May to mid-June</note> is forgiving, has a restless temperament, takes interest in residing abroad, is intense, possesses a unique intellect, is slow to act, and is highly respected among people. || 3 ||

# Results of Birth in the Month of Ashadha:

> One born in Ashadha spends much, is eloquent in speech, prone to carelessness, dear to his teachers, suffers from poor digestion, performs auspicious deeds, and is deeply proud. || 4 ||

A person born in the month of Ashadha <note>mid-June to mid-July</note> spends excessively, is very talkative, possesses a feminine temperament <note>original: "stri-samana-svabhava"</note>, is beloved by his gurus, has a weak digestive fire, performs noble deeds, and is extremely proud. || 4 ||

# Results of Birth in the Month of Shravana:

> One born in the month of Shravana is happy with sons, grandsons, wife, and friends; he obeys his father's commands, is world-famous, of a phlegmatic constitution, generous, and virtuous. || 5 ||

A person born in the month of Shravana <note>mid-July to mid-August</note> is happy with sons, grandsons, wife, and friends; he is an obeyer of his father's orders, famous in the world, prone to phlegm-related issues <note>Kapha constitution in Ayurveda</note>, a donor, and virtuous. || 5 ||

# Birth Results for the Month of Bhadrapada—
The person born in the month of Bhadrapada <note>August–September</note> will be wealthy but of a slender physical frame. He is a donor <note>generous with charity</note> and finds happiness through his wife and children. Such a man remains unchanged <note>equanimous</note> in both pleasure and pain. || 6 ||

> A person born in the month of Bhadrapada is wealthy, physically weak, a giver, endowed with the happiness of wife and sons, and maintains the same temperament in both happiness and sorrow. || 6 ||

---

# Birth Results for the Month of Ashvina—
The person born in Ashvina <note>September–October</note> is learned, wealthy, and dear to the royal family. He performs good deeds and is served by many attendants. He is a donor, a connoisseur of virtues, blessed with many sons, and possesses riches such as horses and livestock. || 7 ||

> A person born in the month of Ashvina is a scholar, wealthy, beloved by the ruling class, a doer of good works, possesses many servants, is generous, a judge of character, has many sons, and is endowed with wealth like horses and other assets. || 7 ||

---

# Birth Results for the Month of Kartika—
One born in the month of Kartika <note>October–November</note> performs righteous deeds, possesses great eloquence, and is wealthy with beautiful, curly hair. He is lustful, interested in trade <note>buying and selling</note>, and dedicated to virtuous actions. || 8 ||

> A person born in the month of Kartika is a performer of good deeds, talkative, wealthy, has beautiful hair, is amorous, and is clever in commerce. || 8 ||

---

# Birth Results for the Month of Agrahayana—
The person born in Margashirsha <note>November–December; also called Agrahayana</note> is devoted to visiting sacred pilgrimage sites, is of good character, and is skilled in various arts. He is fond of comforts, helps others, follows the path of the righteous, and is endowed with great prosperity. || 9 ||

> A person born in Margashirsha is engaged in pilgrimage, is well-behaved, skilled in the arts, enjoys luxuries, is philanthropic, follows the path of the virtuous, and is full of wealth and grain. || 9 ||

---

# Birth Results for the Month of Pausha—
The person born in Pausha <note>December–January</note> is philanthropic but lacks paternal wealth. He spends money earned through great hardship and is knowledgeable in rituals. He keeps his consultations secret, exerts effort in the study of the scriptures, and is notably thin of body. || 10 ||

A person born in the month of Pausha <note>December–January</note> is philanthropic, deprived of paternal wealth, earns money with great difficulty only to spend it, is clever in his work, keeps his thoughts secret, is a student of the scriptures, and possesses a weak physical constitution. ||10||

### Results of Birth in the Month of Magha—

> The man born in Magha is a knower of excellent mantras, associated with Vedic sages, devoted to the practice of knowledge spoken in Yoga, a conqueror of enemy hosts through his exceptional intelligence, and free from sin. ||11|| <note>original: "sanmantravidvaidikasādhuyogo..."</note>

A person born in the month of Magha <note>January–February</note> is a knower of the science of mantras, a scholar of the Vedas, one who keeps the company of holy men, is engaged in yogic practices, conquers his enemies through the excellence of his intellect, and is virtuous. || 11 ||

### Results of Birth in the Month of Phalguna—

> He who is born in Phalguna is a philanthropist, skillful, compassionate, endowed with strength, possessing a delicate body, inclined toward the arts of amorous play with women, and characterized by light or trivial speech. ||12|| <note>original: "paropakārī kuśalo dayālu..."</note>

A person born in the month of Phalguna <note>February–March</note> is philanthropic, clever, compassionate, strong, possesses a delicate body, is skillful in dalliance with women, and is prone to talking without a specific purpose. || 12 ||

### Results of Birth in the Intercalary Month—

> The man born in the intercalary month is of a mind detached from worldly objects, of virtuous character, a performer of various pilgrimages, free from disease, beloved by all, and a doer of his own good. ||13|| <note>original: "viṣayahīnamatiḥ sucaritrahṛd..."</note>

A person born in the Adhika Masa <note>The "extra" month added to the lunar calendar every three years to keep it in sync with the solar year; also called Malamasa or Purushottama Masa</note> is devoid of worldly attachments, possesses a good character, travels to many pilgrimage sites, is healthy, is dear to everyone, and looks after his own well-being. || 13 ||

### Results of Birth in the Bright Fortnight—

> If the time of birth is in the bright fortnight, the person is long-lived, highly well-behaved, possessed of wealth and sons, has a delicate bodily luster, and always spends his time in joy and humility. || 1 || <note>original: "cañvancirāyuḥ sutarāṃ suśīlaḥ..."</note>

A person born in the Shukla Paksha <note>The waxing phase of the moon</note> is long-lived, well-behaved, wealthy, possesses a delicate <insert>body</insert> <note>The source text has a typo 'reer' for 'shareer' (body)</note>, and always spends his time in happiness. ||1||

# The Results of Birth in the Dark Fortnight—
The man whose birth occurs during the dark fortnight <note>The waning phase of the moon, known as Krishna Paksha</note> is powerful, yet physically weak and restless. He is fond of quarrels, arrogant toward his own kin, and possessed by excessive lust. || 2 ||

---

# The Results of Birth during the Day—
One who is born during the day becomes radiant, possesses qualities similar to his father, has beautiful vision, and is dear to the king <note>In a modern context, this implies favor from authorities or the state</note>. He is honored by his kinsmen and is very wealthy. || 1 ||

---

# The Results of Birth during the Night—
One who is born at night has poor eyesight, suffers greatly from lust, is constantly sickly, and is unclean. He possesses a cruel soul and commits sins in secret. || 2 ||

---

# Now the Results of the Lunar Days; First, the Results of Birth on the First Day—
If a living being is born on the first lunar day <note>Pratipada, the first day after the full or new moon</note>, he possesses a large family and excellent knowledge. He is a man of discernment, adorned with ornaments of gold and jewels, and is of good character. He possesses an extremely charming luster and acquires wealth from the protector of the earth <note>The King or government</note>. || 1 ||

---

# The Results of Birth on the Second Day—
He is a giver, compassionate, virtuous, and discerning; he is blessed by his conduct and his habit of constant reflection.

# Jatakabharanam

A person born on the second lunar day <note>Sanskrit: Dvitiya</note> possesses a beautiful form, earns great fame through song, and is a mortal of high renown. || 2 ||
A person born in the second lunar day is a donor, compassionate, virtuous, thoughtful, blessed with good conduct, possesses a beautiful body, and has celebrated fame. || 2 ||

### Results of Birth on the Third Lunar Day

One born on the third lunar day <note>Sanskrit: Tritiya</note> is highly amorous, possessed of faultless knowledge, endowed with strength, and acquires wealth from royal families. Such a person is inclined to live abroad, is clever, luxurious, and possesses great self-respect. || 3 ||
A person born in the third lunar day is extremely lustful, joined with pure learning, <unclear>strong</unclear>, possesses wealth obtained from the royal court, resides in foreign lands, is clever, <unclear>luxurious</unclear>, and proud. || 3 ||

### Results of Birth on the Fourth Lunar Day

If the birth occurs on the fourth lunar day <note>Sanskrit: Chaturthi</note>, the person lives on debt, is very courageous, skilled in battle, but of a miserly nature. They take delight in gambling, possess a restless mind, and are prone to arguments. || 4 ||
One whose birth is in the fourth lunar day is a borrower of money, very daring, a <unclear>warrior</unclear>, a miser, a gambler, fickle-minded, and a disputant. || 4 ||

### Results of Birth on the Fifth Lunar Day

If the time of birth is indeed the fifth lunar day <note>Sanskrit: Panchami</note>, the man has a well-formed body, is endowed with a wife, sons, and friends, and is filled with kindness toward all living beings. He is honored by kings and is exceptionally generous. || 5 ||
One whose birth is in the fifth lunar day has a beautiful body, is joined with a wife, sons, and <unclear>friends</unclear>, is compassionate toward all creatures, respected by the state, and is a giver. || 5 ||

### Results of Birth on the Sixth Lunar Day

Born on the sixth lunar day <note>Sanskrit: Shashti</note>, a man is true to his promise, wealthy, blessed with sons, and possesses long thighs and knees. He is highly energetic, has wide fame, is clever, and distinguished, though his body may be covered in scars or sores. || 6 ||
One whose birth is in the sixth lunar day fulfills his word, is <unclear>wealthy</unclear>, has sons, possesses long thighs and long knees, is very powerful...

### Results of Birth on the Seventh Day (Saptami)—

> The man born on the seventh day is wise, a connoisseur of virtues, and possesses large eyes. His mind is naturally inclined toward honoring worthy people and worshipping the gods. He is a father of daughters, a seizer of others' wealth, and a conqueror of his enemies. || 7 ||

One born on the seventh day <term>Saptami; the seventh day of the lunar fortnight</term> is knowledgeable, recognizes merit in others, has large eyes, is a gentleman who maintains devotion to the deities, has female offspring, takes the wealth of others, and is a vanquisher of foes. || 7 ||

### Results of Birth on the Eighth Day (Ashtami)—

> He whose birth occurs on the eighth day possesses various types of wealth and the happiness of having sons; he is compassionate and holds an authoritative position of learning granted by the protector of the earth. He loves his wife but possesses a restless or fickle mind. || 8 ||

One born on the eighth day <term>Ashtami; the eighth day of the lunar fortnight</term> is endowed with various kinds of property and the joy of children, is merciful, holds an office related to education or knowledge in the King's court <note>original: "Prithvipal" meaning protector of the earth/King</note>, is affectionate toward his wife, and is of a restless nature. || 8 ||

### Results of Birth on the Ninth Day (Navami)—

> If the ninth lunar day is present at a man's birth, he is indifferent to the affairs of his kinsmen, speaks with harsh words, yet is intelligent and prone to opposition. He is a man who has lost his regard for traditional conduct. || 9 ||

A person born on the ninth day <term>Navami; the ninth day of the lunar fortnight</term> is averse to the work of his relatives, speaks harshly, is clever, oppositional, and is devoid of proper conduct and respect. || 9 ||

### Results of Birth on the Tenth Day (Dashami)—

> One born on the tenth day has a mind fixed solely on righteousness, is enriched with worldly grandeur, has a long neck, and is a reader of many scriptures. He is large-hearted, exceedingly humble, handsome, and full of desire. || 10 ||

A person born on the tenth day <term>Dashami; the tenth day of the lunar fortnight</term> possesses an intellect focused on religion and duty <term>Dharma</term>, is wealthy, has a long neck, is a scholar of many sacred texts, is generous, extremely modest, beautiful, and amorous. || 10 ||

# The Results of Birth on the Eleventh Lunar Day (Ekadashi)

> One born on the eleventh day is devoted to the worship of gods and priests, inclined toward charity, possesses a very pure heart, is skillful, focused on meritorious deeds, a performer of excellent actions, and is of a cheerful disposition. || 11 ||

A person born on the eleventh day <note>Ekadashi: the eleventh day of the lunar fortnight, often considered spiritually significant</note> worships deities and Brahmins <note>priestly class</note>, is charitable, has a pure heart, is capable, virtuous, performs superior work, and is always happy in spirit. || 11 ||

# The Results of Birth on the Twelfth Lunar Day (Dwadashi)

> One born on the twelfth day is a lover of water, well-versed in conduct, fond of enjoying life within their own home, a constant giver of food, recipient of wealth from the ruler, and blessed with progeny. || 12 ||

A person born on the twelfth day <note>Dwadashi</note> loves being near water, understands social dealings and etiquette, enjoys the comforts of their own residence, always distributes food to the needy, receives wealth from the king, and has children. || 12 ||

# The Results of Birth on the Thirteenth Lunar Day (Trayodashi)

> One born on the thirteenth day is endowed with beauty, characterized by purity and goodness, has a long neck, possesses offspring, is extremely brave, and is highly clever. || 13 ||

A person born on the thirteenth day <note>Trayodashi</note> is handsome, possesses a virtuous nature <note>Sattva-guna: the quality of balance, harmony, and goodness</note>, has a long neck, is blessed with sons, and is courageous and intelligent. || 13 ||

# The Results of Birth on the Fourteenth Lunar Day (Chaturdashi)

> One born on the fourteenth day is cruel, extremely brave, clever, prone to laughter, has a mind preoccupied with the play of desire, is unbearable, speaks very contrarily, and is full of anger. || 14 ||

A person born on the fourteenth day <note>Chaturdashi: the day preceding the full or new moon</note> is harsh, very valiant, witty, restless with lustful thoughts, intolerant of others, speaks excessively in opposition, and is prone to wrath. || 14 ||

# The Results of Birth on the Full Moon Day (Purnima)

> One with a very graceful body, who acquires wealth through just means,
> who is surrounded by many young women, and who experiences constant joy.

### The Results of Birth on a New Moon—

The person born on the New Moon <note>Sanskrit: Amavasya</note> is peaceful, high-minded, devoted to his father and mother, earns wealth through great hardship, is desirous of acquiring riches, is respected among people, yet is devoid of luster and joy, and possesses a weak or slender body. || 16 ||

### Now the Results of the Days of the Week; First, the Results of Birth on Sunday—

A person born on the day of the Sun <note>Sunday</note> is brave, has little hair, is victorious on the front lines of battle, has a dark-reddish complexion, a temperament dominated by bile <note>Pitta: one of the three humors in Ayurvedic medicine, associated with fire and heat</note>, is charitable, endowed with great enthusiasm, and possesses great physical power. || 1 ||

### The Results of Birth on Monday—

A person born on the day of the Moon <note>Monday</note> is a scholar, peaceful in nature, pleasant in speech, knowledgeable in rituals and procedures, earns his livelihood under the patronage of kings, and maintains an even temperament in both happiness and sorrow. || 2 ||

### The Results of Birth on Tuesday—

One born on the day of the Son of the Earth <note>Tuesday/Mars</note> is sarcastic in speech, extremely fond of battle, a minister to kings, earns a living from the earth <note>likely through agriculture or land ownership</note>, is endowed with courage, and possesses a very fierce or sharp temperament. || 3 ||

# The Fruits of the Lunar Mansions

> *A person born under the Ashwini mansion shall find great joy in women, ornaments, and children.* || 1 ||

A person born in the **Ashwini** <note>The first lunar mansion, associated with the twin physicians of the gods and symbolized by a horse's head.</note> mansion is characterized by a humility that shines through their service to others. They are a speaker of truth, an acquirer of all forms of wealth, and are blessed with the happiness of a spouse, fine jewelry, and children. || 1 ||

---

### The Results of Birth in the Bharani Mansion—

> *Always suffering ill-repute from great scandals, spending time in various diversions, greatly fearing water, restless and wicked is the soul born under Bharani.* || 2 ||

One whose birth occurs in the **Bharani** <note>The second mansion, ruled by Yama, the god of death; its symbol is the yoni or a clay vessel.</note> mansion is one who gains infamy through public scandal. They spend their life in various games and amusements, are extremely fearful of water, and possess a restless and mischievous nature. || 2 ||

---

### The Results of Birth in the Krittika Mansion—

> *Excessively hungry, devoid of the wealth of truth, possessing a mind prone to useless wandering, ungrateful, harsh of speech, and a doer of censurable acts is the creature in whose birth Krittika resides.* || 3 ||

He whose birth occurs in the **Krittika** <note>The third mansion, corresponding to the Pleiades; ruled by Agni, the god of fire.</note> mansion is constantly troubled by hunger and lacks the "wealth" of truthfulness. He wanders aimlessly, is ungrateful to those who help him, speaks bitterly, and engages in despicable or lowly activities. || 3 ||

---

### The Results of Birth in the Rohini Mansion—

> *Skilled in righteous deeds, a tiller of the soil, with a body shining with beautiful character, and an entire heart graced by the charms of speech is he whose birth-star is Rohini.* || 4 ||

A person born in the **Rohini** <note>The fourth mansion, associated with the star Aldebaran; it is considered the favorite dwelling of the Moon.</note> mansion is clever in performing religious and righteous duties. They are a farmer (or one who works the land), possesses a beautiful temperament and a handsome physique, and is able to express all their intentions clearly through eloquent speech. || 4 ||

## The Results of Birth in Ardra Nakshatra—

> <note>original: "क्षुधाधिको रूक्षशरीरकान्तिर्बन्धुप्रियः कोपयुतः कृतघ्नः । प्रसूतिकाले च भवेत्किलाद्रा दयार्द्रचेता न भवेन्मनुष्यः ॥ ६ ॥"</note>

## The Results of Birth in Punarvasu Nakshatra—

A person born in the <term>Punarvasu</term><note>The seventh lunar mansion, associated with Castor and Pollux; its name means "the return of the light."</note> Nakshatra has many friends, is a student of the <term>Shastras</term><note>Sacred Hindu scriptures or treatises.</note>, is adorned with jewels and gold ornaments, is a giver of charity, and is abundant in land and riches. || 7 ||

A person born in the <term>Pushya</term><note>The eighth lunar mansion, considered the most auspicious for spiritual growth; its name means "to nourish."</note> Nakshatra has a beautiful physique, is a devotee of his parents, is engaged in his own <term>Dharma</term><note>Religious and moral duty.</note>, is characterized by humility, is respected among men, and possesses wealth and means of transport. || 8 ||

A person born in the <term>Ashlesha</term><note>The ninth lunar mansion, symbolized by a coiled serpent; associated with the stars in Hydra.</note> Nakshatra is a useless wanderer, possesses wicked habits, causes unnecessary suffering to others, wastes good wealth on evil paths, and is overwhelmed by carnal desire. || 9 ||

# The Fruits of Birth in the Purva Phalguni Mansion

# The Fruits of Birth in the Uttara Phalguni Mansion

Such a man is steady and extremely soft-natured if born under Uttara Phalguni.

A person born in the <term>Uttara Phalguni</term> <note>The "Latter Reddish One," associated with patronage, kindness, and social stability</note> mansion is a donor, compassionate, of excellent character, highly renowned, a royal minister, steadfast, and of an extremely gentle nature. || 12 ||

# The Fruits of Birth in the Hasta Mansion

<header>In the Jatkabharana— <note>A classic 15th-century Sanskrit treatise on predictive astrology.</note></header>

### Results of Birth in Svati Nakshatra—

The person born under the star of **Svati** is as handsome as **Kamadeva** <note>The Hindu god of love and desire</note>, endowed with great luster, and finds immense joy in the company of beautiful women. Such a person remains exceedingly cheerful and possesses wealth obtained from the favor of kings. || 15 ||

### Results of Birth in Vishakha Nakshatra—

A person born under the star of **Vishakha** is always devoted to the performance of sacrifices and the worship of deities. In the practice of **alchemy** <note>original: "dhatu-kriya" — refers to the chemistry of metals or medicinal preparations</note>, they are sometimes fierce and sometimes mild. Such a person does not become a true friend to anyone. || 16 ||

### Results of Birth in Anuradha Nakshatra—

One whose birth occurs under the star of **Anuradha** possesses a beautiful complexion and great fame. They are constantly engaged in celebrations, are victors over their enemies, and are highly skilled in the various arts. Such a person is endowed with vast and diverse kinds of wealth. || 17 ||

### Results of Birth in Jyeshtha Nakshatra—

The person born under the star of **Jyeshtha** is particularly distinguished by excellent fame, beauty, and the power of authority. They are wealthy, possess shining valor, hold the highest reputation, and are considered the most eloquent among speakers. || 18 ||

### Now, the Consideration of Birth in Mula Nakshatra—

The sages declare that a birth occurring in the "forbidden limbs" <note>specific degrees or quarters of the constellation deemed inauspicious</note> of the **Mula** star destroys the entire lineage, root and branch. However, if the birth occurs otherwise <note>in the auspicious portions</note>, it brings special benefits, including good fortune, long life, and the growth of one's family. || 19 ||

Birth in the forbidden parts of the Mula Nakshatra causes the destruction of the family... <note>The text cuts off here and likely continues with specific remedies or further details on the next page.</note>

<header>The Results of the Constellations</header>

Otherwise, if the birth occurs in the auspicious portions of Mula <note>The Mula constellation is often feared, but this clarifies that certain parts are beneficial</note>, there is an increase in the family lineage and the person becomes wealthy. || 16 ||

### Consideration of the Untouchable Mula (Abhuktamula) —

> The final ghatika <note>A unit of time equal to 24 minutes</note> of Jyeshtha and the first two ghatikas of Mula are called "Abhuktamula." A child born during this time is considered a source of great difficulty. || 20 ||
> A father desiring his own welfare should not look upon the face of such a child for eight years. To remove the faults of this birth, the method of pacification (Shanti) is now described. || 21 ||

The final 1 ghatika of the Jyeshtha constellation and the first 2 ghatikas of the Mula constellation are known as *Abhuktamula* <note>original: "Abhuktamula" - literally 'the Mula that must not be enjoyed or experienced'</note>.

A father should not look at the face of a boy born in this period for 8 years. To pacify the negative defects of this birth, the ritual procedures are now stated:

### The Method of Mula Pacification (Mula-shanti) —

> One should fill a jar that has a hundred holes with gems, the roots of a hundred medicinal herbs, and seven types of earth. From the water flowing out of those holes... || 22 ||
> ...the child, the mother, and the father should be bathed by the Brahmins. Once the chanting (Japa), fire sacrifice (Homa), and charity (Dana) are performed, auspiciousness will surely follow. || 23 ||
> This ritual for the unfavorable portions of Mula is remembered by the wise. Those desiring well-being must consider the words of the Sages as truth. || 24 ||

In a water-filled jar with a hundred holes, place the nine gems, the roots of a hundred medicinal herbs, and earth from seven sacred places <note>original: "Saptamrittika" - typically soil from a stable, elephant shed, anthill, river confluence, etc.</note>. The child's mother and father should both be bathed by Brahmins using the water flowing from those holes. They should then perform chanting, fire sacrifices, and give donations. Those who desire welfare must follow these words of the Sages. By doing so, prosperity will certainly occur. || 22-24 ||

### Results of Birth in the Quarters of Mula —

> In the first three quarters of Mula, there is harm to the father, the mother, and wealth respectively. The fourth quarter is exceedingly auspicious. In the case of Sarpa <note>The Ashlesha constellation</note>, the opposite should be understood. || 25 ||

<meta>This page continues the astrological discourse on the effects of specific lunar mansions (Nakshatras), specifically focusing on the potentially malevolent influences of Mula and Ashlesha.</meta>

<page-num>36</page-num>
<header>In the Jatakabharana—</header>

For one born in the first three quarters <note>term: Pada; the four divisions of a lunar mansion</note> of the Mula constellation, there is a destruction of the father, mother, and wealth respectively. That is, if birth occurs in the first quarter, the father is affected; in the second quarter, the mother; and in the third quarter, wealth is lost. [If birth occurs in the fourth quarter, it is considered auspicious.]

In the Ashlesha constellation, the results should be understood as the reverse: the first quarter is auspicious, the second causes loss of wealth, the third causes loss to the mother, and the fourth causes loss to the father. || 25 ||

### Results of Birth During the Mula Constellation—

> <note>original: "कृष्णे तृतीया दशमी..."</note> If at the time of birth the Mula constellation coincides with the third or tenth day of the dark fortnight, or the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight, and is joined by Mars, Saturn, or Mercury, it surely brings about the uprooting of the entire lineage. || 26 ||

> <note>original: "दिवा सायं निशि प्रात..."</note> If birth occurs during the Mula constellation in the daytime, it is harmful to the father's family; in the evening, to the maternal uncle's family; at night, to the livestock; and in the morning, to the circle of friends. || 27 ||

### Placement of Time-Units for Mula and Ashlesha in the Human Form—

> <note>original: "मूर्ध्नि पञ्च मुखे पञ्च..."</note> Five units of time <note>term: Ghati; a period of 24 minutes</note> in the head, five in the mouth, eight in the shoulders, eight in the arms, two in the hands, eight in the heart, two in the navel, ten in the private parts, six in the knees, and six in the feet. By placing these units upon the human form, one should predict the results of Mula. || 28–29 ||

Starting from the beginning of the Mula constellation, one should perform the ritual placement <note>term: Nyasa; the mental or physical assignment of parts</note> of the time-units: 5 units in the head, 5 in the mouth, 8 in the shoulders, 8 in the arms, 2 in the hands, 8 in the heart, 2 in the navel, 10 in the genitals, 6 in the thighs, and 6 in the feet, and then declare the astrological prediction. || 28–29 ||

# The Results of the Human-Form Divisions of Mula—

> If in the head, one gains the royal umbrella; in the face, it destroys the father.
> On the shoulders, one carries heavy burdens; in the pair of arms, one performs no good deeds. || 30 ||
> In the two hands, one becomes a killer; in the heart, one attains a kingdom.
> In the navel area, a short life; and in the private parts, wonderful happiness. || 31 ||
> In the thighs, a love of wandering; in the feet, a shortness of life.
> This is indeed the fruit of the divisions of Mula as declared by the most eminent sages. || 32 ||

If birth occurs in the <term>ghati</term> <note>A unit of time equal to 24 minutes</note> corresponding to the head of the "human-form" of the Mula constellation, there is the gain of a royal umbrella <note>A symbol of high status or sovereignty</note>. In the divisions of the face, it causes the destruction of the father; in the shoulders, the person becomes a carrier of loads; in the arms, a doer of evil deeds; in the hands, a violent person; in the heart, the gain of a kingdom; in the navel, a short lifespan; in the genitals, one experiences extraordinary happiness; in the thighs, one is a wanderer; and in the feet, one has a short life. In this manner, the best of sages have described the results of birth within the various divisions of Mula. 30-32

# The Results of the Ashlesha Divisions—

> The wise should understand all of this regarding the Serpent Star <note>original: "Sarpe" referring to the Ashlesha nakshatra</note> as being exactly the opposite. || 33 ||

The meaning is clear. <note>The auspicious and inauspicious effects listed for Mula are reversed for those born under Ashlesha.</note> || 33 ||

# The Lords of the Moments for Mula and Ashlesha—

> The Demon, the Night-Walker, the Moon, Venus, and the Serpent Kings;
> The Father, the Mother, Death, Time, the Universal Gods, and the Great Lord; || 34 ||
> Sharva, Kubera, Venus, the Cloud, and the Sun;
> The Celestial Musician, the God of Death, Brahma, Vishnu, and Aryaman; || 35 ||
> Ishvara, Vishnu, Rudra, the Wind, and the Sages;
> The Six-Faced One, Bhringiriti, Gauri, and the one named Saraswati; || 36 ||
> And Prajapati—these are the thirty lords of the moments for Mula.
> For Ashlesha, they are in reverse order, and they grant fruits consistent with their names. || 37 ||

The meaning is clear. <note>This list identifies 30 deities who preside over the 30 subdivisions of the Mula constellation. For the Ashlesha constellation, the list is applied in reverse order, starting from Prajapati and ending with the Demon.</note> || 34-37 ||

# The Results of Inauspicious Auspicious-Times—
> The Rakshasa, the Yatudhana, the Pitri, the Yama,
> and the Kala—these lords of the Muhurtas <note>A Muhurta is a unit of time lasting approximately 48 minutes; each is governed by a specific deity or spirit.</note> are considered inauspicious if they are active at the time of birth. || 38 ||

Among the previously mentioned lords of the Muhurtas, the five known as Rakshasa, Yatudhana, Pitri, Yama, and Kala are inauspicious at the time of birth. || 38 ||

# The Tree of Mula—
> Four, seven, eight, ten, nine, five, six, and eleven.
> The root, trunk, bark, branch, leaf, flower, fruit, and crest. || 39 ||

One should construct the "Tree of Mula" <note>A symbolic diagram used to determine the specific influence of the Mula Nakshatra based on the exact timing of birth.</note> by assigning the duration of the Mula constellation as follows: the first 4 Ghatis <note>A Ghati is a traditional unit of time equal to 24 minutes.</note> to the Root, 7 Ghatis to the Trunk, 8 Ghatis to the Bark, 10 Ghatis to the Branch, 6 Ghatis to the Leaf, 5 Ghatis to the Flower, 6 Ghatis to the Fruit, and 11 Ghatis to the Crest (top). || 39 ||

# The Results of the Mula Tree—
> Within the divisions of the Mula Tree, auspiciousness is found in the fruit and the leaf.
> Inauspiciousness should certainly be understood to reside in the remaining parts. || 40 ||

In the divisions of the Mula Tree, if a birth occurs during the Ghatis assigned to the "fruit" or the "leaf," the result is auspicious; birth during any of the remaining parts should be known as inauspicious. || 40 ||

# Auspicious and Inauspicious Results for those born in Mula—
> In the quarter, the Muhurta, the time, the tree, and the human-form diagram;
> If inauspiciousness predominates, the result is bad; if auspiciousness predominates, the result is good. || 41 ||

Among these four factors—the results of the quarter (Pada), the Muhurta, the Tree (Mula-vriksha), and the Human-form diagram (Purushakriti Chakra)—if the inauspicious indications are more numerous, the outcome is bad; if the auspicious indications are more numerous, the outcome should be understood as good. || 41 ||

# Results of Birth in the Father's Constellation—
> If a birth occurs under the same constellation as the father or the brother,
> It certainly causes misfortune to the father or the elder brother. || 42 ||

If a child is born under the same birth star (Nakshatra) as their father or their elder brother, it acts as a cause of misfortune (Arishta) <note>Arishta refers to a period of ill-luck or a "stroke of fate" that can affect health or prosperity.</note> for that father or elder brother. || 42 ||

### Now the Results of Birth in the Yogas; First, the Results of Vishkambha Yoga—

### Results of Birth in Priti Yoga—

> An eloquent speaker, endowed with the wealth of a shimmering form, a great giver, and of cheerful countenance.
> He finds joy in the company of the virtuous and loves righteousness—such is the man born in Priti. || 2 ||

He whose birth occurs in the <term>Priti Yoga</term> <note>The second Yoga; the name means 'affection' or 'love'</note> is an eloquent speaker, possesses a beautiful appearance and wealth, is an extreme donor <note>very charitable</note>, has a cheerful face, is personally delighted by the joy of good people, and maintains an affection for dharma <note>righteousness/duty</note>. || 2 ||

### Results of Birth in Ayushman Yoga—

> He possesses the courage to acquire wealth and is inclined toward various places, gardens, and vehicles.
> He who is born in Ayushman will indeed be long-lived and endowed with honor. || 3 ||

A man born in the <term>Ayushman Yoga</term> <note>The third Yoga; the name means 'the long-lived one'</note> is courageous in the pursuit of earning wealth, enjoys visiting gardens in various places, possesses a long lifespan, and is full of self-respect. || 3 ||

# In the Jatakabharana—

## The Results of Birth in the Auspicious Yoga (Saubhagya-yoga)—

The person born under the Auspicious Yoga will be wise, wealthy, devoted to the truth, virtuous in conduct, strong, and possess great discernment. He shines with commendable good fortune and is highly self-respecting <note>The original Sanskrit 'mahabhimani' can mean 'greatly proud' or 'highly self-respecting' depending on context; here it implies a noble dignity.</note>. || 4 ||

A person born in the Saubhagya <term>Saubhagya: literally 'good fortune' or 'auspiciousness'</term> Yoga is knowledgeable, wealthy, a speaker of truth, well-behaved, powerful, wise, endowed with beautiful fortune, and very proud. || 4 ||

## The Results of Birth in the Brilliant Yoga (Shobhana-yoga)—

The person born under the Brilliant Yoga is quick-witted, highly clever, excellent in conversation, endowed with charming dignity, and possesses a virtuous mind. He is always intent on performing auspicious deeds. || 5 ||

A person born in the Shobhana <term>Shobhana: meaning 'bright', 'brilliant', or 'virtuous'</term> Yoga is clever in giving quick replies, beautiful, dignified, possesses a fine intellect, and is dedicated to doing good work every day. || 5 ||

## The Results of Birth in the Severe Knot Yoga (Atiganda-yoga)—

The person born under the Severe Knot Yoga is always arrogant, suffers from throat ailments, is prone to anger, has very large hands and feet, and is extremely cunning. He is fond of quarrels, has a long jaw, and is a hypocrite. || 6 ||

A person born in the Atiganda <term>Atiganda: literally 'great knot' or 'major obstacle', considered a malefic yoga in Vedic astrology</term> Yoga is always full of ego, has diseases of the throat, is wrathful, has very large limbs, is very deceitful, quarrelsome, has a large chin, and is a fraud. || 6 ||

## The Results of Birth in the Virtuous Action Yoga (Sukarma-yoga)—

The person born at the time of the Virtuous Action Yoga is always joyful, skilled in all arts, endowed with courage and enthusiasm, a benefactor to others, and performs excellent deeds. || 7 ||

A person born in the Sukarma <term>Sukarma: meaning 'good deeds' or 'virtuous actions'</term> Yoga is always filled with joy, expert in all crafts/arts, brave, energetic, philanthropic, and a doer of beautiful works. || 7 ||

## The Results of Birth in the Firmness Yoga (Dhriti-yoga)—

He is wise, generous, constantly delighted, eminent in assemblies, restless, and of good character...

### Now, the results of birth in Taitila Karana—

One who is born in the **Taitila** <term>Karana (one of the eleven divisions of a lunar day)</term> possesses a beautiful and delicate body. Such a person is fond of play and amorous sports, is a connoisseur of the arts, and is highly skilled in the art of speech. They are characterized by a virtuous nature, a pure and flawless intellect, and restless, sparkling eyes. || 4 ||
<note>The Sanskrit verse emphasizes 'Charu-komala-kalevara' (a charming and soft physique) and 'Kala-jna' (one who understands the arts).</note>

### The results of birth in Gara Karana—

A person born in the **Gara** Karana is devoted to helping others and possesses a deep, reflective intellect. They are clever, have conquered their enemies, and are brave and exceptionally firm in their resolve. Such an individual is highly generous and possesses a handsome physical form. || 5 ||

### The results of birth in Vanija Karana—

One whose birth occurs during the **Vanija** Karana is an expert in various arts and is naturally cheerful and smiling. They are wise, held in high esteem by others, and earn their wealth through trade and commerce. || 6 ||
<note>The name 'Vanija' itself relates to trade or a merchant; hence the astrological association with 'Vanijyata' or commercial success.</note>

### The results of birth in Vishti Karana—

A person born when the **Vishti** (also known as **Bhadra**) Karana is active has a beautiful face but is restless and fickle. They are physically powerful and can defeat a multitude of enemies with ease. However, they may possess a wicked or mischievous mind and a tendency to sleep excessively. || 7 ||
<note>Vishti is often considered an inauspicious time in elective astrology, which explains the mention of 'Khala-mati' (a wicked mind) despite the physical strengths mentioned.</note>

### The results of birth in Shakuni Karana—

One born in the **Shakuni** Karana possesses an intellect nurtured by masters and is endowed with a multitude of virtues. They are proficient in the practice of <term>Mantra-Vidya (the science of sacred chants and rituals)</term> and are always alert and cautious. They form friendships with good people, are blessed with all kinds of good fortune, and are naturally inclined toward the knowledge of omens.
<note>original: "Shakuna-jnana-shila" — refers to the study of bird omens or general augury.</note>

# From the *Jatakabharana*—
<note>The *Jatakabharana* is a classical 15th-century Sanskrit treatise on natal astrology authored by Dhundhiraja.</note>

A birth in the *Gandanta* <note>original: "गण्डान्त" - a "knot's end" or spiritual junction point between certain zodiac signs and lunar mansions, considered a precarious time for birth</note> of a lunar day destroys the father; in the *Gandanta* of a lunar date, it destroys the mother; and in the *Gandanta* of the Ascendant <note>the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note>, it destroys the brother.

If the birth occurs in all three types of *Gandanta*, it destroys the entire lineage. || 52 ||

### Now, the Results of Birth in the Various *Ganas*—First, the Results of the Divine *Gana*:

> The man born in the Divine *Gana* possesses a beautiful voice, is straightforward in speech and intellect, and eats sparingly. He recognizes the virtues of others, has his own virtues praised by the wise, and is wealthy. || 1 ||

A person born in the Divine *Gana* <note>original: "देवगण" (Deva Gana) - one of three temperamental categories in Vedic astrology based on the birth star</note> has a pleasant voice, speaks gently, possesses a clear intellect, eats little, is highly appreciative of merit, is virtuous, and is wealthy. || 1 ||

### Results of Birth in the Human *Gana*:

> Devoted to the worship of gods and others, proud, wealthy, compassionate, strong, and skilled in the arts; the man born in the Human *Gana* is wise, possesses great luster, and brings happiness to many. || 2 ||

One born in the Human *Gana* <note>original: "मनुष्यगण" (Manushya Gana)</note> is a devotee of the gods and priests, is proud, wealthy, kind, powerful, knowledgeable in the arts, a scholar, handsome, and a provider of happiness to many. || 2 ||

### Results of Birth in the Demonic *Gana*:

> A great talker and hard-hearted, he is daring, prone to anger, and arrogant. Of wicked conduct, a maker of quarrels, and very strong, the man born in the Demonic *Gana* is an opponent to others. || 3 ||

A person born in the Demonic *Gana* <note>original: "राक्षसगण" (Rakshasa Gana)</note> talks excessively, is hard-hearted, bold, angry, haughty, of bad character, quarrelsome, powerful, and antagonistic toward people. || 3 ||

> Greatly proud, virtuous, and irritable; an opponent to his own friends yet a friend to others. He achieves special fame through his own valor; the man born when Aries is rising is exceedingly wrathful. || 1 ||

A person born in the Aries Ascendant <note>original: "मेषलग्न" (Mesha Lagna)</note> is very proud, virtuous, angry, an adversary to his own friends, a friend to strangers, and one who attains fame through his own courage. || 1 ||

One born when the sign of Aquarius is rising <note>original: "Kumbha Lagna"</note> is restless in mind, excessively lustful, possesses a beautiful body, is affectionate toward friends, an accumulator of grains, and is prone to ostentation. || 11 ||

### Results for one born in the sign of Pisces —

One born when the sign of Pisces is rising <note>original: "Meena Lagna"</note> is clever, eats little, has moderate sexual desire, possesses fine jewels and gold, is restless, extremely shrewd, and is skilled in the creation of various artistic works. || 12 ||

### Now, the variation in the intensity of the aforementioned results —

If the rising sign <note>the Ascendant</note> is strong at the time of birth, the aforementioned results are realized in full. If the rising sign is weak, or if it is occupied or aspected by cruel planets <note>malefics like Mars or Saturn</note>, the results are realized only to a small extent. || 13 ||

### The timing for obtaining the results of the Year and other cycles —

The results mentioned for the Year <note>Samvatsara</note> and others should be understood to manifest at specific times. The results of the Year occur during the period <note><term>Dasha</term>: a planetary period or "ruling" time</note> of the lord of the civil year <note>Savana year</note>. The results of the Solstice <note>Ayana</note> and the Seasons <note>Ritu</note> occur during the period of the Sun. || 14 ||

The results of the Month occur during the period of the Lord of the Month. The results of the Lunar Fortnight <note>Paksha</note> and the Constellations <note>Nakshatra</note> occur during the period of the Moon. The results of the Lunar Day <note>Tithi</note> and the Half-Lunar Day <note>Karana</note> occur during the sub-periods of the Sun within the major period of the Moon. || 15 ||

The results of the Day of the Week should be considered during the period of the Lord of that Day. The results of the Yoga <note>a specific lunar-solar longitudinal relationship</note> occur during the period of the planet strengthened by the Sun and Moon. The results of the Rising Sign occur during the period of the Lord of the Rising Sign; this is the primary way to determine the destruction or fulfillment of the house being aspected. || 16 ||

The results of the Month are obtained during the period of the Lord of the Month; [the results of the Fortnight] during the period of the Moon...

### The Diagram Named Dimba (The Human Form)—

> In the diagram named Dimba, place three stars starting from the Sun's constellation on the head, and three on the face.
> Place two on the shoulders, two on the upper arms, and two on the two hands; five stars are placed on the chest. || 1||
> One each on the navel and the male organ, two on the knees, and six on the pair of feet.
> This should always be envisioned for men; the best of sages have declared the results herein. || 2 ||

Starting from the constellation (<term>Nakshatra</term>) in which the Sun is currently situated: place 3 constellations on the head, 3 on the face, 2 on both shoulders, 2 on both upper arms, 2 on both hands, 5 on the chest, 1 on the navel, 1 on the genitals, 2 on both thighs/knees, and 6 on both feet. By establishing this human-shaped <term>Dimba Chakra</term><note>A diagnostic grid shaped like a human figure</note>, one should understand the results according to which limb the birth constellation falls upon, as described hereafter. || 1-2 ||

If the birth constellation falls on the mouth/face, the person will be an eater of sweet foods, one who sleeps on beautiful beds, and will be of a cheerful, smiling disposition. || 4 ||

### He describes the method for arranging the twelve houses—

> Having constructed a wheel divided into twelve distinct parts, one should place therein
> the twelve zodiac signs starting from the Ascendant, clearly following the counter-clockwise order of the numbers.
> The planets should then be placed clearly within the signs where they are situated;
> from these, the wise practitioner should declare good or bad results according to the traditional scriptures of Horoscopy. || 1 ||

First, having drawn a chart consisting of twelve divisions, one should write the sign of the Ascendant <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of birth.</note> in the first section and then establish the twelve signs in order moving to the left. Now, having written each planet in the sign where it resides, one should declare the auspicious or inauspicious results according to the methods described hereafter. || 1 ||

### What is to be considered in the House of the Body—

> Appearance, the determination of complexion, distinguishing marks, caste, the measure of lifespan,
> happiness, and even sorrows and courage—all of this must indeed be observed from the Ascendant. || 2 ||

Appearance, color, physical marks, class, the determination of age, happiness, sorrow, and boldness—all these should be judged from the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the first house of the horoscope representing the self</term>. || 2 ||

### Determination of the results of the House of the Body—

> If the Ascendant is aspected by all the planets, the person is endowed with graceful charms and is very powerful;
> he is a leader in his family, possesses a long life, is possessed of fear <note>original: "bhaya," likely implying a sense of awe or respectability here, or perhaps "fearless" depending on the specific school of interpretation</note>, and is the destroyer of his circle of enemies. || 3 ||

If the place of the Ascendant is joined by the sight <note>In astrology, "aspects" or "sight" refers to the influence planets exert on houses other than the one they occupy.</note> of all the planets, then the person is full of humor and joy, strong, the best in their lineage, long-lived, respected, and a destroyer of enemies. || 3 ||

### Combinations for Wealth and Poverty—

> If three benefic planets are situated in the Ascendant, they make the person a humble king.
> If three malefic planets are there, they make him utterly joined with sorrow, poverty, and grief, and a great glutton. || 4 ||

If three benefic planets <note>Naturally "gentle" planets like Jupiter, Venus, or a strong Moon.</note> are seated in the Ascendant, the subject becomes a king and is humble. If three malefic planets <note>Naturally "harsh" planets like Mars, Saturn, or Rahu.</note> are seated in the Ascendant, he is miserable, poor, full of grief, and eats excessively. || 4 ||
