# Results of Aspects on Saturn
Page 186

### Results of Jupiter's Aspect on Saturn in Cancer —

The person born when Saturn is in the sign of Cancer and is aspected <note>aspected: in astrology, this refers to a specific angular relationship between planets where one 'looks' at or influences another</note> by Jupiter, is endowed with land, sons, a home, a wife, and wealth, as well as gems, vehicles, and ornaments. (23)

If Saturn, situated in the sign of Cancer, is seen by Jupiter, the native possesses land, children, a house, a spouse, wealth, jewels, transport, and decorations. (23)

### Results of Venus's Aspect on Saturn in Cancer —

Men born when the son of the Sun <note>original: "Arkaputra" — a common epithet for Saturn</note> is in Cancer and aspected by Venus will surely be devoid of generosity, dignity, beautiful honor, beauty, and the excellence of pure, eloquent speech. (24)

If Saturn is situated in Cancer and is seen by Venus, the native is lacking in generosity, pride, respect, physical beauty, superiority, and pleasant speech. (24)

### Results of the Sun's Aspect on Saturn in Leo —

A person born when the son of the Sun <note>original: "Bhanusuta" — another name for Saturn</note> is in Leo and aspected by the Sun will be devoid of wealth, grain, vehicles, good conduct, truth, and excellent endeavors. (25)

If Saturn is situated in the sign of Leo and is seen by the Sun, the native is bereft of money, food stores, transport, proper behavior, and noble actions. (25)

### Results of the Moon's Aspect on Saturn in Leo —

The son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note> situated in the Lion <note>Leo</note> and aspected by the Moon <note>original: "Harinanka" — literally 'the one with the deer-mark', meaning the Moon</note> makes a man possess fine gems, ornaments, clothes, and beautiful fame, and grants him the fullness of happiness from a wife, friends, and sons, giving him a pleasant appearance. (26)

If Saturn is situated in the sign of Leo and is seen by the Moon, the native is filled with jewels, ornaments, garments, lovely reputation, and the happiness of a spouse, friends, and children. (26)

### Results of Mars's Aspect on Saturn in Leo —

A man will be extremely skillful in the works of war, devoid of compassion, prone to anger, and of a cruel nature if the son of the Sun is in Leo and aspected by the son of the Earth <note>original: "Bhumisuta" — an epithet for Mars</note>. (27)

# Jatakabharanam
<note>The title translates to "The Ornament of Nativity," a classic 15th-century treatise on predictive astrology (Jyotisha) authored by Dhundhiraja.</note>

If Saturn is situated in the sign of Leo and is aspected <note>In Vedic astrology, an 'aspect' or 'drishti' refers to a planet 'looking at' or influencing another from a specific distance.</note> by Mars:
The person born is highly skilled in warfare, merciless, irritable, and possesses a cruel nature. || 27 ||

->The result of Mercury aspecting Saturn while in the sign of Leo:<-

> The son of the Sun <note>original: "tapanasya sunuh" — a common epithet for Saturn</note>, situated in Leo and aspected by the son of the Moon <note>original: "somasuteksitashcha" — an epithet for Mercury</note>, 
> makes the person born devoid of wealth, wife, children, and happiness; they are miserable and overcome by low-class vices. || 28 ||

If Saturn is situated in the sign of Leo and is aspected by Mercury:
The person born is deprived of the happiness of wealth, wife, and sons; they are wretched and engaged in base or demeaning activities. || 28 ||

> Saturn <note>original: "saurir" — 'Son of the Sun'</note> staying in the Lion <note>Leo</note> and aspected by the Teacher <note>Jupiter</note>, 
> makes a man endowed with good friends, sons, and virtues; famous, of excellent conduct, exceedingly humble, and the lord of a city or village. || 29 ||

If Saturn is situated in the sign of Leo and is aspected by Jupiter:
The person born is endowed with excellent friends, sons, and various virtues; they are famous, virtuous, very humble, and the master of a town or village. || 29 ||

->The result of Venus aspecting Saturn while in the sign of Leo:<-

> The son of the Sun, staying in the Five-Faced One <note>original: "panchananastho" — a poetic term for the Lion/Leo</note> and aspected by the son of Bhrigu <note>Venus</note>, 
> would make a man endowed with wealth, grains, vehicles, and comforts, yet tormented by women. || 30 ||

If Saturn is situated in the sign of Leo and is aspected by Venus:
The person born is endowed with wealth, food-grains, vehicles, and comforts, but suffers distress caused by women. || 30 ||

->The result of the Sun aspecting Saturn while in the house of Jupiter:<-

> A man obtains fame, acquisition of wealth, great honors, and a tendency for affection toward the children of others, 
> when Saturn is in the house of the Teacher of the Gods <note>Sagittarius or Pisces, ruled by Jupiter</note> and aspected by the Lord of the Day-Lotuses <note>the Sun</note>. || 31 ||

If Saturn is situated in Sagittarius or Pisces and is aspected by the Sun:
The person born is famous, an acquirer of wealth, highly dignified, and shows great affection toward the children of others. || 31 ||

# The Results of Saturn and Other Planets

### The result of the Moon's aspect on Saturn when located in the house of Jupiter—

**"A person born with Saturn in the house of the Preceptor <note>Jupiter</note> and viewed by the Moon is possessed of good conduct, separated from his mother, adorned with two names, and enjoys the happiness of children, wealth, and a wife." || 32 ||**

If Saturn is situated in the sign of Sagittarius or Pisces and is viewed by the Moon, the native is characterized by righteous behavior, suffers separation from the mother, is known by two names, and desires the happiness of a wife for the sake of having a son. || 32 ||

---

### The result of Mars's aspect on Saturn when located in the house of Jupiter—

**"The son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note> in the house of the Minister of the Gods <note>Jupiter</note>, when observed by the son of the Earth <note>Mars</note>, makes a man afflicted by wind-related diseases, acting against the world, a traveler, and very miserable." || 33 ||**

If Saturn is situated in the sign of Sagittarius or Pisces and is viewed by Mars, the native is afflicted by <term>Vata</term> <note>wind-based ailments in Ayurvedic medicine</note>, acts in opposition to the people, resides in foreign lands, and is impoverished. || 33 ||

---

### The result of Mercury's aspect on Saturn when located in the house of Jupiter—

**"A man is beautiful in his virtues, exceedingly wealthy, a recipient of great authority from the king of men, and shines with good conduct when Saturn is viewed by Mercury while in the house of the Preceptor." || 34 ||**

If Saturn is situated in the sign of Sagittarius or Pisces and is viewed by Mercury, the native is beautiful due to his qualities, wealthy, receives authority from a great king, and is of virtuous conduct. || 34 ||

---

### The result of Jupiter's aspect on Saturn when located in the house of Jupiter—

**"A human born when the son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note> has reached the house of Jupiter and is viewed by Jupiter becomes a chief minister to a king or a general of an army, possessed of all wealth, strong, and of good character." || 35 ||**

If Saturn is situated in the sign of Sagittarius or Pisces and is viewed by Jupiter, the native becomes a minister to a king or a commander of an army, is endowed with all types of prosperity, is powerful, and possesses a good nature. || 35 ||

If Saturn is positioned in the house of the Teacher of the Immortals <note>original: "amarācāryya-gṛhaṃ"; referring to the signs of Jupiter: Sagittarius or Pisces</note> and is viewed by the Minister of the Demons <note>original: "dānava-mantri"; referring to the planet Venus</note>, the person will be as follows: ॥ 36 ॥

### The result of the Sun's aspect on Saturn when in its own house—

A man becomes one with an unattractive wife, a consumer of others' food, burdened by many struggles and diseases, and a resident of foreign lands when Saturn is in its own abode <note>original: "nijāgāra"; the signs Capricorn or Aquarius</note> and is aspected by the Sun. ॥ 37 ॥

If Saturn is situated in the sign of Capricorn or Aquarius and is aspected by the Sun, the person born will have a wife of poor appearance, will subsist on the food of others, will be afflicted with illness despite many efforts, and will dwell in a foreign country. ॥ 37 ॥

### The result of the Moon's aspect on Saturn when in its own house—

Saturn, staying in its own sign and aspected by the Nectar-Rayed One <note>original: "amṛtaraśmi"; the Moon</note>, makes a man wealthy in riches and women, yet followed by sin, fickle in nature, opposed to his mother, and overcome by lust. ॥ 38 ॥

If Saturn is situated in the sign of Capricorn or Aquarius and is aspected by the Moon, the person born will possess wealth and women, but will be sinful, restless, hostile toward his mother, and lustful. ॥ 38 ॥

### The result of Mars' aspect on Saturn when in its own house—

Brave, cruel, daring, endowed with many virtues, superior to all, always cheerful of heart, and famous—such a mortal is born when the Son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note> is in his own sign and attains the gaze of the Son of the Earth <note>original: "dhātrī-putra"; Mars</note>. ॥ 39 ॥ <note>The original text repeats the number 36 here in error; it is corrected to 39 for sequence.</note>

If Saturn is situated in the sign of Capricorn or Aquarius and is aspected by Mars, the person born will be brave, fierce, courageous, endowed with beautiful qualities, the best among people, always happy, and famous. ॥ 39 ॥

### The result of Mercury's aspect on Saturn when in its own house—

The Son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note>, standing in his own field and aspected by the Son of the Moon <note>Mercury</note>, makes mortals possessors of good vehicles, courageous, full of strength, wise, and devoted to various kinds of work. ॥ 40 ॥

<header>Jataka Bharanam (The Jewel of Nativity)</header>

### The Results of the Sun in Gemini

A person born while the Lord of Day <note>The Sun</note> is in Gemini will be well-versed in the science of mathematics and the fine arts. They are characterized by a pure nature and are famous for their beautiful, wonderful speech. Such a person is truly endowed with great humility and a deep understanding of ethics and diplomacy.

### The Results of the Sun in Cancer

If the Sun is positioned in Cancer, the individual may lack a friendly or virtuous disposition. They are a "knower of time" <note>likely referring to an astrologer or one obsessed with timing</note> and tend to disregard the instructions of their father. Such a person experiences fluctuations between wealth and poverty, yet remains significant or respected in both states.

### The Results of the Sun in Leo

When the Sun resides in Leo <note>original: "karivairigate," meaning the enemy of the elephant, a poetic term for the Lion</note>, the person possesses a steady mind and great prowess. They are endowed with wonderful and widespread fame. Such a person is devoted to the king <note>or government/authorities</note> and finds joy in helping or pleasing others.

### The Results of the Sun in Virgo

With the Lord of Day situated in the sign of the Maiden <note>Virgo</note>, a person shall receive wealth from the king. They are soft-spoken, devoted to sacred scriptures and music, and possess such great power that they are capable of destroying their enemies.

### The Results of the Sun in Libra

If the Jewel of the Day <note>The Sun</note> is in the Scales <note>Libra</note>, the person remains perpetually fearful of the king. They tend to create opposition among people and may lean toward sinful acts. Such a person possesses a quarrelsome mind and takes interest in the work of others, rather than finding wealth in jewels or riches.

### The Results of Mars in Aries—

The son of the Earth <note>original: "Avanijah," a name for Mars</note>, when placed in the sign of the Goat <note>Aries</note>, constantly provides a man with honors from kings, the arrival of wealth, pleasant speech, splendor, and great courage, making him beloved by the whole world. || 25 ||

If Mars is situated in the sign of Aries, the person will be endowed with honor and wealth by the king, will be a sweet speaker, radiant, very courageous, and a favorite of everyone in the world. || 25 ||

### The Results of Mars in Taurus—

Mars situated in the Bull <note>Taurus</note> indicates little happiness regarding home and wealth, the rise of enemies, and residing in the houses of others. It brings a lack of humility, digestive fire ailments <note>Agnimandya, or dyspepsia</note>, and suffering caused by one's own children. || 26 ||

If Mars is situated in the sign of Taurus, the person will have little happiness from home and wealth, an increase in enemies, will dwell in the houses of others, will be immodest, afflicted by digestive diseases, and troubled by his sons. || 26 ||

### The Results of Mars in Gemini—

When situated in the Twins <note>Gemini</note>, the son of the Earth <note>Mars</note> certainly grants a man mastery over many arts, but also causes quarrels with family members, a love for wandering away from one's own place, and happiness primarily derived from his sons. || 27 ||

If Mars is situated in the sign of Gemini, the person will be skilled in many arts, will quarrel with his kinsmen, will be fond of traveling, and will receive happiness from his sons and family. || 27 ||

### The Results of Mars in Cancer—

When Mars is in the abode of the Moon <note>original: "Himakaralayage," referring to the sign of Cancer</note>, the person stays in the homes of others, is very miserable, lacks intelligence, is subdued by the rise of enemies, and enters into quarrels with powerful women. || 28 ||

If Mars is situated in the sign of Cancer, the person will reside in the houses of others, be very poor, foolish, troubled by enemies, and will fight with a strong-willed woman. || 28 ||

### The Results of Mars in Leo—

Exceedingly endowed with the happiness of children and wife, with enemies destroyed, and possessing great diligence and courage...

# The Jewel of Natal Astrology

When the Son of the Earth <note>original: "avanine"; a name for Mars</note> occupies the sign of the Lion <note>Leo</note>, a man becomes endowed with the knowledge of both right and wrong conduct. ||29||

If Mars is situated in the sign of Leo, the native will be exceedingly happy with his sons and wife, a destroyer of enemies, highly industrious and courageous, and one who understands the distinction between ethics and injustice. || 29 ||

### The Results of Mars in the Sign of Virgo

He becomes a worshiper of virtuous people, a leader among the masses, and devoted to the performance and officiating of sacrifices. When the Son of the Earth is associated with the Maiden <note>Virgo</note>, he is a lord of the land and happy through the festivities of women. ||30||

If Mars is situated in the sign of Virgo, the native is a worshiper of holy men, a leader among groups of people, one who performs and sponsors Vedic sacrifices <note>term: "yajna" (sacred fire rituals)</note>, and one who enjoys happiness derived from the earth and from women. || 30 ||

### The Results of Mars in the Sign of Libra

Afflicted by heavy expenditures of wealth, physical deformity, and the distress of having previously displeased his elders; when the Son of the Earth is in the Merchant <note>Libra</note>, the man is restless and suffers sorrow arising from land and women. ||31||

If Mars is located in the sign of Libra, the native spends a great deal of wealth, may have a missing limb or physical disability, feels remorse after having been unkind to his teachers or elders, is agitated, and suffers grief on account of property and women. || 31 ||

### The Results of Mars in the Sign of Scorpio

Endowed with the fear of poison, fire, and weapons, yet possessing great happiness from sons, daughters, and his wife; when the Son of the Earth occupies the Reptile <note>Scorpio</note>, he is devoted to the king and achieves victory over others. ||32||

If Mars is located in the sign of Scorpio, the native is subject to fears involving poison, fire, and weapons, but is extremely happy with his sons, daughters, and wife; he is devoted to the sovereign and attains victory over his enemies. || 32 ||

### The Results of Mars in the Sign of Sagittarius

Endowed with the dignity of chariots and horses, yet pained by wounds inflicted by great enemies; when the Son of the Earth is stayed in the Bow <note>Sagittarius</note>, the man has a good wife but is fond of wandering away from the forest of his home. ||33||

If Mars is seated in the sign of Sagittarius, the native is possessed of chariots, horses, and gravity <note>or honor</note>—

### The Results of Jupiter in Sagittarius—

> **Indeed, there is a love for distribution <note>charity</note>, great magnificence, wealth, and a collection of vehicles. When the Divine Guru is in Sagittarius, the intellect becomes very beautiful, and there is an acquisition of lovely ornaments.** || 57 ||

If Jupiter is situated in the sign of Sagittarius, the person is charitable, endowed with many splendors and vehicles, possesses a beautiful intellect, and is adorned with fine jewelry. || 57 ||

### The Results of Jupiter in Capricorn—

> **The man is of ruined intellect, a servant to others, devoid of desire, and possesses much anger. When the Guru of the Gods is in Capricorn, he does not win the hearts of people, nor does he achieve his goals.** || 58 ||

If Jupiter is situated in the sign of Capricorn, the person has a wicked intellect, performs the work of others, is devoid of passion, is excessively angry, and is lacking in the fulfillment of his desires. || 58 ||

### The Results of Jupiter in Aquarius—

> **Afflicted by disease, of wicked mind, abandoned by wealth, devoted to stinginess, and a committer of sins. When the Priest of the Gods is in the Water-pot <note>Aquarius</note>, he eats bad food and suffers from pains in the teeth and stomach.** || 59 ||

If Jupiter is situated in the sign of Aquarius, the person is diseased, of wicked intellect, poor, miserly, sinful, a consumer of base food, and suffers from ailments of the teeth and stomach. || 56 || <note>The number 56 here is a misprint in the original text; contextually it should be 59.</note>

### The Results of Jupiter in Pisces—

The man possesses wealth through his own side <note>or through partiality/inheritance</note>, has an increase in passion, and is devoted to providing housing and giving charity.

### Results of Venus in Aries—

If Venus is in the sign of Cancer, the subject performs excellent deeds, is virtuous, and brings people under his influence through his sweet speech. || 64 ||

### The Results of Venus in Leo—

When the priest of the demons <note>original: "suravairapurohite" – a title for Venus/Shukra, who in mythology is the preceptor of the Asuras</note> is situated in the sign of the Lion <note>Leo</note>, a person gains wealth, honor, and happiness through women. However, such a man may also experience distress regarding his own kin and might find himself favoring his enemies over his own people. || 65 ||

If Venus is seated in the sign of Leo, the native <term>native: the person whose birth chart is being read</term> obtains wealth, respect, and pleasure through women, but acts to the detriment of his own relatives while benefiting his foes. || 65 ||

### The Results of Venus in Virgo—

When the son of Bhrigu <note>Venus</note> is associated with the Maiden <note>Virgo</note>, the man becomes very wealthy and possesses a deep desire for visiting holy pilgrimages. He is greatly adorned by the Goddess of Fortune <note>Lakshmi/wealth</note> and is characterized by speech that is measured yet profound. || 66 ||

If Venus is in the sign of Virgo, the native is exceedingly wealthy, a performer of pilgrimages, graced with immeasurable prosperity, and is a man of few words. || 66 ||

### The Results of Venus in Libra—

Endowed with flowers, fine raiment, and diverse types of wealth, such a man is constantly on the move with much coming and going. When the Poet <note>Venus</note> is weighed in the Balance <note>Libra</note> at the time of birth, the person surely becomes a leader among poets. || 67 ||

If Venus is in the sign of Libra, the native possesses flowers, clothes, and various riches; he experiences frequent travels and arrivals of people, and he becomes preeminent among poets. || 67 ||

### The Results of Venus in Scorpio—

A mind bent on conflict and striking others, reproach from the public, and constant physical ailments are certain for men. When the Poet <note>Venus</note> takes refuge in the Scorpion <note>Scorpio</note> at birth, he brings about addictions and ensures that wealth remains scarce. || 68 ||

If Venus is in the sign of Scorpio, the native is one who strikes others in quarrels, is censured by the people, is sickly from birth, possesses vices, and has very little wealth. || 68 ||

### The Results of Venus in Sagittarius—

Celebrations regarding the arrival of women, children, and wealth, as well as a position as a minister and a naturally virtuous disposition, are guaranteed. When the Poet <note>Venus</note> is in the Bow <note>Sagittarius</note> at birth, he grants the native a long-lasting detachment from worldly passions. || 69 ||

If Venus is in the sign of Pisces, the person obtains glory from the king, is humble, attacks their enemies, gains wealth, is charitable, and desires to swim in water. || 72 ||

### Results of Saturn in Aries—

### The Results of Saturn in Pisces—

> *A man who is humble, wealthy in conduct, virtuous, and whose qualities are embraced by all people; though perhaps not skillful in returning favors, when the son of the Sun <note>Saturn</note> resides in the sign of the Fish <note>Pisces</note>, he is endowed with great majesty and wealth.* || 84 ||

If Saturn is situated in the sign of Pisces, the person born is humble, well-behaved, good-natured, loved by everyone, and possessed of great wealth and power. || 84 ||

### On the Increase or Decrease of These Results—

> *If the Lord of the Sign and the Sign itself are both powerful, or if the planet is strong, the results of that Sign are realized in full. One must determine the increase or decrease of these effects based on whether the Lord of the Sign is in its debilitation, exaltation, home, or combust state.* || 85 ||

If both the zodiac sign and its ruling planet are strong, they provide the stated results in their entirety. However, if the Lord of the Sign is in a state of debilitation <term>Neecha: the point where a planet is weakest</term>, exaltation <term>Uccha: the point where a planet is strongest</term>, its own house, or is combust <term>Astamaya: rendered invisible/weak by proximity to the Sun</term>, one should calculate the results as being more or less than the standard. || 85 ||

### The Saturn-Cycle is Drawn to Discern Good and Evil Fortune—

> *One should draw a diagram in the shape of a human figure; this is called the Saturn-Cycle (Shani-Chakra). From this, the good and evil fortunes of men are to be known.* || 1 ||
> *First, identifying the "Son of the Friend" <note>A poetic reference to Saturn</note>, and starting from the birth constellation, one should place the lunar mansions upon this human-shaped diagram and declare the results.* || 2 ||

By drawing a human-shaped diagram, one should ascertain the auspicious and inauspicious fortunes of the subject; this is known as the *Shani-Chakra*. In this Saturn-Cycle, starting from the birth constellation <term>Nakshatra: the lunar mansion the moon was in at birth</term>, all subsequent constellations should be arranged according to the method described in the following verses. One must understand the results based on which part of the body the constellation currently occupied by Saturn falls upon. || 1-2 ||

### The Arrangement of Constellations in the Human-Shaped Saturn-Cycle—

> *Place one constellation in the region of the head, three in the mouth, and four in the private parts. <insert>^In the eyes</insert> place two, a pair of constellations in the heart, five in the left hand, and four [in the right].* || 3 ||

-># Results from the Chart<-

Three stars are placed on the left foot, and three stars are placed on the right foot.
Four stars are placed in the right hand; this has been taught by the Sage Narada. || 4 ||

Starting from the <term>Janma Nakshatra</term> <note>The birth star or the lunar mansion the moon was in at the time of birth</note>, one should place 1 star on the head, 3 stars on the mouth, 2 stars on the genitals, 2 stars on the eyes, 5 stars on the heart, 4 stars on the left hand, 3 stars on the left foot, 3 stars on the right foot, and 4 stars on the right hand. This is what the Sage Narada has stated. || 3-4 ||

### Results of Saturn's Position by Sequential Placement of Stars—

> Disease, gain, loss, acquisition, happiness, imprisonment, pain, travel, and gain.
> These are to be considered in the Saturn Chart when the planet is moving normally; if the planet is in rapid motion, the results are reversed. || 5 ||

In the human-shaped Saturn Chart <note>A diagram where the stars are mapped onto a human figure to predict physical and life effects</note>, if Saturn's star falls on the head, it causes disease; if in the mouth, gain; if on the genitals, loss; if in the eyes, gain of wealth; if in the heart, happiness; if in the left hand, imprisonment or bondage; if in the left foot, pain; if in the right foot, travel; and if in the right hand, it brings gain. || 5 ||

### Example—

For instance, if someone's <term>Birth Star</term> <note>Janma Nakshatra</note> is <term>Uttarabhadra</term> and Saturn's current star is <term>Vishakha</term>, then counting from the birth star Uttarabhadra to Vishakha gives the number 18. In the Saturn Chart, the 18th star falls on the left foot; therefore, according to the rule "Disease, loss, etc.," this person should specifically experience pain in their life during this period.

### The Sarvatobhadra Chart—

> Now, I shall describe the chart that illuminates the three worlds.
> Known as the <term>Sarvatobhadra</term> <note>Literally "Good from all sides" or "All-auspicious"</note>, it provides immediate conviction and proof. || 1 ||

Following this, the chart named <term>Sarvatobhadra</term> is described, which illuminates the three worlds and produces quick results for the believer. || 1 ||

### Describing the Construction of the Chart—

A wise person should create a chart with nine squares running North-to-South and East-to-West.

### Now, the results of the "piercing" by malefic planets are described—

> Confusion arises from the piercing of a letter; loss from the piercing of a name-syllable; disease from a vowel; and fear is said to come from the lunar day. When the zodiac sign is pierced, obstacles occur. How can a creature survive when all five are pierced? || 3 ||

If there is a "piercing" <term>Vedha: an astrological "hit" or aspect where a planet aligns with a specific point in the grid</term> by a malefic planet <note>such as Saturn or Mars</note> on the birth constellation, there is confusion; if the piercing is on the letter of the name, there is loss; if on the vowel, there is disease; if on the lunar day, there is fear; and if on the zodiac sign, there are obstacles. ||

# Results from the Chart

If the five components—beginning with the birth star—are all pierced by malefic planets, how can that person survive? || 3 ||

->The method of piercing is explained as follows:<-

> A planet situated in the Krittika star pierces Bharani, the letter 'A', Taurus, the Nanda and Bhadra lunar days, the letter 'Ta', Shravana, Vishakha, and Libra. This is the chart described by those who know the secrets of sounds. || 4 ||
> A celestial wanderer <note>original: "nabhashcharendra," referring to a planet</note> situated in the Rohini star pierces the letters 'Cha', 'Au', 'U', and 'Re', the stars Ashwini, Swati, and Abhijit, as well as the zodiac signs of Gemini and Virgo. || 5 ||
> A planet located in Mrigashira pierces Cancer, the letter 'Ka', Leo, the letter 'Pa', the stars Chitra and Revati, the letter 'La', the letter 'A', and the star Uttarashadha. || 6 ||
> In this manner, the wise should contemplate the piercing in the Sarvatobhadra Chakra for all stars. Piercing by a benefic planet yields good results, while piercing by a malefic planet causes extreme suffering. || 7 ||
> When a malefic planet, acting as the piercer, moves from the star it currently occupies to another star, the wise say that the suffering of the afflicted ends at that time; it is never otherwise. || 8 ||

In this chart, the <term>Vedha</term> <note>literally "piercing" or "obstruction"; an astrological aspect where one planet influences a specific point in the grid</note> occurs diagonally and directly in front. Therefore, if a planet is situated in the <term>Krittika</term> <note>the 3rd Nakshatra or lunar mansion</note> star, it pierces the <term>Bharani</term> star, the letter **A**, the zodiac sign of **Taurus**, the <term>Nanda</term> and <term>Bhadra</term> <note>specific groups of lunar days or Tithis</note> dates, the letter **Ta**, and the stars **Shravana** and **Vishakha**, as well as the sign of **Libra**.

A planet situated in the <term>Rohini</term> star pierces the letters **Cha**, **Au**, **U**, and **Re**, the stars **Ashwini**, **Swati**, and **Abhijit**, and the signs of **Gemini** and **Virgo**.

If a planet is in <term>Mrigashira</term>, it pierces the sign of **Cancer**, the letter **Ka**, the sign of **Leo**, the letter **Pa**, the stars **Chitra** and **Revati**, the letter **La**, the letter **A**, and the star **Uttarashadha**. In this way, one should consider the piercing for all stars in the <term>Sarvatobhadra Chakra</term> <note>literally "The Chart Auspicious on All Sides"; a 9x9 square grid used in Vedic astrology</note>. If the piercing is by benefic planets, it gives auspicious results, and if by malefic planets, it gives inauspicious results. || 4-7 ||

**Example—** Here, the <term>Birth Star</term> <note>Janma Nakshatra</note> is **Uttara Bhadrapada**, the date is the **Third Lunar Day** (Tritiya), the zodiac sign is **Pisces**, the name-letter is **Da**, and the vowel is **U**.

Furthermore, the Sun is in *Dhanishtha* <note>The 23rd lunar mansion</note>, the Moon is in *Uttarabhadra*, Mars is in *Moola*, Mercury is in *Uttarabhadra*, Jupiter is in *Shravana*, Venus is in *Uttarashadha*, and Saturn is in *Vishakha*.

From the constellation *Uttarabhadra*, Saturn creates a *Vedha* on the constellation *Hasta*, the sounds 'Sa', 'Ai', and 'Ja', the constellation *Purvashadha*, the sounds 'Cha', 'Lu', and 'Dha', and the constellation *Ardra*. In this same manner, one should determine the results by considering the *Vedha* from the Sun and other planets.

However, when that malefic planet leaves the "pierced" constellation and moves into another constellation through its transit <note>original: "Gochar"</note>, it destroys the person's suffering and brings well-being. ||8||

### The Sun-Kalanal Chakra

> I shall now clearly explain the wonderful Sun-Kalanal Chakra <note>The "Sun-Fire of Time" wheel</note> as described in the Science of Phonetic Astrology <note>original: "Swar Shastra"</note>. ||1||
> One should imagine three straight vertical lines with trident-shaped tops. Three lines should be placed in the middle, and two lines each should be drawn over the corners. ||2||
> Another line should be placed between the corners of the trident, with two horns at its tips. Starting from the base of the trident's staff, the constellations should be placed toward the right, starting from the constellation occupied by the Sun and including *Abhijit*. ||3||

I will now describe in detail the miraculous Sun-Kalanal Chakra mentioned in the Science of Phonetic Astrology. First, draw three straight vertical lines and make the shape of a trident <note>original: "Trishul"</note> at their tops. Then, draw three horizontal lines in the middle section. Next, draw two lines from one corner to the opposite corner. Then, between the trident and the corner, draw two horns at the tip of a line. In this way, the Sun-Kalanal Chakra is constructed.

### The Twelvefold Results of the Sun’s Transit—

> Travel, fear, wealth, and distress, then poverty, destruction of enemies, journeys, and extreme pain;
> Loss of luster, attainment of desired goals, gain, and expenditure—these are the results of the Sun in order. || 2 ||

If the Sun is situated in the birth sign <note>The first house from the Moon</note>, there is travel; in the second, fear; in the third, Lakshmi <note>Wealth and prosperity</note>; in the fourth, sorrow; in the fifth, poverty; in the sixth, destruction of enemies; in the seventh, travel; in the eighth, extreme pain; in the ninth, loss of luster <note>Loss of reputation or physical vitality</note>; in the tenth, attainment of desired goals; in the eleventh, gain; and if in the twelfth, there is expenditure. || 2 ||

### The Twelvefold Results of the Moon’s Transit—

> Good food, loss of wealth, gain of wealth, and stomach ailments; failure in work, then gain;
> Wealth, disease, fear of the King, happiness, gain, and grief—these are caused by the Moon. || 3 ||

If the Moon is situated in the birth sign, there is excellent food; in the second, loss of wealth; in the third, gain of wealth; in the fourth, stomach pain; in the fifth, failure in work; in the sixth, gain; in the seventh, wealth; in the eighth, disease; in the ninth, fear of the King <note>Trouble with authorities or the state</note>; in the tenth, happiness; in the eleventh, gain; and if in the twelfth, there is grief. || 3 ||

> The Moon in the houses of children, religion, and wealth is said to give bad results;
> This should be understood for the waning Moon; for the waxing Moon, it is auspicious. || 4 ||

The inauspicious results mentioned for the Moon in the second, fifth, and ninth houses should only be understood for the Moon during the dark fortnight <note>original: "Krishna Paksha"</note>; for the Moon of the bright fortnight <note>original: "Shukla Paksha"</note>, the results are indeed auspicious. || 4 ||

### The Results of Mars’ Transit—

> Fear, injury, wealth, and increase of enemies; loss of money, wealth, and destruction of assets;
> Injury by weapons, sickness, disease, gain, and expenditure—these are spread by the Son of the Earth. <note>original: "Bhutanaya," a name for Mars</note> || 5 ||

### Regarding the Special Characteristics of the Ashtakavarga in Transit—

> The results of the planets in each sign during transit from the birth sign were spoken of by the ancients.
> Yet, for mortals born under the same sign, these results are certainly seen to be different for each individual. || 11 ||

The results described by ancient teachers for each sign based on the transit of planets from the birth sign <term>Janma Rashi: the zodiac sign of the Moon at birth</term> are observed to vary even among different people who share the same birth sign.

### Explaining the Reason for Differences in Results—

> The sign in which the "Cool-Rayed One" <note>original: "Sheetarashmi" (the Moon)</note> is placed at birth
> Is declared to be the birth sign.
> In the same way, the seven planets along with the Ascendant—
> Why should these not also be the "birth signs" for living beings? || 12 ||

> Therefore, for men, there are indeed eight such signs; from these come auspicious and inauspicious results.
> Thus, from the interval found by combining the "lines," the clear result is obtained through the Ashtakavarga system. || 13 ||

The sign in which the Moon is situated at the time of birth is called the "Birth Sign" <note>Janma Rashi</note>. In the same way, why should the signs occupied by the seven planets and the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note> not also be considered birth signs? Therefore, a person has eight "birth signs." Having understood the auspicious and inauspicious results from them, one marks a "line" <term>Rekha: a symbolic mark for a positive point</term> in auspicious places and a "dot" <term>Bindu: a symbolic mark for a negative point</term> in inauspicious places. By calculating the difference between these two—

<vocab>Jatakabharana (a classical astrological treatise), Gochara (planetary transits), Rahu (the North Node), Ketu (the South Node), Ashtakavarga (a system of points based on eight reference points), Janma Rashi (Moon sign), Rekha (auspicious point/line), Bindu (inauspicious point/dot), Sheetarashmi (the Moon), Kheta (planet)</vocab>

->The Ashtakavarga System<-

One should understand the results as either auspicious or inauspicious. That is to say, after performing the subtraction, if a "Rekha" <note>original: रेखा; a vertical mark representing a positive point</note> remains, the result is auspicious; if a "Bindu" <note>original: बिन्दु; a dot representing a negative point</note> remains, the result is inauspicious. In this way, the results of planetary transits <term>Gochar: the movement of planets through the zodiac relative to one's birth chart</term> combined with the Ashtakavarga system will differ even for individuals born under the same zodiac sign. || 12-13 ||

### The Ashtakavarga of the Sun

> From its own position, Saturn, and Mars, the Sun is auspicious in the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th, 9th, 10th, and 11th houses. From Venus in the 6th, 7th, and 12th; from Jupiter in the 5th, 6th, 9th, and 11th; from the Moon in the 3rd, 6th, 10th, and 11th; from Mercury in the 3rd, 5th, 6th, 9th, 10th, 11th, and 12th; and from the Ascendant in the 3rd, 4th, 6th, 10th, 11th, and 12th houses. || 14 ||

The Sun gives auspicious results in the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th, 9th, 10th, and 11th positions from its own natal position, Saturn, and Mars. From Venus, the 6th, 7th, and 12th; from Jupiter, the 5th, 6th, 9th, and 11th; from the Moon, the 3rd, 6th, 10th, and 11th; from Mercury, the 3rd, 5th, 6th, 9th, 10th, 11th, and 12th; and from the Ascendant <note>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note>, the 3rd, 4th, 6th, 11th, and 12th positions. || 14 ||

<header>In the Jatakabharanam—</header>

By marking the positions with dots and calculating the difference between the two, the planet yields its results when it passes through that remaining position during its transit <note>transits are known as Gochara, the movement of planets through the zodiac relative to one's birth chart</note>. || 21 ||

### On the Number of Auspicious Points (Rekhas)—

> The values are represented by the following mnemonic terms: Serpent-Vedas (48), Nine-Oceans (49), Nine-Fires (39), Ocean-Arrows (54), Flavor-Arrows (56), Pair-Arrows (52), and Nine-Three-Equals (39). These are the Rekhas for the Ashtakavarga in sequence. || 22 ||
<note>original: "भुजङ्गवेदा नवसागराश्च..." This Sanskrit verse uses a system called Katapayadi or symbolic words where 'Vedas' equals 4 and 'Serpents' equals 8, totaling 48.</note>

In the <term>Ashtakavarga</term> <note>a system of "eight-fold classification" used to predict the strength of planetary transits</note> of the Sun, there are a total of 48 points (Rekhas); in the Moon 49; in Mars 39; in Mercury 54; in Jupiter 56; in Venus 52; and in Saturn there are 39 points. || 22 ||

### Description of the Ascendant's (Lagna) Ashtakavarga—

> In whatever signs the points occur based on the sign occupied by the Lord of the Ascendant, the wise should establish those points in the corresponding signs starting from the Ascendant itself. || 23 ||

Just as a planet is auspicious in a certain sign relative to another planet, the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note> is also auspicious in that same position relative to the Lord of the Ascendant. Therefore, learned scholars should construct the Ashtakavarga of the Ascendant in the same manner as they do for the Lord of the Ascendant. || 23 ||

### On the Results of Points from One Onward—

> Distress, loss of wealth, addiction, neutrality, constant happiness, daily arrival of wealth, increase in prosperity, and vast, pure fortune—these are the declared results for each point respectively. || 24 ||

When a planet transits through a sign containing 1 point, it causes distress; 2 points cause loss of wealth; 3 points cause addiction or vice; 4 points result in a neutral or balanced state; 5 points bring constant happiness; 6 points bring the daily acquisition of wealth; 7 points lead to an increase in prosperity; and 8 points result in great fortune and wealth. || 24 ||

> Thus are the results declared for the points of a single planet. By totaling the points of all planets in all signs, which should sum to twenty-eight on average, one should judge the good or bad results based on whether the total is higher or lower. || 25 ||

This describes the results based on the points of a single planet. Similarly, one should understand the results by totaling the points located in each sign for every planet.

If the sum of points is 28, the result is middling. For every 2 points above or below 28, the auspicious or inauspicious results should be understood proportionately. || 25 ||

# Page 227
## Chapter on the Conjunction of Two Planets

->He explains who gives results and when:<-

Mars and the Sun <note>original: "Ilatanuja" (Mars) and "Patinalininya" (Sun)</note> are said to give their results at the very moment they enter a new zodiac sign. Venus and Jupiter <note>original: "Bhruguja" and "Amarejya"</note> give results when they have traversed half of the sign. Saturn and the Moon give results at the end of the sign, while Mercury <note>original: "Indusunu"</note> gives results throughout the entire duration. || 26 ||

**Mars and the Sun give results as soon as they enter a sign. Jupiter and Venus give results in the middle of the sign, while Saturn and the Moon give results at the end of the sign.** || 26 ||

->Now he describes the affliction of planets according to the divisions of the body:<-

The Sun <note>original: "Dinesha"</note> governs the head and the face; the Moon <note>original: "Kalavan"</note> governs the chest and the throat. Mars <note>original: "Bhutanaya"</note> affects the back and the stomach, while Mercury <note>original: "Saumya"</note> spreads his influence over the feet and the hands. || 27 ||
Jupiter <note>original: "Jiva"</note> governs the waist and the hips; Venus <note>original: "Kavi"</note> governs the private parts and the scrotum. Saturn <note>original: "Nalinishasunu"</note> governs the knees and thighs. These should be considered during their transit or at the time of birth. || 28 ||

**The Sun gives inauspicious results in the head and mouth. The Moon in the chest and throat; Mars in the back and stomach; Mercury in the feet and hands; Jupiter in the waist and thighs; Venus in the anus and scrotum; and Saturn gives inauspicious results in the knees.** || 27-28 ||

Whenever a planet is unfavorable <note>term: "Pratikulavarti" - moving in opposition or acting as a malefic</note>, it causes pain or suffering in its respective limb. Having first considered all of this, one should apply these findings to horary questions <note>term: "Prashna" - the branch of astrology dealing with questions asked at a specific moment</note> or birth charts. || 29 ||

**Whenever planets are unfavorable, they cause pain in their respective assigned limbs. One should form conclusions after considering these factors in the time of a query or at birth.** || 29 ||

->Thus ends the Ashtakavarga <note>term: "Ashtakavarga" - a system of points used to predict the strength of planetary transits</note>.<-

### Now begins the Chapter on Royal Yogas

->Invocation (Mangalacharana)<-

May the Auspicious Form <note>The elephant-headed deity Ganesha</note>, who delights in beautiful play and possesses a sweet, resonant voice, who constantly curves his trunk into a circle, and who bears the crescent moon upon his forehead, truly grant you auspiciousness. || 1 ||

> May Lord Ganesha—who makes sweet sounds in beautiful play, who always makes his trunk into a ring, who has the moon shining on his forehead, and who is the embodiment of auspiciousness—be for your welfare. || 1 ||

->The reason for describing Royal Yogas:<-

Whatever fortune is indicated by the <term>House of Fortune (Bhagya-bhava)</term> and other houses is truly realized through Royal Yogas. I shall describe them thoroughly and in detail, for it is through them that the births of men become meaningful. || 2 ||

> The fortunes described through the House of Fortune and other houses are attained in conjunction with Royal Yogas. Therefore, I speak of those Royal Yogas by which the lives of men are made purposeful. || 2 ||

->The Royal Yogas:<-

If five planets are situated in their signs of <term>exaltation (ucca)</term> at the time of birth, that person becomes a universal emperor. If three planets are in their exaltation, he is a king; if he is a king's son, he becomes a ruler, while the son of any other person becomes a minister. || 3 ||

> The subject in whose birth chart five planets are exalted becomes a <term>Chakravarti (universal emperor)</term>. Even if only three planets are exalted, that man becomes a king.

# Chapter on Royal Yogas

<page-num>245</page-num>
->**Chapter on Royal Yogas**<-

If the Moon, being the lord of the sky <note>original: "nabhashcharendra," referring to the Moon as the chief of the luminaries</note>, is in its sign of exaltation or its "root-trine" <term>Moolatrikona: a specific favorable position for a planet, stronger than its own sign but less than exaltation</term>, it certainly makes a man a universal monarch. || 17 ||

If at the time of birth, the Moon is purified in the "six-fold division" <term>Shadvarga: a system of six divisional charts used to determine planetary strength</term>, is in the Punarvasu lunar mansion, the sign of Cancer, or in its exaltation or root-trine, the native becomes a universal sovereign. || 17 ||

---

If two planets are purified in the six-fold division and positioned as described before—that is, in their exaltation, their own signs, or their root-trines—at the birth of a king, his lordship extends even over the Kinnaras <note>mythological celestial musicians; here implying vast or divine-like reaches</note> and other islands; what then to speak of his rule over this earth? || 18 ||

If two planets are purified in the six-fold division and are placed as mentioned (in exaltation, own sign, or root-trine), the native becomes a king even of the Kinnara country. What need is there to mention his rule over the mortal world? || 18 ||

---

With three planets purified in the six-fold division, but lacking the status of exaltation or root-trine, one becomes a Minister. With four such planets, one is a King. With five planets, or with Jupiter alone being purified in the six-fold division, one becomes a universal monarch. || 19 ||

If at the time of birth, three planets are purified in the six-fold division but are devoid of their exaltation or root-trine positions, the person becomes a Minister. If four planets are so purified, he is a King. If five planets, or even just Jupiter alone, are purified in the six-fold division, he becomes a universal sovereign. || 19 ||

---

If the Moon is in the Ascendant in the sign of Taurus, and the Sun, Jupiter, and Saturn are respectively in the 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, then during that person's military expeditions, the darkness caused by the rising dust makes it seem as if night has arrived even during the day. || 20 ||

If the Moon is placed in the Ascendant in Taurus, and the Sun, Jupiter, and Saturn are in the 4th, 7th, and 10th houses respectively, then in the native's war marches, the dust clouds are so thick that they create the appearance of night. || 20 ||

---

If Jupiter, the Moon, Mercury, and Venus are placed in the 1st, 3rd, 9th, and 11th houses, and Saturn is in the Ascendant in Capricorn, the native surely enjoys the rule of the entire earth under a single umbrella <note>a symbol of undisputed imperial sovereignty</note>. || 21 ||

If Saturn is in the sign of Capricorn in the Ascendant, and Jupiter, the Moon, Mercury, and Venus are seated in the 1st, 3rd, 9th, and 11th houses respectively, the native becomes a "Chakravarti" <term>Chakravarti: an emperor whose chariot wheels roll everywhere without obstruction; a universal ruler</term>. || 21 ||

---

Venus and Mercury are in their exaltation in the Ascendant, Mars is in Capricorn, and Jupiter and the Moon are in Sagittarius...

# In the Jātaka-bharaṇam—

If Mercury is situated in any sign and is aspected <note>In Vedic astrology, an 'aspect' or 'drishti' is a planetary influence cast from one sign to another.</note> by Jupiter, the person born becomes a king endowed with extraordinary wealth. If any planet is situated in the fifth Navamsha <note>A Navamsha is a 1/9th division of a zodiac sign, used to determine the hidden strength of a planet.</note>, the person becomes a king. || 39 ||

> If the Lord of the Stars <note>original: "Nakshatranatha" - referring to the Moon</note> is in the division of a great friend and is aspected by Venus, it makes one a ruler of men. Or, if the Moon is in its own division or that of a great friend and is aspected by Jupiter, it creates a protector of men. || 40 ||

If the Moon is situated in the Navamsha of a "great friend" <term>Adhimitra: a planetary relationship where two planets are exceptionally compatible</term> and is aspected by Venus, the person becomes a king. If the Moon is in its own or a great friend's Navamsha and is aspected by Jupiter, the person becomes a king. || 40 ||

> If the Lord of the Day <note>original: "Dinadinatha" - referring to the Sun</note> is in the house of a great friend and is fully aspected by the Moon, one becomes a king even among a multitude of thieves, possessing a virtuous character and great generosity. || 41 ||

If the Sun is situated in the house of its great friend and is aspected by both the Sun <note>The Hindi commentary mentions the Sun aspecting itself, though the Sanskrit verse emphasizes the Moon's aspect.</note> and the Moon, the person becomes an exceedingly generous king of beautiful character, even if he resides among thieves. || 41 ||

> The son of the Moon <note>original: "Somasuta" - referring to Mercury</note> situated in its sign of exaltation along with the Moon makes a man the King of the Magadha country. If the Moon is full, powerful, and situated in an auspicious house, it makes one a king. || 42 ||

If Mercury is in the sign of Virgo <note>Mercury's sign of exaltation</note> along with the Moon, the person becomes the King of the Magadha region <note>An ancient kingdom in east-central India, modern-day Bihar</note>. If the Moon is at full strength and placed in an auspicious house, the person becomes a king. || 42 ||

> If the Lord of the Birth Sign or the Lord of the Ascendant is strong and placed in a Center, even one born in a lowly family becomes a king, exceedingly generous and pure; what wonder is there then if the son of a king becomes one? || 43 ||

If at the time of birth, the Lord of the Moon-sign or the Lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</term> is powerful and situated in a Center <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a birth chart</term>, even a man born in a humble family becomes a king. It goes without saying that a prince would become a king under such circumstances. || 43 ||

> He in whose birth the Sun is in Aries joined with the Moon becomes a sovereign who is favored by the kings of the Karnataka, Dravida, Kerala, and Andhra countries. || 44 ||

> If Venus and Jupiter are in their respective signs of exaltation <note>Exaltation refers to the zodiac sign where a planet is at its maximum strength.</note> and are placed in the Angles or Trines <note>Angles (Kendra) are the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses; Trines (Trikona) are the 1st, 5th, and 9th houses.</note>, they make a person born in a royal family a king, and one born in another family a prime minister. || 45 ||

If at the time of birth, all planets are seated in the seventh, second, twelfth, and the ascendant <note>Lagna</note>, then the *Chatra Yoga* (Parasol Combination) occurs. Such a combination arises due to the emergence of merits earned in previous births. || 46 ||

> If a malefic planet is in the ascendant at birth and is aspected by Jupiter <note>original: "Chitrasikhandija," a poetic name for Jupiter</note>, and Jupiter is in Cancer, the man will be a devotee of priests and gods, and a builder of temples, step-wells, and cities. || 47 ||

If at the time of birth, even a single auspicious planet is situated in its exaltation or in an Angle and is aspected by Jupiter located in the fifth house, the person becomes a king. || 48 ||

If Jupiter is situated in the ascendant, having left the sign of Capricorn <note>where it is traditionally weak or "debilitated"</note>, the person born becomes a king possessing a retinue of rutting elephants. || 49 ||

# Chapter on Royal Yogas

If the Moon is at full strength and positioned in the <term>Vargottama Navamsha</term><note>The best division of a sign where a planet occupies the same zodiac sign in both the main chart and the ninth divisional chart, increasing its strength.</note> of the asterisms Pushya, Ashwini, or Krittika, the person born becomes a king. -> If a <term>Bhadra Tithi</term><note>The 2nd, 7th, or 12th lunar days of a fortnight.</note> falls on the first or third quarter of a constellation on the days of Jupiter, Mars, or Saturn, it is declared as the Tripushkara Yoga. It bestows a triple-fold result in both prosperity and loss. || 56 || <-

### Regarding the timing of attaining the kingdom—
The acquisition of a kingdom occurs during the planetary period <term>Dasha: a period of time in which a specific planet's influence dominates a person's life</term> of the planet situated in the tenth house, or the period of the planet in the ascendant <note>the rising sign</note>. In the absence of these, it occurs in the period of the strongest planet, provided there is a powerful Royal Yoga <note>auspicious planetary combination for power</note> at the time of birth. || 67 ||

If there is a strong Royal Yoga at the time of birth, then the gain of a kingdom occurs during the period of the planet in the tenth house, or the period of the planet in the ascendant, or failing these, in the period of the most powerful planet. || 67 ||

## Now begins the Chapter on the Correspondence of Royal Yogas in Palmistry

If powerful Royal Yogas are present for a man at the time of his birth, then clear royal marks will also appear on his feet or on the palms of his hands. || 1 ||

For a person who has powerful Royal Yogas at birth, there are pure royal signs on their hands and feet. || 1 ||

The auspicious line at the base of the ring finger is known as the Line of Merit <note>original: "punya-vidhana-rekha"</note>. The vertical line that goes from the middle finger to the wrist is known as the Upward Line <note>original: "urdhva-rekha"</note>; it provides the support of a kingdom. || 2 ||

There is a Line of Merit at the root of the ring finger, and an Upward Line from the middle finger to the wrist. This line is one that brings about the acquisition of a kingdom. || 2 ||

If a man has a shining barley-shaped mark <note>original: "yava-lāñchanam" - a grain-shaped island on the thumb joint</note> in the middle of his thumb, he will be famous, an ornament to his lineage, endowed with royal distinctions, and humble. || 3 ||

# Chapter on the Cancellation of Royal Yogas

If the Ascendant <note>The zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of birth</note> at birth is Aquarius, the Royal Yoga <term>Rajayoga: combinations indicating power, wealth, and status</term> is destroyed.
If even a single planet is in its sign of debilitation <note>The zodiac sign where a planet is at its weakest</note> and malefic planets are situated in the tenth house, the Royal Yoga is destroyed. || 7 ||

> If at the time of birth, the Minister of the Demons <note>original: "Danavamatya" – a title for the planet Venus</note> is situated in its highest degree of debilitation, it surely causes the downfall of men from great positions. || 8 ||

If Venus is situated in its deepest point of debilitation at the time of birth, the native falls from grace even after attaining a high position. || 8 ||

> If Rahu <note>The North Node of the Moon</note> is situated in the first house and is aspected by the Moon, while the Sun, Saturn, and Mars are located in the third and sixth houses, and the benefics are absent from the angles or are in the seventh house, the Yoga for kingship should be considered useless. || 9 ||

<note>The number ६ (6) in the verse above appears to be a printer's error for ९ (9).</note>

If Rahu, situated in the Ascendant, is aspected by the Moon; and the Sun, Saturn, and Mars are situated in the third, sixth, and eleventh houses respectively; and the benefic planets are either absent from the angles <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</term> or are situated in the seventh house, then the native's Royal Yoga becomes fruitless.

> When the angles are devoid of benefic planets, or when they are combust, or situated in their signs of debilitation, or if four planets are in enemy houses, the Yogas for kingship go to their destruction. || 10 ||

If benefic planets are not in the angles, are combust <note>Too close to the Sun to be seen</note>, are in their signs of debilitation, or if four planets are sitting in enemy signs, the Royal Yoga is destroyed. || 10 ||

> If all the malefic planets are in the angles but are in debilitated or enemy signs and are not joined with or aspected by benefics, and the planets known as benefics are in debilitated, enemy, or the twelfth houses, the Yogas of kings indeed vanish. || 11 ||

If all malefic planets are situated in the angles and are in their debilitated or enemy signs, are not aspected by benefics, and the benefic planets are in debilitated signs, enemy signs, or the twelfth house, then the Royal Yoga is destroyed. || 11 ||

->Thus ends the Chapter on the Cancellation of Royal Yogas.<-

## Now, the Chapter on the Five Great Person Yogas

Those kings known as "Great Persons" <note>Sanskrit: Mahapurusha</note> who were proclaimed by the ancient sages—I shall describe them with great and simple eloquence, desiring to demonstrate the rules of the Royal Yogas <note>Rajayoga: planetary combinations indicating power and status</note>. || 1 ||

> The five Great Person Yogas, which are of the nature of Royal Yogas as propounded by the ancient sages: I speak of them in detail with the desire to show how Royal Yogas are observed. || 1 ||

When Mars and the other four planets are situated in their own signs or in their signs of exaltation, and occupy a quadrant <note>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a birth chart</note>, the yogas formed are, in order: Ruchaka, Bhadra, Hansa, Malavya, and Shasha. || 2 ||

> If the five planets starting with Mars are placed in their own house or in exaltation and are in a quadrant, then the Ruchaka and other yogas occur. That is: Mars creates Ruchaka, Mercury creates Bhadra, Jupiter creates Hansa, Venus creates Malavya, and Saturn creates Shasha yoga. || 2 ||

### The Results of Ruchaka Yoga—

The person will be long-lived, possessing a clear luster and great strength of blood. They achieve success through courage, possessing beautiful eyebrows and black hair. Their hands and feet are well-proportioned, and they are famous for their knowledge of mantras <note>sacred chants or counsels</note>. They have a reddish-dark complexion, are exceedingly brave, and are destroyers of the enemy's strength. They possess a shell-like neck <note>Kambu-kantha: a sign of beauty and auspiciousness</note> and great vigor. Though they may be cruel, they are devoted to the gods, respectful to priests <note>Brahmins</note> and teachers, and have slim knees, thighs, and shanks. || 3 ||

Their hands and feet are marked with the signs of a sword, a noose, a bull, a bow, a discus, a lute, or a thunderbolt. Their fingers are straight. They are skilled in mantras and incantations. They weigh one thousand <note>units of weight</note>, and their waist is said to be equal in circumference to the length of their face. || 4 ||

This person will be the lord of the Sahya and Vindhya mountains and of Ujjain. They live for seventy autumns. Having been pained by weapons or fire, the person of the Ruchaka name meets their end in a temple. || 5 ||

# Chapter on the Combinations of Functional Significators

- If the Ascendant <note>original: "Lagna"; the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at birth</note> is situated in Cancer or Taurus, then the Sun, Saturn, and <insert>4</insert> Jupiter—these three—become mutual functional significators <note>original: "Karaka"; planets that carry the power to produce specific results for the individual</note> for one another. || 1-2 ||

When a benefic planet is in the Ascendant, any planet situated in the tenth or fourth house is designated as a functional significator. If planets are in their sign of exaltation, their root-trine <note>original: "Moolatrikona"; a specific potent area of a zodiac sign</note>, their own sign, or their own divisional sign <note>original: "Navamsha"</note> while occupying the tenth house, they become especially powerful significators. || 2-3 ||

If a benefic planet is in the second house from the Sun, and the birth Ascendant is in its own divisional sign, and all the cardinal houses <note>original: "Kendras"; the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note> are occupied by benefic planets, then the Goddess of Wealth <note>original: "Lakshmi"</note> makes her residence in that person's home. || 4 ||

If Jupiter, the Lord of the Ascendant, and the Lord of the Moon-sign are situated in the cardinal houses, they grant great fortune during the middle of one's life. If they are placed in signs that rise by the head, the rear, or both <note>note: "Shirshodaya," "Prishthodaya," and "Ubhayodaya" signs refer to how the constellations appear to rise over the horizon, indicating the timing of results</note>, they grant their fruits at the beginning, middle, and end of life respectively. || 5 ||

Even if a person is born into a lowly family, they will become a Minister <note>original: "Mantri"</note> if these planetary significators are present. If a person is born into a royal lineage under such conditions, how could they not certainly become a Sovereign King? || 6 ||

# Now begins the Chapter on Celestial Configurations

## Regarding the Rope, Pestle, and Pipe Configurations—

> **If all planets are situated in movable signs, or all in fixed signs, or all in dual signs,**
> **they are called, respectively, Rope, Pestle, and Pipe. These three are known as Dependent Configurations. || 1 ||**

If all planets are in <term>Movable</term> <note>original: "Chara"; signs like Aries or Cancer that represent change</note> signs, it is a <term>Rope</term> <note>original: "Rajju"</note> configuration. If they are in <term>Fixed</term> <note>original: "Sthira"; signs like Taurus or Leo representing stability</note> signs, it is a <term>Pestle</term> <note>original: "Musala"</note> configuration. If they are in <term>Dual</term> <note>original: "Dvisvabhava"; signs like Gemini or Virgo representing flexibility</note> signs, it is a <term>Pipe</term> <note>original: "Nala"</note> configuration. These three are the <term>Dependent Configurations</term> <note>original: "Ashraya Yoga"</note>. || 1 ||

## The Two Configurations: Garland and Serpent—

> **When the three angular houses contain only benefic planets, it is a Garland; if only malefic planets, it is called a Serpent.**
> **These two configurations are known as the "Half" type, as taught by the sage Parashara. || 2 ||**

If there are benefic planets in three of the <term>Angular Houses</term> <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, which are the pillars of a birth chart</note>, it is a <term>Garland</term> <note>original: "Mala"</note> configuration. If there are malefic planets in them, it is a <term>Serpent</term> <note>original: "Vyala"</note> configuration. These two are the <term>Half Configurations</term> <note>original: "Dala Yoga"</note> as described by <term>Parashara</term> <note>the legendary father of Vedic astrology</note>. || 2 ||

## Regarding the Mace, Cart, Bird, and Triangle Configurations—

> **Planets in two adjacent angles form the Mace; in the Ascendant and the Seventh, the Cart;**
> **in the Fourth and Tenth, the Bird; and in the Ascendant, Ninth, and Fifth, the Triangle. || 3 ||**

If all planets are in the 1st and 4th houses (1), the 4th and 7th (2), the 7th and 10th (3), or the 10th and 1st (4), these four are the <term>Mace</term> <note>original: "Gada"</note> configurations. If all planets are in the 1st and 7th houses, it is the <term>Cart</term> <note>original: "Shakata"</note>. If they are in the 4th and 10th, it is the <term>Bird</term> <note>original: "Vihaga"</note>. If they are in the 1st, 9th, and 5th, it is the <term>Triangle</term> <note>original: "Shringataka"</note> configuration. || 3 ||

## The Plow Configuration—

> **When planets are placed in the 2nd, 6th, and 10th; or the 3rd, 7th, and 11th; or the 4th, 8th, and 12th;**
> **this is called the Plow configuration by those learned in all the scriptures. || 4 ||**

If all planets are situated in the 2nd, 6th, and 10th houses; or the 3rd, 7th, and 11th; or the 4th, 8th, and 12th, there are three types of the <term>Plow</term> <note>original: "Hala"</note> configuration. || 4 ||

## Regarding the Thunderbolt, Barley, and Lotus Configurations—

**When benefics are in the Ascendant and the 7th, and malefics are in the 10th and 4th...**

<meta>This page continues the discussion of Nabhasa Yogas (celestial configurations) from the previous section, specifically focusing on the geometric patterns formed by planets in the angular houses.</meta>

<page-num>267</page-num>
-># Chapter on Nabhasa Yogas<-

The configuration known as **Vajra** (Thunderbolt) is formed by the opposite placement of planets; **Yava** (Barley-corn) is its reverse; and the mixture of these results in the **Kamala** (Lotus) yoga. || 5 ||

If benefic planets <note>planets with a positive influence, such as Jupiter or Venus</note> are in the Ascendant <note>1st house</note> and the 7th house, while malefic planets <note>planets with a challenging influence, such as Mars or Saturn</note> are in the 4th and 10th houses, it is **Vajra Yoga**. If malefic planets are in the Ascendant and 7th house while benefics are in the 4th and 10th, it is **Yava Yoga**. If all planets, both benefic and malefic, are distributed across all four centers <note>the 'Kendra' or angular houses: 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th</note>, it is **Kamala Yoga**. || 5 ||

How can Mercury and Venus be in the fourth house from the Sun? This is not possible. Regarding the names Yava and Vajra, I shall now demonstrate the reasoning behind this. || 6 ||

In the previously mentioned Vajra and Yava yogas, it is impossible for Mercury and Venus (benefics) to be in the fourth house from the Sun (a malefic). This is because their mean motions are equal, and their actual positions never differ by more than one sign <note>Mercury and Venus always stay close to the Sun from the perspective of Earth</note>. I will now explain the logic for this. || 6 ||

If any two among Mercury, Venus, and Jupiter are in the two sides of the Ascendant <note>the 2nd and 12th houses</note> and the remaining one is in the Ascendant itself, while Mars is in the 10th, Saturn in the 4th, and the Moon in the 7th, it is called **Vajra**. The reverse of this is called **Yava**. || 7 ||

If the Nabhasa yogas are formed by all the planets, how can the **Vyala** (Serpent) and **Mala** (Garland) yogas be formed by only three planets? One might wonder about this, but the teachings of the Sages are correct and cannot be otherwise. || 8 ||

### Vapi Yoga (The Well Configuration)

If all planets are situated in the remaining houses, excluding the centers <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses</note>, then according to the ancient teachers, **Vapi Yoga** is formed. || 9 ||

### Regarding the Yūpa, Shara, Shakti, and Daṇḍa Yogas—

If all the lordly planets are situated in the four houses starting from the Ascendant, the fourth house, the seventh house, and the tenth house respectively, those who know the science of birth-charts declare these to be the <term>Yūpa</term><note>Sacrificial Pillar</note>, <term>Shara</term><note>Arrow</note>, <term>Shakti</term><note>Spear or Power</note>, and <term>Daṇḍa</term><note>Staff</note> combinations. || 10 ||

If all planets are placed from the Ascendant to the fourth house, it is Yūpa; if from the fourth to the seventh, it is Shara; if from the seventh to the tenth, it is Shakti; and if from the tenth to the Ascendant, it is the Daṇḍa yoga. || 10 ||

### Regarding the Nau, Kūṭa, Chatra, Dhanu, and Ardhachandra Yogas—

If the seven planets occupy the seven houses starting from the Ascendant, the fourth, the seventh, or the tenth, they are known as <term>Nau</term><note>Boat</note>, <term>Kūṭa</term><note>Mountain Peak or Trap</note>, <term>Chatra</term><note>Umbrella</note>, and <term>Dhanu</term><note>Bow</note>. When these seven-house sequences begin from houses other than these four centers, they are called <term>Ardhachandra</term><note>Half-moon</note> yogas. || 11 ||

If one planet is situated in each of the seven houses from the Ascendant to the seventh house, it is Nau yoga. If the seven planets are in the seven houses from the fourth to the tenth, it is Kūṭa yoga. If the seven planets are in the seven houses from the seventh to the Ascendant, it is Chatra yoga. If the seven planets are in the seven houses from the tenth to the fourth, it is Dhanu yoga. If the seven planets occupy seven consecutive houses starting from any house other than these four (the angles), then eight types of Ardhachandra yoga are formed. || 11 ||

### Regarding the Chakra and Samudra Yogas—

When the lordly planets occupy six houses starting from the Ascendant or the second house, skipping every other house, they are called <term>Chakra</term><note>Wheel</note> and <term>Samudra</term><note>Ocean</note>. Thus, there are twenty such "Shape-based" combinations. || 12 ||

If the seven planets including the Sun are placed in six houses starting from the Ascendant, skipping one house in between (i.e., in houses 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, and 11), it is Chakra yoga. If the seven planets are in the six houses starting from the second house, skipping one house in between (i.e., in houses 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12), it is Samudra yoga. In this manner, there are 20 <term>Ākṛti Yogas</term><note>Combinations based on the geometric shape formed by planets in the chart</note>. || 12 ||

### Regarding the Seven Yogas starting with Gola—

When the many combinations mentioned previously are absent, <term>Gola</term><note>Sphere</note> occurs if all planets are in one house; <term>Yuga</term><note>Yoke/Pair</note> if in two houses; and <term>Shūla</term><note>Trident</note> if they occupy three houses.

<summary>This page defines various 'Shape Yogas' in Vedic astrology, explaining how the placement of planets in specific house sequences creates symbolic patterns like the Boat, Bow, or Wheel. It concludes by introducing the 'Sankhya Yogas' which are based on the total number of houses occupied by planets.</summary>

# Chapter on Nabhasa Yogas

> If all the planets are situated in four signs, it is Kedara; if in five, it is Pasha; if in six, it is Daminika; and if all seven planets are in seven signs, it is Veena. These are the Numerical Yogas. || 13 ||

In the absence of the previously mentioned yogas <note>referring to the primary configurations like Gola or Shula</note>, if all planets are situated in a single house, it is Gola yoga; if in two houses, Yuga yoga; if in three houses, Shula yoga; if in four houses, Kedara yoga; if in five houses, Pasha yoga; if in six houses, Daminika yoga; and if all seven planets are distributed across seven houses, it is Veena yoga. In this manner, there are seven types of [Numerical] yogas. || 13 ||

> The various types of yogas proclaimed by the great masters of time <note>astrologers/sages</note> yield their fruits during the planetary periods and sub-periods of the planets forming them; these results should be considered according to the relative strength of those planets. || 14 ||

The results of the aforementioned yogas propounded by the great sages who knew the movements of time should be judged according to the strength and intensity of the planets during their respective <term>Dasha</term> <note>major planetary period</note> and <term>Antardasha</term> <note>sub-period</note>. || 14 ||

### Results of Rajju Yoga—

> Those born in Rajju Yoga are endowed with a trembling or unstable beauty, are prone to cruelty, and are exceedingly enthusiastic in performing harsh deeds. They wander through their own country and others in pursuit of wealth. || 15 ||

A person born in Rajju Yoga <note>formed when all planets are in moveable signs</note> is very handsome, yet miserable, highly enthusiastic in wicked deeds, and travels through his own land and foreign lands for the sake of acquiring wealth. || 15 ||

### Results of Musala Yoga—

> Endowed with various honors, knowledge, and grain, such a person shines with sons and wealth, possessing the splendor of a king. Attached to a protector of the earth <note>a king</note>, he remains joyful and attains great heights of wealth through his exuberant happiness. || 16 ||

A person born in Musala Yoga <note>formed when all planets are in fixed signs</note> is possessed of great honor, knowledge, wealth in grain, sons, and prosperity. He is as powerful as a king, lives under the patronage of a king, is full of joy, and attains wealth through the height of his excellence and happiness. || 16 ||

### Results of Nala Yoga—

> Their homes are constantly filled with various gems; they enjoy the affection of kings and possess meritorious bodies.

### Results of the Mala Yoga—

Those men at whose birth the Mala Yoga <note>original: "Mala Yoga" - literally "Garland," where auspicious planets occupy three specific houses</note> occurs are endowed with sons, friends, excellent ornaments, and various vehicles; they are inclined toward the pleasure of wearing garlands, swinging on swings, and enjoying the company of women. ||18||

A person born in the Sarpa Yoga eats the food of others, has a terrifying appearance, is poor, sleeps excessively, is prone to anger, has an unlucky form, and possesses a useless ego directed toward harming others. ||19||

### Results of the Gada Yoga—

Devoted to various scriptures and many mantras, skilled in singing and instrumental music, and a performer of sacrifices; though fierce and hateful, they are free from enemies and endowed with women and ornaments in the Gada Yoga <note>original: "Gada Yoga" - literally "Mace," where planets occupy two adjacent corner houses</note>. ||20||

A person born in the Gada Yoga is dedicated to various sciences and the study of sacred chants, is an expert in music and instruments, performs religious sacrifices, has a fierce appearance, is prone to hatred yet remains free of enemies, and is blessed with the company of women and fine jewelry. ||20||

### Results of the Shakata Yoga—

Miserable, devoid of grandeur, wealth, and friends, and necessarily possessing a lean body; such a person finds joy only after obtaining and then abandoning a wicked woman if their birth occurs in the Shakata Yoga <note>original: "Shakata Yoga" - literally "Wagon," where planets are placed in the 1st and 7th houses</note>. ||21||

A person born in the Shakata Yoga is wretched, lacking in splendor, money, and friends, and has a thin physique; they find happiness only after leaving a bad wife whom they had previously acquired. ||21||

## The Results of Vihanga Yoga—

> For those humans in whose birth the Vihanga <note>Bird</note> Yoga occurs, there is no happiness derived from worldly enjoyments. They possess a constant love for travel and wandering, always residing in foreign lands; they possess little wealth but speak as if they have much. || 22 ||

A person born in the Vihanga Yoga is devoid of the pleasures of consumption, a lover of wandering, always living abroad, and despite having few possessions, is a great boaster. || 22 ||

> One becomes a person of sustained excellence, courageous, desiring battle, endowed with happiness, and possessing extreme intelligence. A person born in the Shringataka Yoga is repeatedly energetic, brave, desirous of war, endowed with happiness, highly intelligent, and maintains affection for the first wife while harboring malice toward the second. || 23 ||

## The Results of the Configuration Named Hala—

> One becomes a servant, associated with virtuous people and friends, earning a living through agriculture, yet miserable and a glutton. He who is born in the configuration called Langala <note>Plough</note> suffers greatly due to extreme poverty. || 24 ||

A person born in the Hala <note>Plough</note> Yoga performs the work of a messenger, is surrounded by gentlemen and friends, lives by farming, is sorrowful, eats excessively, and suffers intense distress due to a lack of wealth. || 24 ||

A person born in the Vajra Yoga is happy and fortunate during childhood and old age. However, during the middle stage of life, they are possessed by desire and anger and are devoid of good fortune. || 25 ||

### The Results of Yava Yoga—

### The Results of Shara Yoga—

<note>Shara Yoga (Arrow configuration) occurs when planets occupy the 4th, 5th, 6th, and 7th houses.</note> A person born in the Shara Yoga is very cruel, <unclear>tormented</unclear> by the sorrows of labor, finds happiness in forest regions, is skilled with arrows, and from the start of their life, they do not experience happiness. || 30 ||
