# From the Jatakabharanam—

### The Result of Birth in the Parasol Configuration (Chatra Yoga)—

> The person in whose birth the Parasol configuration is found is wise, an agent of royal affairs, compassionate, and endowed with all comforts in both the early and later stages of life. He attains the honors of the parasol and the fly-whisk <note>The 'Chatra' (parasol) and 'Chamara' (fly-whisk) are traditional Indian symbols of royalty and high status</note>. || 35 ||

A person born in the Parasol Yoga is clever, performs state duties, is kind-hearted, possesses all happiness in childhood and old age, and acquires symbols of authority such as the royal parasol and fly-whisk. || 35 ||

### The Result of Birth in the Bow Configuration (Karmuka Yoga)—

> Endowed with happiness in the first and final parts of life, a wanderer of forests and such places; one born in the Bow Yoga is extremely proud, falls into trouble due to his arrogance, and is skilled with the bow and weapons. || 36 ||

A person born in the Bow Yoga <note>original: "Karmuka"</note> is blessed with happiness in childhood and old age, travels through forests and mountains, is very proud, finds himself in difficulties because of his ego, and is an archer. || 36 ||

### The Result of Birth in the Half-Moon Configuration (Ardhachandra Yoga)—

A person born in the Half-Moon Yoga receives honor from kings, is superior in matters of the military, jewelry, and clothing, and like the moon, brings delight to all people. || 37 ||

### The Result of Birth in the Wheel Configuration (Chakra Yoga)—

### The Result of Birth in the Ocean Configuration (Samudra Yoga)—

> Charitable, brave, of beautiful character, and compassionate; he receives great happiness from the protector of the earth. He who is born in the Ocean Yoga is fortunate, and his lineage is truly blessed by such a man. || 39 ||

In this way, the results of the **Nabhasa Yogas** have been stated clearly and reasonably through the **Shalini** verses. May the wise find happiness through these tender expressions of the gifted poet in this astrological treatise. || 48 ||

# Now begins the Chapter on the Astrology of Planetary Rays

## On the results of one to five rays—

> For those men in whose birth the planetary rays number from one up to five;
> They are in every way subjects of sorrow and poverty, fond of the low-born, from lowly families, and wicked. || 1 ||

He in whose time of birth the sum of the planetary rays is from 1 to 5 is always sorrowful, poor, a friend to the base, belonging to a low family, and a villain. || 1 ||

## On the results of ten rays—

> From five up to the measure of ten <note>original: "kha-indu" (0 and 1, signifying 10)</note>, those rays certainly produce;
> Men who are fond of foreign lands, very miserable, devoid of fortune, and dependent on others for their maintenance. || 2 ||

He in whose time of birth the sum of the planetary rays is from 5 to 10 is one who lives in a foreign country, is wretched, luckless, and is nourished by others. || 2 ||

## On the results of fifteen rays—

> Beyond ten up to fifteen <note>original: "tithayah" (the 15 lunar days)</note>, those rays <note>original: "bhanavah"</note> make a man of little wealth;
> A lover of righteousness <term>Dharma: the moral and religious law</term>, happy according to his family status, and well-dressed. || 3 ||

He in whose time of birth the sum of the planetary rays is from 10 to 15 is a man of modest means, a lover of religion, happy according to the standards of his lineage, and handsome. || 3 ||

## On the results of twenty rays—

> From fifteen up to twenty, those rays <note>original: "gabhastayah"</note> make a man of good character;
> They make him a bringer of good fame, very steadfast, the jewel of his lineage, and skilled in the arts. || 4 ||

He in whose time of birth the sum of the planetary rays is from 15 to 20 is a man of good conduct, a performer of good deeds, patient, an ornament to his family, and clever in various arts. || 4 ||

## On the results of twenty-five rays—

> In whose birth there are twenty-five <note>original: "nakha" (referring to the 20 nails plus 5, or a specific numerical code for 25)</note> rays <note>original: "mayukhah"</note>, his line of fortune brings happiness to his friends.

## **The Result of Thirty-Five Rays—**

One who is born when the sum of the planetary rays <note>original: "mayūkhaiḥ"</note> is thirty-five becomes a leader of a district or province. ## **The Result of Thirty-Six Rays—**

One who is born when the rays number thirty-six or thirty-seven <note>The Sanskrit uses numerical codes: "rasa-agni" (6 and 3) and "naga-agni" (7 and 3)</note> respectively, protects—through his great majesty—either one hundred and fifty thousand or three hundred thousand villages. || 11 ||

> He in whose birth the sum of planetary rays is 36 or 37 becomes the master of three hundred thousand or one hundred and fifty thousand villages. || 11 ||

## **The Result of Thirty-Eight Rays—**

He in whose birth the measure of rays is thirty-eight becomes a man of great energy. A lord of the earth, he rules over four hundred thousand villages and possesses wealth equal to that of Indra <note>The King of the Gods in Hindu mythology</note>. || 12 ||

## **The Result of Thirty-Nine Rays—**

If the rays at birth number thirty-nine, that person becomes a king of celebrated fame. Through his mature prowess, he is like the divine eagle Garuda <note>The celestial bird who is the natural enemy of serpents</note> toward his enemies, who are like arrogant serpents. || 13 ||

> He in whose birth the sum of planetary rays is 39 becomes a man of famous renown, a king, and is like Garuda for destroying his serpent-like enemies. || 13 ||

## **The Result of Forty Rays—**

One born with forty rays <note>original: "kha-abdhi" (0 and 4)</note> becomes a lord of the earth. During his victory marches, the thundering roars of his war-elephants create echoes in the sky that resemble the crashing of monsoon clouds. || 14 ||

# In the Jatakabharana—

He at whose birth the sum of the planetary rays is 40 becomes a king; when he sets out on a campaign of world-conquest, the roar of his army and elephants reaches the heavens like the rumbling of thunderclouds. || 14 ||

### The Result of Forty-One Rays—

If the web of light <note>original: "mayukhajalam," referring to the collective rays of the planets</note> at the time of birth for a man is forty-one, he becomes the protector of the earth, which is adorned by the pure girdle of the shores of the two oceans. || 15 ||

He at whose birth the sum of the planetary rays is 41 becomes the sovereign of the earth as far as the oceans. || 15 ||

### The Result of Forty-Two Rays—

If the sum of the rays at the birth of men is equal to forty-two or forty-three, they possess incomparable strength and splendor, terrifying the ranks of their enemies; they are the protectors of the earth encircled by the three oceans. || 16 ||

He at whose birth the sum of the planetary rays is 42 or 43 becomes a man of great strength, fond of luxuries, a source of distress to his enemies, and the lord of the land surrounded by three seas. || 16 ||

### The Result of Forty-Four Rays—

If at birth the rays measure forty-four, that man becomes a Universal Emperor <term>Chakravarti; a supreme ruler whose chariot wheels roll everywhere without obstruction</term>. In the ocean of his army, the rutting elephants <note>elephants in a state of "mada" or temporal musk, signifying strength</note> resemble mountains, the various ceremonial umbrellas resemble tortoises, the fish-adorned banners resemble actual fish, the chariots resemble boats, and the luster of the weapons resembles the rows of billowing waves. || 17 ||

He at whose birth the sum of the planetary rays is 44 becomes a Universal Emperor. In the ocean-like formation of his army, the intoxicated elephants are like mountains, the various types of umbrellas are like tortoises, the fish-banners are like fish, the chariots are like ships, and the brilliance of the weapons is like the rows of waves. || 17 ||

# Chapter on the Radiant States of the Planets

### The Result of the Forty-Five Ray Combination—

> If the sum of the planetary rays at a person's birth is forty-five or more, they become invincible even to the gods, and the special glory of their fame is sung even in distant lands across the oceans. ॥18॥ <note>original: "pañcābdhitaścet..." The Sanskrit verse uses 'pañca' (5) and 'abdhi' (4) to denote the number 45.</note>

A person at whose birth the sum of the planetary rays is 45 or higher cannot be defeated even by divine beings, and their fame spreads to other continents. ॥ 18 ॥

->Thus ends the Chapter on the Nativity of Rays.<-

### Now begins the Chapter on the Radiant and Other States of the Planets

> A planet in its sign of exaltation is **Radiant**; in its own sign, **Healthy**; in a friend's sign, **Joyful**; and a planet in a beneficial division is **Peaceful**. A planet with shimmering rays is **Powerful**. One that is obscured <note>combust by the sun</note> is **Deformed**; in its sign of fall, **Deficient**; joined with a malefic planet, **Cruel**; and a planet defeated in planetary war is called **Afflicted**. ॥ 1 ॥

A planet situated in its highest point of exaltation is **Radiant** <term>Dīpta: glowing or blazing</term>, in its own zodiac sign it is **Healthy** <term>Svastha: self-abiding or comfortable</term>, in a friend's sign it is **Joyful** <term>Harṣita: delighted</term>, and in a beneficial division <note>Varga: sub-divisional charts</note> it is **Peaceful** <term>Śānta: calm</term>. A planet whose rays are full and strong is **Powerful** <term>Śakta</term>. One that is set <note>ast: hidden by the sun's light</note> is **Deformed** <term>Vikala: impaired</term>. One in its sign of debilitation is **Deficient** <term>Hīna: low or poor</term>. One joined with a "sinful" or malefic planet is **Cruel** <term>Khala: wicked</term>, and one defeated by other planets is **Afflicted** <term>Pīḍita: pained</term>. ॥ 1 ॥

### The Result of a Radiant Planet—

> Under a Radiant planet, a man becomes one who scorches enemies with the heat of his majesty, possessing lordly elephants adorned with flowing ichor. In his home, the Goddess of Fortune <note>Lakshmi</note> resides with playful grace. ॥ 2 ॥

If a planet is Radiant, the subject will distress their enemies through their own glory, will possess intoxicated elephants <note>a symbol of great wealth and military power</note>, and Lakshmi <note>the goddess of wealth</note> will always reside in their home. ॥ 2 ॥

### The Result of a Healthy Planet—

> Under a Healthy planet, a man possesses great vehicles, grain, jewels, large halls, and many servants. He becomes a powerful commander of armies, possessing the glory of victory over the dwellings of enemy multitudes. ॥ 3 ॥

### Results of a Miserable Planet—

> Under a **Miserable** <note>Sanskrit: *Dina*; a planet in its sign of debilitation</note> planet, one becomes exceedingly wretched, tormented by losses, and lives in constant fear of the King and his enemies.

# Now begins the Chapter on the Fruits of Planets Endowed with Position and Other Strengths
## First, the results of a planet endowed with Positional Strength (Sthana-bala):
It certainly produces great prosperity, an increase in strength, and an abundance of splendor. A planet endowed with positional strength provides various types of wealth, skill, and dignity. || 1 ||
If a planet possesses "Sthana-bala" <term>Sthana-bala: Positional strength calculated based on a planet's placement in specific zodiac signs or houses</term>, the person born will be endowed with many manifestations of power, will be strong, radiant, wealthy, skillful, and possessed of great dignity. || 1 ||

## The results of a planet endowed with Directional Strength (Dig-bala):
When a planet's directional strength is excellent, it leads the person toward its own specific direction as a rule. During its period, it brings specific gains to men, mixed with their own earned wealth. || 2 ||

<note>The text transitions here from the internal "moods" or states of planets to their mathematical strengths based on location and compass direction.</note>

### The Results of Planets Endowed with Temporal Strength—

### The Results of Strong Malefic Planets—

They hate virtuous people, destroy their own lineage, and are filled with the quality of darkness <term>Tamoguna: the psychological attribute of ignorance, inertia, and vice</term>. They are of a cruel nature, unclean, and ungrateful. || 5 ||

### Regarding Natural Strength—

> If two or three planets are strong, one should determine the results accordingly.

->The Results of a Planet Endowed with Motion-Strength<-

Sometimes kingdom, sometimes honor, sometimes wealth, and sometimes fame;

->The Results of a Planet Endowed with Aspect-Strength<-

If a planet giving evil results is aspected by a benefic, it does not give the full evil result.

If a planet destined to give bad results is seen <note>aspected</note> by a benefic planet <note>such as Jupiter or Venus</note>, it does not deliver its full negative impact. Conversely, if a planet destined to give good results is seen by a malefic planet <note>such as Saturn or Mars</note>, it does not deliver its full positive impact. This is the essential consideration of *Drik-bala* <term>Drik-bala: strength or influence gained through the planetary aspects/gaze</term>. || 8 ||

# Now begins the Chapter on Solar Combinations
->First, the Voshi and related Yogas-<-

When planets, excluding the Moon, are in the twelfth, the second, or both houses from the Sun,
The ancient teachers have named these the Voshi, Veshi, and Ubhayachari yogas respectively. || 1 ||

The ancient teachers have stated that if any planet other than the Moon is in the twelfth house from the Sun, it is *Voshi Yoga*; if in the second house, it is *Veshi Yoga*; and if planets are present in both the twelfth and second houses, it is *Ubhayachari Yoga*. || 1 ||

->The Results of Voshi Yoga<-

One may have weak eyesight, be a performer of many deeds, look downwards, and have an elevated upper body.

## The Results of Veshi Yoga—

## The Results of Ubhayachari Yoga—

> The man born under *Ubhayachari* <note>A combination where planets are situated in both the 2nd and 12th houses from the Sun, surrounding it</note> is all-enduring, very stable, exceedingly prosperous, full of courage, and graced with a proportionate body. He is not overly tall, possesses a straightforward gaze, and is endowed with great, spotless fortune. || 4 ||

If *Ubhayachari Yoga* is present at the time of birth, the subject is tolerant of all things, steady, very wealthy, dominated by the quality of *Sattva* <note>The quality of purity, goodness, and harmony</note>, possesses a well-proportioned body, is not excessively tall, has a direct gaze, and is blessed with the grace of the goddess of wealth. || 4 ||

> Considering the strength of the Sun, the nature of the planets forming the yoga, and the combination of signs and divisions, the wise should determine whether the results for men will be diminished, moderate, or full. || 5 ||

One should determine the intensity of the results of the aforementioned yogas—whether they will be more or less—by evaluating the strength of the Sun, the specific planet causing the yoga, and the influence of the zodiac signs and degrees. || 5 ||

# Now begins the Chapter on Lunar Yogas

->Regarding the Sunapha, Anapha, Dhurdhura, and Kemadruma Yogas:<-

If planets—excluding the Sun—occupy the second house from the Moon, it is <term>Sunapha</term> (wealth-producing combination). If they occupy the twelfth house, it is <term>Anapha</term>. If planets are present in both houses, the great sages have declared with great respect that the <term>Dhurdhura</term> yoga is formed. || 1 ||

If any planet except the Sun is in the second house from the Moon, it is <term>Sunapha</term>; if in the twelfth, it is <term>Anapha</term>; and if in both, it is the yoga named <term>Dhurdhura</term>. || 1 ||

->The Kemadruma Yoga:<-

If at the time of birth, no lord of the planets occupies the second or twelfth positions from the Moon, they call this the <term>Kemadruma</term> yoga. It certainly causes the loss of wealth. || 2 ||

In whose birth chart there are no planets in the second and twelfth houses from the Moon, the yoga called <term>Kemadruma</term> (the yoga of poverty) occurs. This makes the subject poor. ||

->The Results of Sunapha Yoga:<-

One born under the Sunapha yoga attains honor through his own efforts <note>literally: "earned by his own arms"</note>, possesses clear fame, is intelligent, and happy. Indeed, such a man becomes a minister to a king, virtuous, and skillful. || 3 ||

If born in Sunapha yoga, the person gains respect through their own strength, is famous, happy, a royal minister, and a scholar. ||

->The Results of Anapha Yoga:<-

A person born under the name of Anapha is of generous form, endowed with virtues and fame, as handsome as the god of love <note>original: "Kandarpa," a name for Kamadeva</note>, possesses eloquent speech, follows a good profession, and is always humble and powerful. || 4 ||

If born in Anapha yoga, the person is generous, virtuous, famous, beautiful, a fine orator, possesses a good livelihood, and is humble. || 4 ||

->The Results of Dhurdhura Yoga:<-

The excellent Dhurdhura yoga always grants a man wealth, vehicles, and the happiness of owning land; it makes him a king who has conquered his enemies and is fond of the glances of beautiful-eyed women. || 5 ||

# In the Jatakabharanam—

A person born under the **Durudhara Yoga** <note>A configuration where planets, excluding the Sun, occupy both the 2nd and 12th houses from the Moon</note> possesses wealth, vehicles, horses, and land. They are endowed with happiness, act as a leader or king, conquer their enemies, and are desired by the side-long glances of beautiful women. ॥ 5 ॥

### The Results of Birth in Kemadruma Yoga—

> One who follows a contrary path, is soiled, poorly dressed, a servant, and lives in a foreign land; even the son of a king is deprived of a wife, friends, children, and wealth in Kemadruma. ॥ 6 ॥

A person born in the **Kemadruma Yoga** <note>A difficult configuration occurring when there are no planets in the 2nd or 12th houses from the Moon, and no planets in the lunar angles</note> behaves in a manner contrary to social norms, is unclean, unattractive, performs the work of a messenger or servant, lives abroad, and is separated from his wife, friends, children, and wealth. ॥ 6 ॥

### On the Cancellation of Kemadruma—

> If the Lord of the Night <note>The Moon</note> is in a quadrant from the Lord of the Lotuses <note>The Sun</note>, it creates shining progress and skill, which may be of lesser, middle, or highest quality. ॥ 7 ॥

If the Moon is in a **Quadrant** <note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note> from the Sun, it grants beautiful honor, progress, and cleverness. If the Moon is in a **Succedent** house <note>Panaphara; the 2nd, 5th, 8th, or 11th houses</note>, these results are moderate, and if in a **Cadent** house <note>Apoklima; the 3rd, 6th, 9th, or 12th houses</note>, they are of the highest quality. ॥ 7 ॥

> If at the time of birth, the Moon is aspected by all the celestial bodies, it quickly destroys the Kemadruma defect and makes the man a long-lived universal emperor. ॥ 8 ॥

If all the planets aspect <note>look upon</note> the Moon at the time of birth, the person destroys the Kemadruma affliction and becomes a long-lived sovereign king. ॥ 8 ॥

> Even if this Kemadruma Yoga is seen, if planets are situated in the four Quadrants, it completely leaves behind its Kemadruma nature and becomes **Kalpadruma Yoga** <note>named after the wish-fulfilling tree of heaven</note> for the attainment of auspicious results. ॥ 9 ॥

Even when Kemadruma Yoga is present, if planets are situated in all four Quadrants <note>Kendra houses</note>, then a Yoga called Kalpadruma is formed, which yields highly auspicious results. ॥ 9 ॥

> If Mars is with Jupiter at the time of birth in Libra, the Sun shines in Virgo, and the Moon is in Aries and not aspected by the remaining planets, it destroys Kemadruma and makes one a king of kings. ॥ 10 ॥

## Now begins the Chapter on Renunciation

For those men in whose birth charts Royal Yogas <note>Yoga: a specific planetary combination or "union" that produces a particular result</note> exist alongside Renunciation Yogas, they shall become ascetic practitioners. I shall briefly describe those ascetic yogas as established by the opinions of the ancient masters. || 1 ||

If both Royal status and Renunciation are indicated at the time of birth, the person becomes an ascetic. I am stating these ascetic combinations according to the views of the ancients. || 1 ||

->Renunciation Yoga formed by four or more planets:<-

If four, five, or six planets are situated together in a single house <note>house: one of the twelve divisions of the zodiac in a birth chart</note> at the time of birth, all Royal Yogas are indeed destroyed, and it is declared to be a Yoga of Renunciation. || 2 ||

If four, five, or six planets reside in one place at birth, all "King-making" combinations are nullified, and the Renunciation Yoga prevails. || 2 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant <note>Lord of the Ascendant: the planet that rules the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the moment of birth</note> is not aspected by any other planets and does not see Saturn, and if Saturn—even if weak—does not see the Lord of the Ascendant, the person will be a man highly skilled in initiation and religious vows. || 3 ||

If no planet aspects the Lord of the Ascendant, and the Lord of the Ascendant does not see Saturn, and a strengthless Saturn does not see the Lord of the Ascendant, the person becomes an initiated ascetic. || 3 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant is in a decan <note>decan: a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign; original: "Drekkana"</note> of Saturn, and is in the ninth-part <note>ninth-part: a 3.20-degree subdivision of a sign used for fine detail; original: "Navamsha"</note> of Mars or Saturn while being aspected by Saturn, it makes the person born deceitful, of bad character, and a heretic <note>heretic: one who follows a non-Vedic or heterodox path; original: "Pakhandi"</note> devoted to justifying false doctrines. || 4 ||

If the ruler of the birth sign is in Saturn's decan, and is in the ninth-part of Mars or Saturn while being aspected by Saturn, the person will be crooked, of ill-disposition, and a supporter of heretical sects. || 4 ||

# Jatakabharanam

### On the Different Types of Renunciation—

> According to the strength of the Sun and other planets, the renunciant becomes a Vaikhanasa, a skull-bearer, a wearer of religious marks, a staff-bearer, a wandering ascetic, a wheel-bearer, or a naked monk. If the Lord of the Ascendant is defeated in planetary combat, the person falls from their vows. || 6 ||

Among the planets causing the yoga for renunciation:
If the Sun is the strongest <gloss>of</gloss> all, the person becomes a **Vaikhanasa** (one who lives in forests or mountains, performing fire sacrifices and worshipping the Sun).
If the Moon is strong, he becomes a **Kapali** (a skull-bearing ascetic).
If Mars is strong, he becomes a **Lingi** (one who wears saffron robes and has no top-knot/shikha).
If Mercury is strong, he becomes a **Dandi** (one who carries a ritual staff).
If Jupiter is strong, he becomes a **Yati** (a wandering ascetic who wears saffron and follows the forest-dweller's path).
If Venus is strong, he becomes a **Chakradhara** (a yogi who carries a discus or wheel symbol).
If Saturn is strong, he becomes a **Nagna** (a naked ascetic).
(If the planet causing the yoga or the Lord of the Ascendant is defeated by another planet <note>in "Graha Yuddha" or planetary war</note>, the native becomes a "half-renunciant" or one who falls from their vows). || 6 ||

> When all planets are situated in a single house and are endowed with strength, the person becomes naked, goes without food, and is devoted to the path of Yoga. || 7 ||

If all the planets causing the renunciation yoga are strong and seated in a single zodiac sign, the native remains naked, abstains from food, and becomes a practitioner of Yoga. || 7 ||

## Now begins the Chapter on Portents of Misfortune

> Because the lifespan of men is dependent upon the Chapter on Portents (Arishta), I shall therefore speak only of these portents. In their absence, the calculated lifespan becomes authoritative; if they are present, the calculation is entirely superseded. || 1 ||

The determination of lifespan is subordinate to these portents of misfortune. For this reason, I shall first describe the <term>Arishta Yogas</term> <note>Combinations indicating early death or significant suffering that can override a long-life calculation.</note>. The lifespan of a person free from these portents will be equal to their <term>calculated age</term> <note>The mathematical lifespan derived from planetary positions, known as Ayurdaya.</note>. || 1 ||

### Now, the Portents of Misfortune:

> If the Moon is in the house of Mars <note>Aries or Scorpio</note>, aspected by the Sun and Saturn, and if Jupiter is in the eighth house and not aspected by any auspicious planets, the person loses their life. || 2 ||

<header>In the Jatakabharana—</header>

## Yoga for Early Death—

If the Moon is situated in the 1st, 7th, 8th, or 12th house, joined with malefic planets and not aspected <note>aspected: in astrology, this refers to the angular relationship between planets that allows them to influence one another</note> by any benefic planets, and if the cardinal houses <note>cardinal houses: the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, also known as Kendras</note> are devoid of any benefic planets, the infant surely goes to the land of the Lord of Death. || 21 ||

If the Moon is placed in the 1st, 4th, 7th, 8th, or 10th house while being joined by malefic planets, is not seen by any benefic planet, and no benefic planets occupy the cardinal houses, the newborn meets an early death. || 21 ||

## Yoga for Early Death—

If there is a conjunction of malefic planets in the 8th house or in the cardinal houses, and the Moon, diminished in its phases <note>waning or weak Moon</note>, is situated in the Ascendant <note>the 1st house or rising sign</note>, the one who is born perishes. || 22 ||

When malefic planets join together in the 8th house or the cardinal houses, and a weak Moon is situated in the 1st house, the newborn is destroyed. || 22 ||

## The Vajramushti Yoga—

If malefic planets are in the Ascendant in the signs of Cancer or Scorpio, and if malefic planets occupy the first half <note>from the 1st to the 7th house</note> while benefic planets occupy the latter half, this is called the <term>Vajramushti</term> <note>literally "Diamond Fist" or "Thunderbolt Fist"</note> Yoga, which certainly causes misfortune. || 23 ||

If malefic planets are situated in the 1st house in the signs of Cancer or Scorpio, and malefic planets are placed from the 1st to the 7th house while benefic planets are placed from the 7th back to the 1st house, the <term>Vajramushti</term> Yoga occurs, and it causes <term>Arishta</term> <note>Arishta: a term for planetary combinations indicating ill-health, misfortune, or death in early childhood</note>. || 23 ||

## Yoga for Early Death—

If those called benefic planets are in the 12th, 6th, and 8th houses, and malefic planets are in the trines <note>the 5th and 9th houses</note> or cardinal houses, and the birth occurs when the Moon is rising, the child goes to the other world with haste. || 24 ||

If benefic planets are in the 12th, 6th, or 8th houses, malefic planets are in the trines or cardinal houses, and the Moon is situated in the 1st house, the newborn meets an early death. || 24 ||

## Yoga for Death on the Eleventh Day—

If Jupiter is situated in the house of Saturn <note>Capricorn or Aquarius</note> and occupies the 8th house from the Ascendant, and the body <note>the 1st house</note> is aspected by malefic planets, death occurs on the eleventh day. || 25 ||

### Combination for Rapid Death

If all the planets are situated in the <term>eighth</term>, <term>fourth</term>, and <term>seventh</term> houses, and the <term>Moon</term> is placed between two <term>malefic planets</term>, the ancients say that the one born certainly goes to the abode of Yama <note>the God of Death</note>. || 26 ||

### Combination for Rapid Death

If at the time of birth it is the <term>Hora</term> <note>an astrological hour or division of a sign</note> of the Moon, the birth occurs during either of the two <term>twilight periods</term> <note>sunrise or sunset</note>, the <term>malefic planets</term> are at the very end of a zodiac sign, and the <term>Moon</term> is situated in a <term>quadrant</term> <note>original: "kendra"; the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note> joined with a malefic planet, then the child surely goes to the house of Time <note>meaning death</note>. || 27 ||

### Combination for Rapid Death along with the Mother

If <term>malefic planets</term> situated in the <term>seventh</term> and <term>eighth</term> houses are aspected by other malefic planets and are not seen by <term>benefic planets</term> <note>original: "shubha khaga"; favorable planets like Jupiter or Venus</note>, it quickly causes <term>misfortune</term> <note>original: "arishta"</note> for the infant along with the mother. This is the opinion of many [sages]. || 28 ||

### Combination for Death by a Weapon along with the Mother

If during its own <term>eclipse</term> <note>original: "grahana"</note> the <term>Moon</term> is joined with a malefic planet in the <term>ascendant</term> <note>original: "lagna"; the rising sign</note> and <term>Mars</term> is in the <term>eighth</term> house, the child dies along with the mother. Likewise, if the <term>Sun</term> is joined with a malefic planet in the <term>ascendant</term> during its own eclipse and <term>Mars</term> is in the <term>eighth</term> house, the child dies with the mother by a <term>weapon</term> <note>original: "shastra"</note>. || 29 ||

### Combinations for Early Death

> If Mars or Saturn is in the Ascendant, and the Sun is in the seventh house or elsewhere, and the Moon is joined with either of them, death should be known to occur shortly. || 30 ||

If Mars or Saturn is in the Ascendant <note>the first house or rising sign</note>, the Sun is situated in the seventh house, and the Moon is in any place other than the Ascendant or the seventh house, the newborn dies quickly. || 30 ||

### Combinations for Early Death

> When malefic planets are situated in the Ascendant or the eighth house, the waning Moon is in the twelfth house, and no benefic planets are in the angles, the death of the child is certain. || 31 ||

If malefic planets <note>planets with a harsh influence, like Saturn or Mars</note> are located in the Ascendant or the eighth house, the waning Moon is in the twelfth house, and no benefic planets <note>gentle planets like Jupiter or Venus</note> are in the <term>Kendras</term> <note>the angular houses: 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th</note>, then the death of the newborn occurs. || 31 ||

### Combinations for Misfortune

If malefic planets are in the <term>Trikonas</term> <note>the trines: 5th and 9th houses</note> or the angles and are not aspected <note>viewed through an astrological glance</note> by benefic planets, and either the Sun or the Moon is situated in the Ascendant, the newborn suffers from <term>Arishta</term>. || 32 ||

### Combinations for Death in the Ninth Year

If the Sun, Saturn, and Venus are joined with malefic planets and are aspected by Jupiter, the newborn still faces misfortune in the ninth year. || 33 ||

> If the Moon is in the seventh house and the Lord of the Eighth is in the Ascendant and aspected by Saturn, it is declared by the ancient sages who knew the secrets of birth to cause misfortune in the ninth year. || 34 ||

If the Moon is in the seventh house and the <term>Lord of the Eighth</term> <note>the planet ruling the house of death</note> is in the Ascendant and aspected by Saturn, the newborn suffers misfortune in the ninth year; this is the opinion of the ancient sages. || 34 ||

## Combinations for Death Within One Year

> If a fatal indication is observed, and the Moon <note>original: "praleyamshau" - the cool-rayed one</note> is in its own house <note>Cancer</note> or in the Ascendant, endowed with strength and joined or aspected by powerful malefic planets, the time of death occurs within a year. || 35 ||

In the previously mentioned fatal combinations where the specific timing was not defined, death occurs within one year if a strong Moon is situated in Cancer or the Ascendant and is aspected by a strong malefic planet <note>malefic planets typically include Saturn, Mars, and the Sun</note>. || 35 ||

## Fatal Combination

> If the Moon is in the 1st, 5th, 9th, 12th, 7th, or 8th house, joined with malefic planets, decreasing in light <note>the waning phase</note>, and is neither joined with nor aspected by benefic planets, there is no doubt that a fatal misfortune occurs. || 36 ||

If the Moon is not associated with or aspected by benefic planets <note>benefics typically include Jupiter, Venus, and Mercury</note> and is positioned in the 1st, 5th, 9th, 12th, 7th, or 8th house, the child suffers a fatal misfortune. || 36 ||

## Combination for Death in the Fifth Year

> If at the time of birth, the Sun, Mercury, and Jupiter; or Saturn, Mars, and Venus; or the Sun, Mars, and Saturn are joined together in a single sign along with the Moon, the destruction of the child occurs in the fifth year. || 37 ||

If at the time of birth, the Moon is in the same sign as (1) Sun, Mercury, and Jupiter; or (2) Saturn, Mars, and Venus; or (3) Sun, Mars, and Saturn, the child meets death in the fifth year. || 37 ||

## Death Timing Based on Zodiacal Signs

> The Lord of the Ascendant <term>Lagnasha: the planet ruling the rising sign</term> situated in the 6th house causes destruction in a number of years equal to the number of the sign. The Lord of the Decanate <term>Drekkana: a 10-degree subdivision of a sign</term> causes it in months, and the Lord of the Navamsha <term>Navamsha: a 1/9th subdivision of a sign</term> causes it in days; so say all the great sages. || 38 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant is placed in the 6th house <note>the house of enemies and disease</note>, death occurs in as many years as the numerical value of that sign. If the Lord of the Decanate is in the 6th house, death occurs in that many months. If the Lord of the Navamsha is in the 6th house, death occurs in that many days. || 38 ||

## Death in a Month, Sixteen Days, or a Year

> Saturn in the Ascendant aspected by a cruel planet <note>malefic</note> causes destruction in sixteen days. If joined with malefic planets, it causes death in a month; and if surrounded by malefics, in a year. || 39 ||

If Saturn is joined with one malefic planet, death occurs in one month; if joined with two or more malefics, death occurs within one year. || 39 ||

### Death Yoga in the Eleventh Year and Others—

Mercury, when joined with the Sun and Moon and aspected by a malefic planet, causes destruction in the 11th year. Alternatively, if the Sun, Saturn, and Mars are all in the Ascendant and a waning Moon is in the 7th house, death occurs in either the 6th or 7th year. || 40 ||

### Death Yoga in the Seventh Year—

If a waning Moon is in the 7th house, and Saturn, Mars, and Venus are in the Ascendant without receiving the <term>aspect</term><note>A 'drishti' or planetary gaze, where one planet influences another from a distance.</note> of Jupiter, they certainly cause the death of the newborn in the 7th year. || 41 ||

### Death Yoga within Two Years—

If both the Moon and a <term>combust Mercury</term><note>A planet so close to the Sun that its light is 'burnt up' or obscured.</note> are situated in <term>quadrants</term><note>The 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a birth chart.</note> and are aspected by Mars and Saturn, the child suffers a fatal misfortune within two years. So say Vashistha and other ancient sages. || 42 ||

### Another Death Yoga within Two Years—

If the Moon is waning and situated in the 8th house from the <term>Lord of the Ascendant</term><note>The planet that rules the sign rising at birth.</note>, and is aspected by malefics but not by <term>benefics</term><note>Gentle planets like Jupiter or Venus.</note>, it causes death at the end of two years. || 43 ||

## Now begins the Chapter on the Cancellation of Afflictions

Even though the various combinations known as <term>Arishta</term> <note>Arishta refers to planetary combinations indicating misfortune, illness, or early death</note> have been described in great detail by the masters of <term>Hora Shastra</term> <note>The science of predictive astrology</note>, those afflictions are sometimes unable to manifest if they are neutralized. Therefore, the methods for the cancellation of these afflictions are now being declared. || 1 ||

The experts in astrological science have described "Arishta" yogas (inauspicious combinations) at length. For those afflictions that cannot be overcome on their own, the methods of their destruction (neutralization) are now explained. || 1 ||

If at the time of a person's birth, the Moon—the Lord of the Night-blooming Lilies—is full and beheld by all the other celestial bodies, it destroys the affliction. Alternatively, if a powerful Moon is situated in a friend's <term>Navamsha</term> <note>A one-ninth division of a zodiac sign, used to determine the hidden strength of a planet</note> and is aspected by a benefic planet, it destroys the affliction. Even a waning Moon, if placed in its own exalted sign and aspected by Venus, removes the approaching misfortune just as a lion slays an elephant. || 2 ||

If at the time of birth the Moon is aspected by all eight planets starting with the Sun, it destroys the afflictions. Or, if a strong Moon is situated in a friend's ninth-part and is seen by a benefic planet, it destroys the misfortune. Or, even a weak Moon situated in a friend's ninth-part and seen by a benefic planet destroys the misfortune. Or, if the Moon is in its sign of exaltation and is seen by Venus, the misfortune is destroyed. || 2 ||

Benefic planets, excluding the malefic ones, destroy afflictions if they are situated in the 6th, 7th, or 8th houses from the Moon. Furthermore, the Moon—the embodiment of nectar—destroys misfortune if it is joined with a benefic planet and situated in a benefic <term>Drekkana</term> <note>A ten-degree division of a sign, also known as a decanate</note>. || 3 ||

In a person's birth chart, if all benefic planets (excluding the cruel ones) are placed in the 6th, 7th, or 8th positions from the Moon, or if the Moon is joined with a benefic planet and resides in a favorable decanate, the misfortunes are destroyed. || 3 ||

Benefic planets situated in the twelve houses or a full Moon are declared to be destroyers of affliction. If the Moon is in a benefic sign, aspected by the <term>Lagnesha</term> <note>The Lord of the Ascendant or Rising Sign</note> and not aspected by any others, it protects one from the yoga of misfortune. || 4 ||

# Chapter on the Cancellation of Misfortune

If Jupiter is in the tenth house from the Moon, Mercury and Venus are both in the twelfth, the malefic planets are in the eleventh, and the Lord of the Ascendant <note>The planet ruling the rising sign</note> is situated in the 3rd, 4th, 10th, 11th, or 12th house, and the Moon is aspected by <note>received the gaze of</note> a benefic planet, then the destruction of misfortune certainly occurs. || 9 ||

->If at the time of birth the Lord of the Birth <note>Lagnēśa</note> is aspected by pure planets and is possessed of great strength, it brings about the destruction of the misfortune arising from the Moon. || 10 ||<-

If the birth occurs at night and the full Moon is in its sign of exaltation <note>Taurus</note> or its own house <note>Cancer</note>, or in its own division <note>Navamsha</note>, and is aspected by a benefic planet, the Moon destroys death. || 11 ||

If the Moon is in the constellations of Ashvini, Krittika, or Pushya, or is in the best division <term>Vargottama</term> <note>occupying the same sign in both the main chart and the ninth harmonic chart</note>, and is full of digits <note>bright and full</note>, then even the most severe misfortune known as Tripushkara quickly goes to destruction. || 12 ||

If the Moon is in the second or third quarter of the constellation Pushya, or in the second quarter of Rohini, and is aspected by a benefic, it protects the newborn from the blemish of death. || 13 ||

The Moon, even if eclipsed, leads to the cancellation of misfortune without a doubt if it is situated in Cancer or Aries and occupies a cardinal house <term>Kendra</term> <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note> while being aspected by a benefic planet. || 14 ||

# Now begins the Chapter on the Breaking of All Planetary Misfortunes

If, at the time of birth, the powerful Jupiter—shining with the pure brilliance of a garland of rays—is situated in the first house, the sages declare that he surely destroys all misfortunes. || 1 ||

If the rising Jupiter is strong and seated in the ascendant, it destroys all misfortunes; so the ancient sages have said. || 1 ||

When the malefic planets are weak and the benefics are powerful, and the ascendant falls in the sign of a benefic planet and is aspected <note>Glanced at or influenced by</note> by benefic celestial bodies, then any approaching misfortune is truly diminished. || 2 ||

In a person's birth chart, if the malefic planets are powerless, the benefic planets are strong, the ascendant is in a benefic sign, and the ascendant is viewed by a benefic planet, then their misfortunes are destroyed. || 2 ||

Malefic planets situated in the divisions <note>Varga: harmonic divisional charts</note> of a benefic planet, when aspected by benefic planets also situated in benefic divisions, are capable of destroying even the most severe misfortune. || 3 ||

If a malefic planet in a benefic's division is seen by a benefic planet that is also in a benefic's division, misfortune is destroyed. || 3 ||

Rahu <note>The North Node of the Moon</note> situated in the third, sixth, or eleventh house from the ascendant destroys misfortune if aspected by benefics. Likewise, if all the planets are in "head-rising" signs <note>Signs that rise head-first on the horizon, considered auspicious</note> and are not in a state of affliction, there is a total breaking of misfortune. || 4 ||

If Rahu, located in the third, sixth, or eleventh house from the ascendant, is seen by a benefic planet, or if all planets are situated in "head-rising" signs, then all misfortunes are destroyed. || 4 ||

At the time of birth, a benefic planet possessing the strength of victory and not aspected by any malefic, removes misfortune...

# Chapter on the Destruction of All Evil Planetary Influences

If a planet moving within a white halo is victorious at the time of birth, and is beheld by other auspicious planets, or if a planet that has set <note>referring to heliacal setting or combustion</note> is beheld by malefic planets, the evil omens are destroyed. || 5 ||
->If at the time of birth a victorious auspicious planet is seen by other auspicious planets, or if a malefic planet looks upon a planet that has set, the misfortunes are destroyed. || 5 ||<-

If the sky is free of dust and the planets are "healthy" <note>well-placed in their signs</note>, if the clouds are a deep, healthy blue, if gentle winds blow and the moments are pure at the time of delivery, the evil omens are surely destroyed. || 6 ||
->If at the time of birth the sky is clear, all planets are in healthy states, the clouds are blue, the wind blows slowly, and it is a beautiful auspicious moment, then all misfortunes are destroyed. || 6 ||<-

If the birth occurs during the rising of the Sage born from a water-pot <note>The star Canopus, associated with the Sage Agastya</note>, then the evil omen surely dissolves just as lac <note>a resinous secretion used as wax</note> melts in the fire. || 7 ||
->If the star Agastya rises at the time of birth, then all misfortunes are destroyed like lac in a fire. || 7 ||<-

Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon</note> situated in the Ascendant in the signs of Taurus, Aries, or Cancer becomes the destroyer of misfortune. Likewise, if there are many auspicious yogas <note>planetary combinations</note>, the evil omen meets its end. || 8 ||
->If the Ascendant is Taurus, Aries, or Cancer and Rahu is seated there, and there are many auspicious combinations, then the misfortunes are destroyed. || 8 ||<-

Ketu <note>the South Node of the Moon</note> situated in the three signs starting with Capricorn <note>Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces</note> in the 11th, 6th, or 3rd houses is the cause for the pacification of death. If Venus, Jupiter, and Mercury are in trines <note>the 5th and 9th houses</note> to each other, they also remove the evil omen. || 9 ||
->If Ketu is in Capricorn, Aquarius, or Pisces in the 11th, 6th, or 3rd house, or if Venus, Jupiter, and Mercury are all situated in the ninth or fifth houses, then the misfortunes are destroyed. || 9 ||
<note>The number in the Hindi translation (६) is likely a typo for ९ (9) in the original print.</note>

Even if born during the twilights, or during the astronomical periods of Vaidhriti, Vyatipata, Bhadra, or Gandanta, if all planets are situated in the visible hemisphere <note>houses 7 through 12</note> at the time of birth, it serves to destroy the evil omen. || 10 ||
->If at the time of birth all planets are situated from the Ascendant to the seventh house, then even for those born during the two twilights, Vaidhriti, or Gandanta, the misfortunes are destroyed. || 10 ||

<term>Arishta-bhanga</term>: The cancellation or destruction of planetary ill-fortune.

<term>Trikonaga</term>: Planets situated in the trinal houses (1st, 5th, or 9th).

# In the Jatakabharana—

The Sun, when positioned in its sign of exaltation <note>Aries</note> and not afflicted by eclipses or malefic influences, destroys all misfortunes. Likewise, if all the planets are situated in the third, sixth, or eleventh houses from the ascendant, they pacify all planetary evils. || 11 ||
<margin>If the Sun is in its highest dignity and placed in the 3rd, 11th, or 6th house without being seized by malefic planets, or if all planets are gathered in a single sign within the 6th, 3rd, 10th, or 11th houses, the "Arishta" <note>unfavorable planetary combinations</note> is destroyed.</margin>

Whether from the Moon or from the Ascendant, if two, three, or many planets are positioned in a single house other than the one occupied by the Moon or Ascendant, the destruction of misfortune certainly occurs. || 12 ||
<margin>If two or more planets are situated together in a sign different from the Moon or the Ascendant, it is certain that the planetary evils will be nullified.</margin>

If Jupiter is in its own home <note>Sagittarius or Pisces</note> and placed in the fourth house, and is aspected by a powerful Moon at the time of birth, it surely destroys the inauspiciousness arising from planetary afflictions in an instant. || 13 ||
<margin>If Jupiter, the "Minister of the King of Gods," is in the 4th house from the Ascendant in its own sign and is viewed by a full and strong Moon, misfortunes are dispelled.</margin>

If there are three planets each in the twelfth and second houses from a planet situated in the Ascendant, those planets born of that moment become the destroyers of misfortune. || 14 ||
<margin>If three planets are placed in the 12th house and three in the 2nd house, the defect arising from the planet in the Ascendant is removed.</margin>

Whether in the angles, the succedent houses, or the cadent houses, if all planets are situated in auspicious subdivisions <note>Navamshas</note>, they are remembered as the causes for the breaking of misfortune. || 15 ||
<term>Kendra</term> <note>Angles: 1st, 4th, 7th, 10th houses</note>, <term>Panaphara</term> <note>Succedent: 2nd, 5th, 8th, 11th houses</note>, and <term>Apoklima</term> <note>Cadent: 3rd, 6th, 9th, 12th houses</note>.
<margin>If at the time of birth all planets are placed in these house groups and occupy favorable divisions, the Arishta is destroyed.</margin>

If planets are situated in dual signs and are placed in the fourth house from one another, they take away the defects of misfortune. || 16 ||
<term>Dual Signs</term> <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, and Pisces</note>.
<margin>If all planets are in dual signs and are mutually in the fourth position from each other, the planetary evils are removed.</margin>

# Chapter on the Neutralization of Afflictions from All Planets

If a benefic planet <note>a naturally auspicious planet like Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury</note> is positioned in a quadrant <note>the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses, known as Kendra</note> with superior strength, and there are no planets at all in the eighth house, the person will certainly live for thirty years. If this same combination is also aspected by another benefic planet, the lifespan becomes forty years. || 17 ||

If Jupiter is situated in its own decan <note>original: "drekkana"; a one-third division of a zodiac sign</note>, the lifespan is twenty-seven years. If Jupiter is in its sign of exaltation <note>Cancer</note> in the ascendant, and Venus is also in a quadrant, the person lives for one hundred years. || 18 ||

If a strong Moon is in the ascendant or in its sign of exaltation, and other benefic planets are in their own signs, the lifespan is sixty years. If the benefic planets are in their root-trine <note>original: "moolatrikona"; a specific favorable position for a planet</note> and Jupiter is in its exaltation or in the ascendant, the lifespan is eighty years. || 19 ||

If the Moon is not in the first, sixth, or eighth houses, and the malefic planets are in their own signs, and two strong planets are situated in the tenth house, the great sages declare that the person born will live for one hundred years. || 20 ||

If the eighth house is empty, benefic planets are in the quadrants, Jupiter is in the ascendant, and benefics are in the third, sixth, or eleventh houses without being aspected by malefic planets, then the measure of life will be seventy years. || 21 ||

->Thus ends the Chapter on the Neutralization of Afflictions from All Planets.<-

# Chapter on the Consideration of Auspicious and Inauspicious Periods

> The results produced by royal yogas <note>Raja Yogas: planetary combinations indicating power and status</note>, planetary positions, house placements, and those arising from misfortune;
> Since these results manifest during the planetary periods, I shall now fully describe those effects. || 1 ||

The fruits of royal power, zodiac signs, house placements, and misfortunes all occur during the period of the planet responsible for that yoga. Therefore, I am describing the results of these periods. || 1 ||

## Prayer to the Deities—

> May the bestower of boons to all gods <note>Ganesha</note> grant you boons; may Sharada <note>Saraswati, the goddess of learning</note> also grant boons within your lotus-like mouth;
> May Indira <note>Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth</note> truly dwell within your home, and may your fame travel even unto the ocean. || 2 ||

May Lord Ganesha, who grants boons to all the gods, give you his blessing; may Saraswati reside in your mouth; may Lakshmi reside in your house; and may your fame spread as far as the sea. || 2 ||

> If the Lord of the Ascendant <note>Lagnasya: the planet ruling the first house of the birth chart</note> is in its sign of exaltation, its own home, its root-trine <note>Moola-trikona: a specific favorable placement</note>, its own divisional chart, or in a quadrant;
> And if it is not combust <note>hidden by the sun's light</note> nor aspected by malefic planets, it shall grant auspicious results during its ripening <note>its Dasha or planetary period</note>. || 3 ||

If the Lord of the Ascendant is situated in its exaltation, its own sign, its root-trine, or its six divisional charts, and is not hidden by the sun or seen by harmful planets, it gives auspicious results during its period. || 3 ||

> If all the benefic planets are placed in the third, sixth, or eleventh houses, there is happiness and wealth in childhood;
> If the malefic planets are in those same places, then in the final part of life, there is complete happiness regarding wife, wealth, and children. || 4 ||

If all the gentle planets are located in the 3rd, 6th, and 11th houses, one receives happiness in childhood. If the harsh planets are located there, one receives the happiness of a spouse, wealth, and children in old age. || 4 ||

> If a leading planet is in its exaltation, its own home, or a friend's home or division, but is also in its sign of fall or an enemy's sign;
> Then the results in its period will be mixed; this should be understood by those learned in the science of horoscopy. || 5 ||

If a planet is placed in its exaltation, its own sign, or a friend's house or division, but is simultaneously placed in its sign of debilitation or an enemy's house, there will be mixed results during its period. || 5 ||

# Chapter on the Consideration of Good and Bad Periods

> When Jupiter <note>original: "Vachampati" - Lord of Speech</note> is situated in the Ascendant, in its sign of exaltation, in its own sign, or in the 10th, 11th, or 3rd houses at birth, it grants a kingdom <note>or high administrative authority</note> proportionate to one's lineage, along with distinguished excellence in various sciences. > The "Ascending" period <term>Arohini Dasha: a period where a planet moves from its point of debilitation toward its exaltation</term> of a planet bestows auspicious results. If the period is "Descending" <term>Avarohini Dasha: a period where a planet moves from its point of exaltation toward its debilitation</term>, it causes a decrease in good results. (7)

If a planet's period is Ascending (situated within five signs from its point of debilitation), it gives auspicious results. If it is Descending (situated within five signs from its point of exaltation), it gives inauspicious results. (7)

### Results of the Moon's Period in Cancer:

> The Moon in Cancer during its period brings the acquisition of a wife, sons, friends, and wealth.

In the period of the Moon situated in the sign of Cancer, one obtains a wife, children, friends, and riches. (7½)

### Results of the Moon's Period in the Signs of Mars:

> It creates a tendency toward the destruction of one's wife and livestock when in the home of the Son of the Earth <note>Mars</note>. (8)

In the period of the Moon situated in a sign owned by Mars <note>Aries or Scorpio</note>, there is the loss or harm of one's wife and cattle. (8)

### Results of the Moon's Period in the Signs of Mercury and Jupiter:

> It brings the acquisition of excellent scriptures and friends when staying in the home of Mercury or Jupiter.

In the period of the Moon situated in the signs of Mercury <note>Gemini or Virgo</note> or Jupiter <note>Sagittarius or Pisces</note>, one gains beautiful knowledge of the scriptures and good friends. (8½)

### Results of the Moon's Period in the Signs of Venus:

In the period of the Moon situated in the signs of Venus <note>Taurus or Libra</note>, one receives wealth through the pleasure of the King <note>government or authorities</note>. (9)

# In the Jatakabharanam—

> High fame and honor from kings shall occur at the onset of the Sun's period when positioned in the sign of the Lion. || 9 ||

During the period of the Sun situated in the sign of Leo <note>The Sun is the ruler of Leo, making this a particularly powerful placement</note>, one gains various types of wealth, grain, and prestige through agriculture in forts and forests, as well as great honor in the royal court. || 9 ||

### Results of the Sun's Period in the Sign of Virgo—

> There shall be the birth of daughters, the constant worship of gods and the twice-born, and the acquisition of cattle during the period of the Friend of the Lotus <note>original: "Ambujabandhu," a poetic epithet for the Sun</note> when situated in Virgo. || 10 ||

During the period of the Sun situated in the sign of Virgo, there is the birth of a daughter, the respectful worship of <term>Brahmins</term> <note>The "twice-born" or priestly class</note> and deities, and the gain of four-legged animals such as cows. || 10 ||

### Results of the Sun's Period in the Sign of Libra—

> Suffering regarding fields, children, wealth, and women; fear of thieves and fire; travel to foreign lands; and a great loss of status for men occurs during the period of the Sun in the sign of the Balance. || 11 ||

During the period of the Sun situated in the sign of Libra <note>The Sun is "debilitated" or at its weakest in Libra, hence the negative predictions</note>, there is suffering related to agriculture, sons, and wives; fear of theft and fire; wandering in foreign lands; and experiences of disrespect. || 11 ||

> In the period of the Sun joined with its lowest degree, one is easily deceived by others; there is the attainment of sorrow caused by a wife, and constant friendship with base people. || 12 ||

During the period of the Sun situated in its sign of debilitation, one is effortlessly cheated by others, suffers grief on account of a woman, and forms alliances with low-minded individuals. || 12 ||

> In the period of the Sun situated in the eighth house while in its sign of debilitation, there shall be anxiety and the arising of faults; if situated in the sixth house, there is pain from ulcers and many kinds of obstacles from enemies. || 13 ||

During the period of the Sun situated in the sign of Libra while placed in the eighth house <note>The house of transformations and chronic issues</note>, there is agitation of the mind; if the Sun is in the sixth house <note>The house of debt, disease, and enemies</note>, there is suffering from wounds and distress caused by enemies. || 13 ||

### Results of the Sun’s Period in Sagittarius

Happiness from wife, children, and wealth; honor from the royal family and the twice-born; and great joy from the study of music and traditional scriptures occurs during the period of the Sun when it has reached the Bow. || 15 ||

During the period of the Sun located in the sign of Sagittarius <note>Dhanu</note>, there is happiness derived from one's wife, children, and wealth. ### The results of the Sun's period when placed in its sign of exaltation in the eighth house—

The period of the Sun <note>original: "Dinesha," literally 'Lord of the Day'</note> when situated in its highest exaltation <note>Aries</note> in the eighth house <note>the house of longevity and obstacles</note> brings suffering. At the beginning of the Sun's period, various obstacles befall the parents. The first period of the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note> grants specific distress, while the first period of the Moon <note>original: "Nakshatranatha," Lord of the Constellations</note> is highly auspicious. || 20 ||

If the Sun's period is the first in life, there is suffering for the parents; if the Ascendant's period is first, there is special distress; and if the Moon's period is first, the results are auspicious. || 20 ||

### Chapter on the results of the Moon's period

The ascending <term>Arohini</term><note>A planet moving toward its exaltation point</note> period of the Moon is said to bring the fulfillment of all goals for men, especially success. Likewise, the descending <term>Avarohini</term><note>A planet moving away from its exaltation point</note> period causes delays in all undertakings and a dullness of intellect. || 1 ||

If it is the ascending period of the Moon, there is especially the fulfillment of all tasks. If it is the descending period, there is slow intelligence in all works. || 1 ||

At the onset of the period of the Moon <note>Lord of the Constellations</note>, men achieve great prestige. They attain high ministerial positions, the favor of the King, and a tendency toward the worship of gods and priests <note>Brahmins</note>. || 2 ||

There is the acquisition of various types of good counsel and knowledge, the attainment of wealth, and skill in various arts. Wealth is obtained through perfumes, oils, fruits, flowers, trees, or gems. || 3 ||

There is fame, good reputation, an increase in humility, a mind inclined toward helping others, and glory. There is a love for wandering here and there, the birth of female children, and a gentle nature. || 4 ||

There is a great interest in water-related works, but also a tendency toward laziness, excessive sleep, and a forgiving nature.

In the period of the Moon situated at degrees higher than its point of maximum debilitation (3°) within the sign of Scorpio, there is profit from trade, difficulty in performing religious duties, an inclination toward unrighteousness, and limited friendship with one's circle of friends. || 17 ||

In the period of the Moon located in the sign of Sagittarius, there is an increase in livestock like elephants and horses <note>In a modern context, this signifies an increase in vehicles or status symbols</note>, loss of previously accumulated wealth, and happiness derived from good luck. || 18 ||

# Chapter on the Results of the Period of Mars

->Results of the Moon's Period when situated in the Twelfth House<-

At the commencement of the Moon's period, if it is located in the twelfth house <note>The house of loss and expenditure</note>, wealth will be acquired through sinful or unethical means. If the Moon is waning and situated in the sixth house <note>The house of enemies and debt</note>, the results are exactly as previously described. ||24||

In the period of the Moon situated in the twelfth house, there is gain of wealth through sin; if the waning Moon is in the sixth house, wealth is likewise gained through sinful means. || 24 ||

->Results of the Moon's Period when in its Sign of Debilitation or the Eighth House<-

At the start of the period of the Moon when it is in its sign of debilitation <note>Scorpio</note> or located in the eighth house, there will be the <term>onset of disease</term> <note>original: gadogdamaḥ</note>. If it is also joined by malefic planets, then the person suffers death or <term>loss of caste status</term> <note>original: jāticyutiṃ; social ostracization or loss of community standing</note>. ||25||

If the Moon in its sign of debilitation is situated in the eighth house, then in its period comes the arrival of disease; if in the aforementioned state the Moon is joined by malefic planets, the person meets death or is fallen from his caste. || 25 ||

->Thus ends the Chapter on the Results of the Moon's Period.<-

# Chapter on the Results of the Period of Mars

If the <term>star-planets</term> <note>original: tārā-grahāḥ; refers to the five planets Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, and Saturn, excluding the Sun and Moon</note> are in their signs of exaltation but are also retrograde or combust, they will surely yield mixed results during their ripening period <note>dasha/planetary period</note>; this should be carefully considered by the wise. ||1||

The <term>star-planets</term> (Mars and the other four planets), if situated in an exalted sign while being combust or retrograde, give mixed results during their period.

In the period of <term>the son of the Earth</term> <note>original: kṣitinandanasya; a traditional name for Mars</note>, wealth is gained through weapons, from the king, from medicine, from four-legged animals, and through various types of industrious efforts. However, the learned say the results also include suffering from bile and blood-related fevers, fear of the sovereign, deviation from moral conduct, fainting spells, and strife within one's own home. ||2||

In the period of Mars situated in an auspicious place, wealth is gained through weapons, the king, medicine, animals, and many kinds of enterprises. In an inauspicious place...

# Chapter on the Results of the Mercury Period

->The Results of the Period of Mars situated in the Sign of Pisces<-

At the commencement of the period of the Son of the Earth <note>original: "Aninanandana," a title for Mars</note> when he has entered the sign of Pisces, there will be anxiety regarding children and family. One experiences expenses, illness, but also gradual gains, as well as skin ailments like scabies or ringworm, and residence in foreign lands. || 17 ||

In the period of Mars situated in the sign of Pisces, there is worry about sons and others, expenditure, disease, gain of wealth, itching, ringworm, and living abroad. || 17 ||

->The Results of the Period of Mars in the Best Division<-

One becomes possessed of victory achieved in battle, endowed with strength, and exceedingly delightful due to their virtues. In the ripening <note>term: "Paka" (ripening), referring to the active period or Dasha of a planet</note> of the Son of the Earth situated in the Best Division <term>Vargottama: the position where a planet occupies the same zodiac sign in both the main chart and the ninth divisional chart, increasing its strength</term>, there is the acquisition of various kinds of goods. || 18 ||

In the period of Mars situated in the Vargottama Navamsha, there is victory in battle, strength, beauty through virtues, and the gain of many objects. || 18 ||

->The Results of the Period of Mars situated in its Debilitated Division<-

In the ripening of Mars <note>original: "Kuja," another name for Mars</note> staying in its debilitated division <term>Nichamsha: the ninth divisional chart position where a planet is at its weakest</term>, there is wandering in vain and depression of the mind. Success in one's work remains very far off; one suffers from lowliness and a great loss of status. || 19 ||

In the period of Mars situated in the Navamsha of its debilitated sign, there is useless wandering, mental grief, obstacles in work, the company of low-minded people, and loss of prestige. || 19 || <note>The number '16' in the prose appears to be an original typesetting error for '19'.</note>

->The Results of the Period of Mars situated in its Root-Trine Sign<-

In the ripening of Mars when it is situated in its Root-Trine <term>Moolatrikona: a specific favorable placement for a planet, stronger than its own sign but less than its exaltation</term> or its exaltation house, and occupying the tenth house of action, there is surely the attainment of kingdom, victory over enemies, and the acquisition of fine vehicles and ornaments. || 20 ||

If Mars is in its Moolatrikona and seated in the tenth house, then in its period, there is the attainment of a kingdom (or high status), victory over enemies, and the gain of vehicles and jewelry. || 20 ||

# In the Jatakabharana—

One who is a knower of good deeds, righteousness, and the traditional scriptures <note>original: "Agama Shastra"</note>, always humble, respectful toward sacrifices and rituals, a devotee of the priestly class <note>original: "Brahmins"</note> and the gods, exceedingly wealthy, and authoritative. Such a person finds contentment through children and the like, enjoys comforts from land, clothing, and horses, is powerful, famous within their lineage, a knower of the past and future, a seeker of good company, intelligent, and steadfast. In the period <note>term: Dasha (the planetary period governing a specific span of a person's life)</note> of an inauspicious Jupiter <note>original: "Brihaspati"</note>, one should also consider the possibility of occasional pain in the throat or similar areas. The ancient teachers have stated these as general results. Now, the specific results of Jupiter's period while situated in each zodiac sign are described. ॥ 1-4 ॥

### Results of Jupiter's Period in Aries—

**At the commencement of the period of the one worshiped by the thirty gods <note>A poetic title for Jupiter, the teacher of the gods</note> when positioned in Aries, men shall experience:**
**Wealth from the lord of wealth, leadership over many, and the attainment of happiness from wife, children, and so forth. ॥ 5 ॥**

In the period of Jupiter situated in the sign of Aries, a person receives wealth from the government or king, becomes a leader of many, and attains happiness through their spouse and children. ॥ 5 ॥

### Results of Jupiter's Period in Taurus—

**At the commencement of the period of the Lord of Speech <note>Jupiter</note> when positioned in Taurus, a man becomes exceedingly miserable.**
**He dwells in foreign lands, performs great acts of daring, possesses little wealth, and is devoid of celebrations. ॥ 6 ॥**

In the period of Jupiter situated in the sign of Taurus, a person is unhappy, lives abroad, undertakes great risks, possesses meager wealth, and lacks festive joy in his life. ॥ 6 ॥

### Results of Jupiter's Period in Gemini—

**At the commencement of the period of Jupiter when positioned in the Pair <note>Gemini</note>, a man becomes pure.**
**Yet he opposes his mother and those born of his own lineage, and is scorched by the great sorrow of disputes with his wife. ॥ 7 ॥**

In the period of Jupiter situated in the sign of Gemini, a man is pure in character, but he becomes an opponent to his mother and kinsmen, and remains filled with dejection due to arguments with his spouse.

### Results of Jupiter's Period in its Highest Exaltation—

**During the ripening <note>term: Paka-kala (the time when a planet's influence bears fruit)</note> of the Lord of Speech when resting in its exaltation <note>Cancer</note>, one attains the kingdom of their lineage.**
**One becomes highly renowned by a distinguished name, forms friendships with the high-born, and gains great opulence. ॥ 8 ॥**

> In the ripening of the period of the Lord of Speech <note>original: "Vachaspati" (Jupiter)</note> when it has left its debilitated degrees, wealth is gained through hunters or forest-dwellers. However, the person may suffer distress through trees or through the deception of their wealth. || 17 ||

In the period of Jupiter when it is free from its debilitated degrees, a person gains wealth through the work of boatmen <note>The Sanskrit "Nishada" refers to forest-dwellers or hunters; the Hindi gloss suggests boatmen</note>, agriculture, or trees, but suffers hardship due to being cheated of their money. || 17 ||

## Results of the Jupiter Period in Aquarius—

At the beginning of the period of the Lord of Speech <note>original: "Vachamadheesha," a title for Jupiter</note> situated in the Water-bearer <note>Aquarius</note>, a man becomes a connoisseur of the arts. He possesses great intelligence directed toward the attainment of knowledge and fame, and remains deeply devoted to the charms and pleasures of women. || 18 ||

In the period of Jupiter situated in the sign of Aquarius, a person is a knower of arts, learned, famous, wealthy, intelligent, and attached to the pleasures of women. || 18 ||

## Results of the Jupiter Period in Pisces—

At the commencement of the period of the Lord of Speech <note>Jupiter</note> who has reached the Fish <note>Pisces</note>, a man becomes a wise thinker. He is endowed with the wealth of honor, sons, and a wife, and attains great happiness while living within the lineage of kings. || 19 ||

In the period of Jupiter situated in the sign of Pisces, a person is thoughtful, possessed of wealth such as sons and a wife, and one who gains happiness by residing in a royal family. || 19 ||

### Chapter on the Results of the Venus Period

->First, the general results of the period of Bhrigu <note>Venus</note>:<-

The Minister of the Daityas <note>original: "Daityamatya," a title for Venus as the preceptor of the titans</note>, at the start of his own period, brings about the acquisition of women, ornaments, and garments. He grants various honors to men and high happiness arising from the awakening of the God of Love <note>original: "Kandarpa," referring to increased libido or romantic success</note>. || 1 ||

The person feels extreme joy in song and dance, finds pleasure in the practice of knowledge, and possesses a beautiful character. With superior intelligence, he is inclined toward the giving of food and is clever in buying or selling. || 2 ||

Happiness is surely derived from cattle, vehicles, and sons, as well as from the children of sons <note>grandchildren</note>. There is the recovery of previously earned wealth, but there may be strife in the family due to moving from one's place. || 3 ||

The body may indeed become weak due to phlegm and wind <note>term: Kapha and Vata, two of the three humors in Ayurvedic medicine</note>, and there is enmity with low-born people. The mind is distressed by worries regarding Brahmins and others, and there is occasional friendship with wicked people. || 4 ||

In the period of Venus, a man acquires women, ornaments, gems, and clothes; he is endowed with various honors, is lustful, happy, delighted by song and dance, pleased by the study of science, possesses a beautiful nature, is intelligent, a giver of food, clever in buying and selling, and gains happiness from cows, vehicles, and sons...

# Results of the Period of Venus in Aries

In the period of Venus situated in Aries <note>Mesha</note>, men experience a decrease in happiness regarding women, wealth, and comfort. They are constantly wandering, prone to vices, filled with anxiety, and possess a restless mind. || 6 ||

In the period of Venus located in the sign of Aries, a person suffers the loss of wife, wealth, and happiness; they are always traveling, addicted to bad habits, troubled by distress, and have an unstable temperament. || 6 ||

# Results of the Period of Venus in Taurus

In the period of Venus situated in Taurus <note>Vrisha</note>, there is an increase in happiness through agriculture and fine cattle. The intellect becomes exceptionally diverse in the sciences <note>Shastras</note>, and there is a disposition toward charity, the birth of daughters, and general contentment. || 7 ||

In the period of Venus located in the sign of Taurus, a person becomes happy through farming and livestock, possesses an intellect capable of understanding sacred scriptures, is charitable, begets daughters, and remains joyful. || 7 ||

# Results of the Period of Venus in Gemini

In the period of Venus traveling through Gemini <note>Mithuna</note>, a person becomes a connoisseur of poetry and the arts. They have a great interest in humor, wonder, and storytelling, and their mind is eager to travel to foreign lands. || 8 ||

In the period of Venus located in the sign of Gemini, a person is a knower of poetry and various arts, takes interest in comedy, marvelous tales, and legends, and desires to go to other countries. || 8 ||

# Chapter on the Results of the Period of Venus

### Results of the Period of Venus in the Sign of Cancer—

> When the period of Venus, situated in Cancer, arrives, a person becomes expert in their own work. Although they may be eager to live with another wife, they engage in various types of endeavors and remain grateful. || 9 ||

In the period of Venus <note>Sanskrit: Shukra</note> located in the sign of Cancer, a person is skilled in their duties, may take a second wife, performs many kinds of industries/labors, and is a grateful person.

### Results of the Period of Venus in the Sign of Leo—

> Upon the commencement of the period of the one worshiped by the leaders of the demons <note>original: "daityendra-vandyasya" - an epithet for Venus</note> situated in the sign of the Lion, one obtains wealth through a woman. Surely, the person lives on the wealth of others and later experiences little happiness from cattle and sons. || 10 ||

In the period of Venus located in the sign of Leo, a person attains a wife and wealth, subsists on the wealth of others, and receives only a small amount of happiness from livestock and children. || 10 ||

### Results of the Period of Venus in the Sign of Virgo—

> In the period of the one praised by the demons <note>Venus</note> situated in Virgo, there is a decrease in happiness. There is a scarcity of wealth, broken desires, a restless mind, and displacement from one's own home. || 11 ||

In the period of Venus located in the sign of Virgo <note>Venus is considered "debilitated" or at its weakest in Virgo</note>, a person finds little happiness, possesses little wealth, sees their heart's desires destroyed, is fickle-minded, and wanders away from their own place. || 11 ||

### Results of the Period of Venus in the Sign of Libra—

> At the start of the period of the one honored by the demons situated in the Scales, a person becomes an agriculturist. They possess distinguished honor, are rich in wealth and vehicles, and attain great happiness from their own kinsmen. || 12 ||

In the period of Venus located in the sign of Libra <note>Venus's own sign, where it is strong</note>, a person engages in farming, is highly respected, is endowed with wealth and means of transport, and receives happiness from their relatives.

### Results of the Period of Venus in the Sign of Scorpio—

> Upon the commencement of the period of Venus situated in the sign of the Scorpion, a person becomes a traveler. They are devoted to the work of others, powerful, burdened by debt, and fond of quarrels. || 13 ||

In the period of Venus located in the sign of Scorpio, a person lives abroad, performs the work of others, is influential/majestic, but is also associated with debt and a quarrelsome nature. || 13 ||

### The Results of the Period of Venus in Sagittarius—

In the period of the <term>Preceptor of the Asuras</term><note>original: "asurapujitasya" - a title for Venus, who in mythology is the teacher of the titans</note> when positioned in Sagittarius, a person attains great prestige from the sovereign.
